title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text: 廣西鄉試錄〔正德八年〕
punctuated: 廣西鄉試錄〔正德八年〕
translation_en: Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination〔Eighth year of the Zhengde reign (1513)〕

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
皇上嗣大歷服改元之八年是為
正德癸酉天下當大比以取
士也於是廣西巡按監察御
史朱志榮謀于總督兩廣右都
御史林廷選總鎮太監潘忠總
兵武定侯郭勛咸謂此
===
國家致治之事莫有大焉者鉅
細之務具載甲令盍豫飭所
司如令行之而鎮守太監陳
彬副總兵金堂相與賛襄益
力巡按御史以責任尤專也
遂博訪儒紳之有名行者移
檄禮聘司鑑衡之任比及期
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

皇上嗣大歷服，改元之八年，是為正德癸酉，天下當大比以取士也。於是，廣西巡按監察御史朱志榮謀于總督兩廣右都御史林廷選、總鎮太監潘忠、總兵武定侯郭勛，咸謂：「此國家致治之事，莫有大焉者。鉅細之務，具載甲令，盍豫飭所司如令行之？」而鎮守太監陳彬、副總兵金堂相與賛襄益力。巡按御史以責任尤專也，遂博訪儒紳之有名行者，移檄禮聘，司鑑衡之任。比及期，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

His Majesty succeeded to the great imperial charge [?]. The eighth year since he changed the reign title was the guiyou year of Zhengde [1513], when the triennial examinations were due to be held throughout the empire to select scholars for office. Accordingly, Zhu Zhirong, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor for Guangxi, consulted Lin Tingxuan, Supreme Commander of Guangdong and Guangxi and Right Censor-in-Chief; Pan Zhong, Grand Defender and eunuch; and Guo Xun, Regional Commander and Marquis of Wuding. All agreed: “Among the affairs through which the state achieves good government, none is greater than this. All its procedures, great and small, are fully set out in the statutes. Why not instruct the responsible offices in advance to carry them out according to those statutes?” Chen Bin, the garrison eunuch, and Jin Tang, Vice Regional Commander, joined in providing still more vigorous assistance.

Because the Regional Inspector bore especially direct responsibility, he made extensive inquiries for Confucian scholars of the gentry renowned for their conduct, sent official communications, and ceremonially invited them to undertake the work of evaluating the candidates. When the appointed time arrived, …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乃入院主監臨之事而以左
布政使夏暹右參政蔚春為
提調副使陳陽僉事孫徵為
監試其考試則奎偕教諭姜
瀛同考試則學正陳獻教諭
鄭悰杜子新方珩訓導鄭鵬也
至於右布政使周進隆左參政
===
李綱右參政陸徵左參議楊
瑋右參議左唐按察使方良永
副使翁茂南張弘宜僉事薛金都
指揮同知彭鐸又皆協心防
範於外蓋斯事重且大亦弗
敢以弗預而少有弗虔也既
鎖院迺合提督學校副使劉
punctuated: 乃入院主監臨之事，而以左布政使夏暹、右參政蔚春為提調，副使陳陽、僉事孫徵為監試。其考試則奎偕教諭姜瀛，同考試則學正陳獻、教諭鄭悰、杜子新、方珩、訓導鄭鵬也。至於右布政使周進隆、左參政李綱、右參政陸徵、左參議楊瑋、右參議左唐、按察使方良永、副使翁茂南、張弘宜、僉事薛金、都指揮同知彭鐸，又皆協心防範於外。蓋斯事重且大，亦弗敢以弗預而少有弗虔也。既鎖院，迺合提督學校副使劉
translation_en:
… then entered the examination compound to take charge as Supervising Official. Xia Xian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Wei Chun, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner, served as Proctors; Chen Yang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Sun Zheng, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, served as examination monitors. The Examiners were Kui and Jiang Ying, Instructor. The Associate Examiners were Chen Xian, Instructor; Zheng Cong, Du Zixin, and Fang Heng, Instructors; and Zheng Peng, Assistant Instructor.

Meanwhile, Zhou Jinlong, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Li Gang, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Lu Zheng, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Yang Wei, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zuo Tang, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Fang Liangyong, Surveillance Commissioner; Weng Maonan and Zhang Hongyi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Xue Jin, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; and Peng Duo, Vice Regional Military Commissioner, all worked together to maintain safeguards outside the compound. This undertaking was weighty and momentous: even those not directly involved dared not show the slightest lack of dedication.

Once the examination compound had been locked, [the candidates selected by] Liu, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner charged with supervising schools, were assembled …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
台所簡應試之士八百有竒
如式三試而校閱之得其文
之中式者殊多而僅取如額
數第其甲乙揭榜以示仍梓
為録并刻其文之優者進
呈於
上而傳諸四方録有序奎當承乏
===
乃言曰廣西古百粤地也居
荆楚西南距
京師殊僻遠其人物之見於史
牒者自漢以後漸盛入
國朝迄今尤彬彬輩出而名公
碩輔徳業聞望後先相繼與
中州等矣是豈無所自耶竊
punctuated:
台所簡應試之士八百有竒，如式三試而校閱之，得其文之中式者殊多，而僅取如額數，第其甲乙，揭榜以示，仍梓為録，并刻其文之優者，進呈於上，而傳諸四方。録有序，奎當承乏。
乃言曰：「廣西，古百粤地也，居荆楚西南，距京師殊僻遠。其人物之見於史牒者，自漢以後漸盛，入國朝迄今，尤彬彬輩出，而名公碩輔，徳業聞望，後先相繼，與中州等矣。是豈無所自耶？竊
translation_en:
…the more than eight hundred candidates selected by [Liu] Tai. They underwent three examination sessions according to the prescribed procedure, and their papers were assessed. Very many papers met the standard, but only the allotted number of candidates could be accepted. They were ranked in order of merit, and a list was posted to announce the results. A record was then printed from woodblocks, together with the best of their papers, to be respectfully presented to the emperor and circulated throughout the realm. The record required a preface, and I, Kui, was called upon to supply it for want of someone better qualified.
I therefore say: “Guangxi is the ancient land of the Baiyue. It lies southwest of Jingchu, exceptionally remote from the imperial capital. From the Han dynasty onward, increasing numbers of its people appeared in the historical records. Since the founding of our dynasty, accomplished men have emerged in particularly splendid succession. Eminent dignitaries and great ministers, distinguished by their virtue, achievements, renown, and prestige, have followed one another, equaling those of the Central Plain. Can this have come about without a cause? I humbly…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
嘗攷之我
祖宗開基銳意於敦崇教化敻與
前代不同彼漢興雖文武並
用然歷四世至孝武元朔而
後太學始興有宋固號稱崇
儒右文也亦至仁宗慶曆而
後有州郡之學惟我
===
聖祖即位之明年遂
詔天下立府州縣學以養育人
材又明年遂
詔天下設科以起懷材抱德之
士至十七年乃定今制以取
士其儲養簡拔振作人材之
意若汲汲焉惟恐後者
punctuated: 嘗攷之：我祖宗開基，銳意於敦崇教化，敻與前代不同。彼漢興，雖文武並用，然歷四世，至孝武元朔而後太學始興。有宋固號稱崇儒右文也，亦至仁宗慶曆而後有州郡之學。惟我聖祖即位之明年，遂詔天下立府州縣學，以養育人材；又明年，遂詔天下設科，以起懷材抱德之士。至十七年，乃定今制以取士。其儲養、簡拔、振作人材之意，若汲汲焉惟恐後者。
translation_en: …have examined this matter: when our imperial ancestors founded the dynasty, they devoted themselves resolutely to strengthening and honoring moral instruction, differing greatly from preceding dynasties. When the Han arose, it employed both civil and military means; nevertheless, four generations passed, and only in the Yuanshuo era of Emperor Xiaowu did the Imperial University begin to flourish. The Song was certainly renowned for honoring Confucian learning and giving precedence to literary culture, yet schools in prefectures and subordinate prefectures appeared only in the Qingli era of Emperor Renzong. Our sagely founder alone, in the year after his accession, promptly commanded the establishment of schools in prefectures, subprefectures, and counties throughout the realm to nurture men of talent. The following year, he commanded the establishment of examinations throughout the realm to bring into service scholars endowed with talent and virtue. In the seventeenth year, he established the present system for selecting scholars. His determination to cultivate a reserve of talented men, select the worthy, and inspire them was such that he seemed to press urgently forward, fearing only that he might fall behind.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承益隆繼述故論其養之
也有明經之師有廩餼之供
有給復之令而又有憲臣以
董正於上其取之也有刻錄
之傳有錫宴之榮有勸駕之
典而又有敘用之格以激厲
於其間蓋其所以崇尚而歆
===
艷之使之漸磨造就以自趨
於成德達材之域者無弗至
故百餘年來薄海內外人才
之生咸感發奮厲競自洗濯
以效用有古黎獻風廣西雖
僻遠其風化所及固不異也
則人才之盛宜哉然自昔而
punctuated: 列聖相承，益隆繼述。故論其養之也，有明經之師，有廩餼之供，有給復之令，而又有憲臣以董正於上。其取之也，有刻錄之傳，有錫宴之榮，有勸駕之典，而又有敘用之格以激厲於其間。蓋其所以崇尚而歆艷之，使之漸磨造就，以自趨於成德達材之域者，無弗至。故百餘年來，薄海內外，人才之生，咸感發奮厲，競自洗濯以效用，有古黎獻風。廣西雖僻遠，其風化所及，固不異也，則人才之盛宜哉！然自昔而
translation_en: Successive sage emperors have carried on this legacy, ever strengthening the work of their predecessors. Thus, in nurturing scholars, they have provided teachers versed in the Classics, supplies of grain stipends, and orders granting exemptions from taxes and corvée, with censorial officials overseeing and correcting matters from above. In selecting scholars, they have provided for the circulation of printed examination records, the honor of imperially bestowed banquets, and ceremonies sending successful candidates onward, together with rules governing appointment to office, to encourage and spur them on. Indeed, nothing has been left undone to esteem learning and inspire admiration for it, enabling scholars, through gradual cultivation and refinement, to advance of their own accord toward perfected virtue and fully developed talent. Hence, for more than a hundred years, talented men arising throughout the realm, even to its maritime bounds and beyond, have all been moved to exert themselves, vying to purify their conduct and render service, in the spirit of the worthy men of antiquity. Although Guangxi is remote, it shares equally in the reach of this moral transformation. How fitting, then, that talent should flourish there! Yet, from former times onward …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
觀其用於世者雖所遇不同
要皆馳聲樹績有可述而志
者或不然則其所養有未至
故見惑於他岐守變於初志
中道而不能自立耳夫鈞是
人也鈞是化也而人品頓殊
如此亦獨何哉余為是懼用
===
以此告諸士之既見錄者以
究其終并勵未見錄者之志
俾益厚自養以待時而與前
哲匹休此固同有事塲屋者
之意而非余之私也
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣
儒學教諭張奎謹序
punctuated:
觀其用於世者，雖所遇不同，要皆馳聲樹績，有可述而志者。或不然，則其所養有未至，故見惑於他岐，守變於初志，中道而不能自立耳。夫鈞是人也，鈞是化也，而人品頓殊如此，亦獨何哉？余為是懼，用以此告諸士之既見錄者，以究其終，并勵未見錄者之志，俾益厚自養，以待時而與前哲匹休。此固同有事塲屋者之意，而非余之私也。
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學教諭張奎謹序。
translation_en:
…consider those who have served in the world: although their circumstances differed, in the main they all won renown and established achievements worthy of recounting and recording. If some did otherwise, it was because their self-cultivation had not reached its full extent. Thus they were led astray onto other paths, departed in their commitments from their original aspirations, and midway proved unable to stand firm on their own. They are equally human and have equally received this transforming influence; why, then, should their character differ so markedly? Troubled by this, I offer these words to the scholars who have been selected, so that they may carry their endeavors through to the end, while also encouraging the aspirations of those not yet selected. May they deepen their self-cultivation, await their time, and rival the worthies of the past in excellence. This is indeed the intention of all who share responsibility for the examination, and not merely my private wish.
Preface respectfully composed by Zhang Kui, Instructor of the Confucian School of Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
正德八年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史朱志榮〔仁叔湖廣夷陵州人戊辰進士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使夏暹〔景升雲南左衛人甲辰進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政蔚春〔景元直隸合肥縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司副使陳陽〔健夫江西新淦縣人癸丑進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事孫徽〔德夫湖廣襄陽護衛人癸丑進士〕
===
考試官
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學教諭張奎〔應明江西餘干縣人丁卯貢士〕
湖廣衡州府耒陽縣儒學教諭姜瀛〔子登四川墊江縣人甲子貢士〕
同考試官
湖廣襄陽府均州儒學學正陳獻〔汝賢廣東番禺縣人乙卯貢士〕
江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學教諭鄭悰〔一貞福建莆田縣人丁卯貢士〕
直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學教諭杜子新〔明甫福建福寧州人戊午貢士〕
浙江衢州府常山縣儒學教諭方珩〔純禮福建莆田縣人辛酉貢士〕
直隸蘇州府長洲縣儒學訓導鄭鵬〔于漢福建侯官縣人辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
正德八年廣西鄉試

監臨官：
巡按廣西監察御史朱志榮〔仁叔，湖廣夷陵州人，戊辰進士〕。

提調官：
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使夏暹〔景升，雲南左衛人，甲辰進士〕。
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政蔚春〔景元，直隸合肥縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官：
廣西等處提刑按察司副使陳陽〔健夫，江西新淦縣人，癸丑進士〕。
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事孫徽〔德夫，湖廣襄陽護衛人，癸丑進士〕。

考試官：
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學教諭張奎〔應明，江西餘干縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
湖廣衡州府耒陽縣儒學教諭姜瀛〔子登，四川墊江縣人，甲子貢士〕。

同考試官：
湖廣襄陽府均州儒學學正陳獻〔汝賢，廣東番禺縣人，乙卯貢士〕。
江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學教諭鄭悰〔一貞，福建莆田縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學教諭杜子新〔明甫，福建福寧州人，戊午貢士〕。
浙江衢州府常山縣儒學教諭方珩〔純禮，福建莆田縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府長洲縣儒學訓導鄭鵬〔于漢，福建侯官縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangxi Provincial Examination, Eighth Year of Zhengde (1513)

Supervising Official:
Zhu Zhirong, Regional Inspector of Guangxi and Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Renshu and was from Yiling Subprefecture, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuchen year.

Proctors:
Xia Xian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi, had the courtesy name Jingsheng and was from the Yunnan Left Guard. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.
Yu Chun, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangxi, had the courtesy name Jingyuan and was from Hefei County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:
Chen Yang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Guangxi, had the courtesy name Jianfu and was from Xingan County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.
Sun Hui, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner of Guangxi, had the courtesy name Defu and was from the Xiangyang Princely Escort Guard, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Examiners:
Zhang Kui, Instructor at the Confucian School of Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Yingming and was from Yugan County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the dingmao year.
Jiang Ying, Instructor at the Confucian School of Leiyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Zideng and was from Dianjiang County, Sichuan. He was a tribute scholar of the jiazi year.

Associate Examiners:
Chen Xian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Junzhou Subprefecture, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Ruxian and was from Panyu County, Guangdong. He was a tribute scholar of the yimao year.
Zheng Cong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Yizhen and was from Putian County, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar of the dingmao year.
Du Zixin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Mingfu and was from Funing Subprefecture, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.
Fang Heng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Changshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Chunli and was from Putian County, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.
Zheng Peng, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Yuhan and was from Houguan County, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
印卷官
廣西等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事呂韶清〔叔和廣東順德縣人吏員〕
廣西等處提刑按察司經歷司知事衡式〔廷範湖廣興國州人監生〕
收掌試卷官
桂林府知府黃鑅〔子宣福建晉江縣人癸丑進士〕
梧州府知府曹琚〔仲玉湖廣桂陽縣人丙辰進士〕
受卷官
平樂府知府李守經〔秉彞河南洛陽縣人丁酉貢士〕
南寧府同知熊吉〔伯脩江西臨川縣人丙辰進士〕
===
彌封官
柳州府賓州知州孫佐〔朝相江西清江縣人戊辰進士〕
梧州府鬱林州知州何律〔用正廣東番禺縣人巳酉貢士〕
謄錄官
慶遠府同知李學〔行之四川江津縣人甲午貢士〕
桂林府義寧縣知縣潘志高〔希道貴州普定衛籍直隸武進縣人辛酉貢士〕

…one tour of inspection; the assembled lords attend court four times. They report fully in words, are clearly tested through their accomplishments, and receive carriages and robes according to their service.
When virtue is renewed daily, the myriad states cherish it.
From morning until the sun had passed its zenith, he had no leisure to eat.
Then he can abide in it, follow it, and ponder it.

Book of Odes
How the kudzu spreads, extending into the valley, its leaves luxuriant! We cut it and boil it, making fine cloth and coarse cloth; we wear it without tiring of it.
I have fine guests: we play the zithers and blow the mouth organs. Blowing the mouth organs and sounding their reeds, we present baskets of gifts.
King Wen received the Mandate and achieved these martial deeds. Having attacked Chong, he built his city at Feng. How great was King Wen!
He moved to strike them with awe, and none failed to tremble and submit. He conciliated the hundred spirits, including those of the Yellow River and the lofty mountains.

In ordering the court, governing the army, serving in office, and enforcing laws, authority and dignity cannot prevail without ritual propriety.
Thus, the state has its rites, offices have their rules of governance, affairs have their assigned duties, and rites have their proper sequence.
Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great rites share their orderly measures.
For those above, it can be observed and understood; for those below, it can be recounted and remembered.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
修理橋梁道路
第叄塲
策五道
問書謂監于先王成憲其永無愆詩謂不
愆不忘率由舊章蓋言祖宗之當法也
伏覩我
太宗文皇帝甞諭羣臣曰茲予繼承天位恪遵
成憲
仁宗昭皇帝亦甞諭侍臣曰守成之主動法
===
祖宗斯鮮過舉大哉
王言誠萬世人君之龜鑑也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸奄有萬邦垂憲立法盡
善盡美固有非臣下所能周知亦有非
言語所能形容者姑舉
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書所載君道之大者如聖
孝也聖學也敬天也仁民也求言也聽
納也用賢也勤政也謹戒也節儉也而
皇祖之懿德美行過古帝王遠甚然於前數者
punctuated:
修理橋梁道路。

第叄塲
策五道

問：書謂「監于先王成憲，其永無愆」，詩謂「不愆不忘，率由舊章」，蓋言祖宗之當法也。伏覩我太宗文皇帝甞諭羣臣曰：「茲予繼承天位，恪遵成憲。」仁宗昭皇帝亦甞諭侍臣曰：「守成之主，動法祖宗，斯鮮過舉。」大哉王言！誠萬世人君之龜鑑也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，奄有萬邦，垂憲立法，盡善盡美，固有非臣下所能周知，亦有非言語所能形容者。姑舉宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》所載君道之大者，如聖孝也、聖學也、敬天也、仁民也、求言也、聽納也、用賢也、勤政也、謹戒也、節儉也，而皇祖之懿德美行，過古帝王遠甚。然於前數者
translation_en:
Repairing bridges and roads.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Book of Documents says, “Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without error.” The Book of Odes says, “Neither transgressing nor forgetting, follow the old statutes.” These passages mean that the ancestral rulers should be taken as models. We reverently observe that our Emperor Wen, Taizong, once instructed his assembled ministers: “Now that I have succeeded to the throne of Heaven, I scrupulously adhere to the established statutes.” Emperor Zhao, Renzong, likewise once instructed his attendant ministers: “If a ruler preserving an inherited achievement models his actions on his ancestors, he will seldom act amiss.” How great are these royal words! Truly, they are a guide and mirror for rulers of all ages.

We reflect with profound reverence upon our Emperor Gao, Taizu, who rose like a dragon from the Huai region and came to possess the myriad states. He bequeathed statutes and established laws, perfect in every respect. There are certainly aspects of these that his servants cannot fully comprehend, and others that words cannot describe. Let us simply take the principal elements of the ruler’s Way recorded in the imperially composed Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) of Emperor Zhang, Xuanzong: sagely filial piety, sagely learning, reverence for Heaven, benevolence toward the people, soliciting counsel, listening to and accepting advice, employing the worthy, diligence in government, vigilance, and frugality. The admirable virtue and excellent conduct of our imperial ancestor far surpassed those of the emperors and kings of antiquity. Yet, regarding the several matters just mentioned …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可歷指其實歟抑
今日法
祖之所當先者何在歟諸士子莊誦
聖訓有年請敬陳之毋曰日用由之而不知也
問文章所以傳世政事所以澤物君子所
當尚也三代以上文章政事之兼具者
固毋容議矣姑舉三代以下文章政事
言之夫以四百年之漢文章莫若董仲
舒何以政事不聞於當時三百年之唐
===
文章莫若韓退之何以政事不著于後
世宋之周程張朱皆有文章之名世者
也何以政事僅小試而不大著歟之數
君子者果但有文章而無政事歟抑別
有其故歟論者類謂有文章而無政事
則為腐儒有政事而無文章則為俗吏
然自漢唐宋以來不有文章而措之政
事大有足紀者果可目為俗吏歟不有
政事而發為文章亦有可稱者果可目
punctuated:
可歷指其實歟？抑今日法祖之所當先者何在歟？諸士子莊誦聖訓有年，請敬陳之，毋曰日用由之而不知也。

問：文章所以傳世，政事所以澤物，君子所當尚也。三代以上，文章政事之兼具者，固毋容議矣。姑舉三代以下文章政事言之。夫以四百年之漢，文章莫若董仲舒，何以政事不聞於當時？三百年之唐，文章莫若韓退之，何以政事不著于後世？宋之周程張朱，皆有文章之名世者也，何以政事僅小試而不大著歟？之數君子者，果但有文章而無政事歟？抑別有其故歟？論者類謂有文章而無政事，則為腐儒；有政事而無文章，則為俗吏。然自漢唐宋以來，不有文章而措之政事，大有足紀者，果可目為俗吏歟？不有政事而發為文章，亦有可稱者，果可目
translation_en:
…Can concrete instances of these be pointed out one by one? And what should take precedence today in emulating the imperial ancestors? You candidates have solemnly recited the imperial instructions for years. Please respectfully set forth your answers; do not say that you follow them in daily practice without understanding them.

Question: Literary writing is a means of transmitting one's legacy to posterity; governance is a means of bringing benefit to others. Both are things a gentleman should esteem. Those who combined literary accomplishment and governance in the Three Dynasties and earlier surely need no discussion. Let us consider literature and governance after the Three Dynasties. In the four hundred years of the Han, none surpassed Dong Zhongshu in literary writing. Why, then, were his achievements in governance unheard of in his own time? In the three hundred years of the Tang, none surpassed Han Tuizhi. Why, then, were his achievements in governance not renowned in later ages? Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu of the Song all won renown in their age through their writings. Why were their abilities in governance tried only on a small scale, without conspicuous achievement? Did these gentlemen [?] truly possess only literary accomplishment and no ability in governance? Or was there some other reason? Commentators commonly say that someone with literary accomplishment but no ability in governance is a pedantic scholar, while someone with ability in governance but no literary accomplishment is a vulgar functionary. Yet, since the Han, Tang, and Song, there have been those without literary accomplishment whose practical achievements in governance were amply worthy of record. Can they really be called vulgar functionaries? There have also been those without achievements in governance whose literary writings were worthy of praise. Can they really be called…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
為腐儒歟抑果全才之難得歟今之所
取法又果安在歟諸士子力學有年發
為文章行將施諸政事願悉陳之毋隱
問字學之關於天下也大矣所以傳經載
道述史記事治百官察萬民而貫通三
才者也始於伏羲之畫卦成於蒼頡之
造書而其所以畫者何因造者何據擊
壤康衢之播其聲二典三謨之傳於世
上而堯舜禹湯文武之為君所以出令
===
者下而臯陶伊傅周召之為臣所以行
君之令而致之民者曾外於此道歟柰
之何燔燒之禍既熾科斗之文不傳有
變大篆而為小篆者有厭篆書而為隷
書者有縮之以簡便華之以姿媚者有
為楷書為行書為草書為飛白者其創
始也各有其人其是非也皆有定在可
詳辯歟夫字者心之畫也人之賢否見
焉治之隆替寓焉古之人執筆而得五
punctuated:
為腐儒歟？抑果全才之難得歟？今之所取法又果安在歟？諸士子力學有年，發為文章，行將施諸政事，願悉陳之，毋隱。

問：字學之關於天下也大矣，所以傳經載道、述史記事、治百官察萬民，而貫通三才者也。始於伏羲之畫卦，成於蒼頡之造書，而其所以畫者何因，造者何據？擊壤、康衢之播其聲，二典、三謨之傳於世，上而堯舜禹湯文武之為君，所以出令者，下而臯陶伊傅周召之為臣，所以行君之令而致之民者，曾外於此道歟？柰之何燔燒之禍既熾，科斗之文不傳？有變大篆而為小篆者，有厭篆書而為隷書者，有縮之以簡便、華之以姿媚者，有為楷書、為行書、為草書、為飛白者。其創始也，各有其人；其是非也，皆有定在，可詳辯歟？夫字者，心之畫也，人之賢否見焉，治之隆替寓焉。古之人執筆而得五
translation_en:
…be deemed pedantic scholars? Or is comprehensive talent indeed difficult to find? Where, then, should we now seek our models? You candidates have studied diligently for years and expressed your learning in literary compositions; you will soon apply it to government affairs. Please set forth your views fully, concealing nothing.

Question: The study of written characters has great significance for all under Heaven. Through writing, the classics are transmitted and the Way conveyed, histories composed and events recorded, the hundred officials governed and the myriad people scrutinized; it connects the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. It began with Fuxi’s drawing of the trigrams and reached completion with Cangjie’s creation of writing. What prompted the drawing, and on what was the creation based? The songs “Striking the Ground” and “The Broad Thoroughfare” spread their sounds, and the “Two Canons” and “Three Counsels” were transmitted to posterity. Above, rulers such as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu issued commands; below, ministers such as Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao implemented their rulers’ commands and conveyed them to the people. Did any of this ever lie outside the way of writing? How was it, then, that once the calamity of book burning raged, tadpole script ceased to be transmitted? Some transformed large-seal script into small-seal script; some tired of seal script and made clerical script; some abbreviated writing for simplicity and convenience, or embellished it for graceful charm; and some devised standard script, running script, cursive script, and “flying-white” script. Each innovation had its originator, and each has its established merits and faults. Can you discuss these distinctions in detail? Written characters are the delineation of the mind: a person’s worthiness or unworthiness is revealed in them, and the flourishing or decline of government is embodied in them. People of antiquity took up the brush and attained the five…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德宗而後見焉夫漢文唐宗宜其不足
而乃有餘武帝德宗宜其有餘而乃不
足其故何耶
國家財賦之制一倣于古量入為出固未嘗
乏也夫何比年以來司農之藏少府之
用或至告匱將欲務為寬恤乎則軍國
之需無以給將欲肆加征榷乎則意外
之虞亦當慮古人有謂豐財之道當去
其害財者而有三冗之說其果然歟其
===
於
今日之理財亦有所裨否歟昔趙充國計河
湟得三百斛可以制羌人不敢動諸葛
亮用兵如神而以糧道不繼屢出無功
方
今四方已寧實
皇上盛德固無事乎用師也然有備無患又
國家所當預講而博籌者爾諸生懷竒有素
願言漢唐所以有餘不足之故而及
punctuated:
德宗而後見焉。夫漢文、唐宗宜其不足，而乃有餘；武帝、德宗宜其有餘，而乃不足，其故何耶？
國家財賦之制，一倣于古，量入為出，固未嘗乏也。夫何比年以來，司農之藏、少府之用，或至告匱？將欲務為寬恤乎，則軍國之需無以給；將欲肆加征榷乎，則意外之虞亦當慮。古人有謂豐財之道，當去其害財者，而有三冗之說，其果然歟？其於今日之理財，亦有所裨否歟？昔趙充國計河湟，得三百斛，可以制羌人不敢動；諸葛亮用兵如神，而以糧道不繼，屢出無功。方今四方已寧，實皇上盛德，固無事乎用師也。然有備無患，又國家所當預講而博籌者。爾諸生懷竒有素，願言漢唐所以有餘不足之故，而及
translation_en:
…only under Dezong did this become apparent. Under Emperor Wen of Han and Emperor Taizong of Tang, one would have expected insufficiency, yet there was a surplus; under Emperor Wu and Emperor Dezong, one would have expected a surplus, yet there was insufficiency. What was the reason?
The state's system of taxation and revenue follows ancient practice throughout, adjusting expenditure to income, and has certainly never lacked resources. Why, then, in recent years have the reserves of the Minister of Agriculture and the funds for the expenditure of the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues sometimes reportedly run dry? If we seek to concentrate on leniency and relief, there will be no means to meet military and state requirements; if we seek freely to increase taxes and monopoly levies, we must also consider the danger of unforeseen troubles. The ancients said that the way to enrich the treasury was to eliminate what depleted it, and spoke of the “three redundancies.” Is this indeed so? Might this also benefit the management of finances today? Formerly, Zhao Chongguo, making plans for the He-Huang region, obtained three hundred hu of grain and could thereby keep the Qiang from daring to act. Zhuge Liang commanded troops with supernatural skill, yet because his grain supply routes could not be maintained, his repeated expeditions achieved nothing. Now that all quarters are at peace, truly through His Majesty's abundant virtue, there is certainly no occasion to employ armies. Nevertheless, preparedness averts calamity: this, too, is something the state should discuss beforehand and plan comprehensively. You students have long possessed exceptional talents. Explain, I ask you, the reasons for the surpluses and shortages under the Han and Tang, and go on to discuss…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今日理財之宜用以聞於司國計者當亦有
所酌處於其間矣
問兵凶戰危固非學者之所常言至於禦
暴禁亂之策亦學者之所當究心者姑
與論其一二兵所以衛國必屬之於將
將所以統兵必務於得人是強兵要在
乎擇將也審矣先正云賢材居上士卒
處下人安其業是以無敵我
孝宗敬皇帝臨御之日開科以求將材儀式首
===
制迨今
皇上嗣大歷服用廷臣議定儀式每每欲萃天
下之優於將材者于
京師為統兵衛國計誠萬世不刋之
盛典也夫將之論不一而兵之論亦不一故
將有八材而何又有八弊歟將德有五
而何又有八惡歟將善有五而何又有
四欲歟兵強有四而何又有五戒歟武
德有七而何又有七禁歟兵勢有三而
punctuated:
今日理財之宜，用以聞於司國計者，當亦有所酌處於其間矣。
問：兵凶戰危，固非學者之所常言；至於禦暴禁亂之策，亦學者之所當究心者。姑與論其一二。兵所以衛國，必屬之於將；將所以統兵，必務於得人。是強兵要在乎擇將也，審矣。先正云：「賢材居上，士卒處下，人安其業，是以無敵。」我孝宗敬皇帝臨御之日，開科以求將材，儀式首制。迨今皇上嗣大歷服，用廷臣議定儀式，每每欲萃天下之優於將材者于京師，為統兵衛國計，誠萬世不刋之盛典也。夫將之論不一，而兵之論亦不一。故將有八材，而何又有八弊歟？將德有五，而何又有八惡歟？將善有五，而何又有四欲歟？兵強有四，而何又有五戒歟？武德有七，而何又有七禁歟？兵勢有三，而
translation_en:
…the appropriate measures for managing finances today, so that these may be conveyed to those responsible for the state's finances, who should find matters therein to weigh and act upon.
Question: Arms are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is perilous; these are certainly not subjects that scholars ordinarily discuss. Yet strategies for resisting violence and suppressing disorder are also matters to which scholars ought to devote careful thought. Let us discuss one or two aspects. Troops serve to defend the state and must be entrusted to commanders; commanders serve to lead troops, and every effort must be made to obtain suitable men. It is thus clear that the key to strengthening an army lies in selecting its commanders. A worthy predecessor said: “Worthy and talented men occupy the higher positions, and officers and soldiers the lower; each is secure in his occupation, and thus they are invincible.” During the reign of our Emperor Xiaozong Jing, examinations were instituted to seek men with the talents of commanders, and their procedures were first established. Now that His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial mandate, he has adopted procedures deliberated upon and settled by his court officials, ever seeking to assemble in the capital the empire's most gifted potential commanders, with a view to leading troops and defending the state. This is truly a splendid institution to stand unaltered for ten thousand generations. Now, accounts of commanders are not uniform, nor are accounts of armies. Thus, commanders have eight talents: why, then, are there also eight defects? Commanders have five virtues: why, then, are there also eight evils? Commanders have five strengths: why, then, are there also four desires? There are four ways in which an army is strong: why, then, are there also five cautions? There are seven martial virtues: why, then, are there also seven prohibitions? There are three configurations of military advantage, and…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
何又有三機歟顧廣西百粤用武之地
猺獞出没之鄉先世有自奮威武而擊
曹成之寇者有忠義勇敢而戢儂賊之
兵者有歐陽脩薦其智略可任將軍者
有狄青薦其驍勇而破儂賊者有稱其
為文武兼全者有稱其為一代名將者
可歷指其人歟畧將材將德將善之足
錄歟果兵强武德兵勢之足法歟諸士
子佩服
===
聖訓景仰前哲於將兵必知之詳於名賢必考
之精側陋之中豈無非熊伏龍而深知
擇將用兵之略者乎我懷若人適其有
遇用將轉而薦之于
上庶竭區區以人事君之忠
punctuated: 何又有三機歟？顧廣西百粤，用武之地，猺獞出没之鄉。先世有自奮威武而擊曹成之寇者，有忠義勇敢而戢儂賊之兵者，有歐陽脩薦其智略可任將軍者，有狄青薦其驍勇而破儂賊者，有稱其為文武兼全者，有稱其為一代名將者，可歷指其人歟？畧將材、將德、將善之足錄歟？果兵强、武德、兵勢之足法歟？諸士子佩服聖訓，景仰前哲，於將兵必知之詳，於名賢必考之精。側陋之中，豈無非熊、伏龍而深知擇將用兵之略者乎？我懷若人，適其有遇，用將轉而薦之于上，庶竭區區以人事君之忠。
translation_en:
…why, then, are there also three critical opportunities? Consider Guangxi, the land of the Hundred Yue: a region for military action, where the Yao and Zhuang come and go. In former times, there was one who roused himself to martial prowess and attacked Cao Cheng’s bandits; one who, loyal, righteous, and courageous, quelled the forces of the Nong rebels; one whom Ouyang Xiu recommended as possessing the intelligence and strategic ability to serve as a general; and one whom Di Qing recommended for his valor and who defeated the Nong rebels. There was one praised as accomplished in both civil and military affairs, and one acclaimed as a renowned general of his age. Can you identify these men one by one? Can you outline [?] what is worth recording about their abilities, virtues, and strengths as commanders? Do their military strength, martial virtues, and strategic dispositions indeed offer models to follow?

You candidates hold the sagely teachings close to your hearts and look up to the worthy men of the past. Surely your knowledge of commanding troops is detailed, and your study of celebrated worthies exact. Among those living in humble obscurity, might there not be an “extraordinary bear” or a “crouching dragon”—an undiscovered talent like Jiang Ziya or Zhuge Liang—who deeply understands the arts of selecting generals and employing troops? I long for such a man. Should I happen to encounter him, I shall recommend him to His Majesty, hoping thereby to give the fullest expression to my humble loyalty in serving my sovereign by presenting worthy men.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
動靜二字不出令人厭觀此篇融會傳註成文
且挑剔明白而知仁體段宛然在目必甞苦心
於本領者
考試官教諭姜批動靜字發揮痛快且
用字用句無一竒怪險僻讀之令人躍然錄
之以式
考試官教諭張批題似平易而措辭實
難此作不為題窘其必富於學者
聖人論人之造理異而具體自異焉盖理之在
===
人本同而人之所造則異也則夫體段之具又
得無一動一靜之異哉聖人各著以示人宜矣
且夫欲知知仁之喜好不同當知知仁之體段
本異是故知周明通而是非昭然其不昧知者
也知者之體主於動動豈蕩無所見而徇物哉
想其一事具一理也此心有以達其幾微萬事
具萬理也此心有以達其妙用接於日用者有
常有變而應之在我者無適無莫隨宜制事不
拘於一隅也散之天下者有順有逆而處之在
punctuated:
動靜二字不出令人厭。觀此篇，融會傳註成文，且挑剔明白，而知仁體段宛然在目，必甞苦心於本領者。
考試官教諭姜批：動靜字發揮痛快，且用字用句無一竒怪險僻，讀之令人躍然，錄之以式。
考試官教諭張批：題似平易，而措辭實難。此作不為題窘，其必富於學者。
聖人論人之造理異，而具體自異焉。盖理之在人本同，而人之所造則異也。則夫體段之具，又得無一動一靜之異哉？聖人各著以示人，宜矣。
且夫欲知知仁之喜好不同，當知知仁之體段本異。是故知周明通，而是非昭然，其不昧，知者也。知者之體主於動，動豈蕩無所見而徇物哉？想其一事具一理也，此心有以達其幾微；萬事具萬理也，此心有以達其妙用。接於日用者有常有變，而應之在我者無適無莫，隨宜制事，不拘於一隅也；散之天下者有順有逆，而處之在
translation_en:
The two words “activity” and “stillness” do not appear so as to weary the reader [?]. This essay integrates the commentarial explanations into its composition and distinguishes the issues clearly, so that the characteristic dispositions of the wise and the benevolent stand vividly before our eyes. Its author must have labored painstakingly over the foundations of learning.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The words “activity” and “stillness” are expounded with satisfying vigor. Moreover, not a single word or phrase is strange, strained, or obscure. Reading it lifts the spirits. It is recorded here as a model.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The topic seems straightforward, but expressing it is actually difficult. This composition is not hampered by the topic; its author must possess abundant learning.
The Sage discusses how people differ in their attainment of principle, and thus naturally differ in the dispositions they embody. Principle is fundamentally the same in all people, but their attainments differ. How, then, could their embodied dispositions fail to differ, the one active and the other still? It is fitting that the Sage sets forth each to instruct others.
Now, to understand why the wise and the benevolent differ in what they delight in, one must understand that their characteristic dispositions are fundamentally different. Thus, one whose knowledge is comprehensive and whose understanding is clear and penetrating, to whom right and wrong are manifest and unobscured, is wise. The disposition of the wise centers on activity. But could activity mean aimless wandering without discernment and submission to external things? Consider how each affair embodies a principle: this mind can comprehend its subtle workings. The myriad affairs embody myriad principles: this mind can comprehend their marvelous operation. What we encounter in daily life includes both the constant and the changing, while our responses involve neither an inflexible insistence nor an inflexible refusal. We manage affairs as circumstances require, without being confined to a single standpoint. What is spread throughout the world includes both favorable and adverse circumstances, while our handling of them lies in …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
我者無將無迎因時順理□泥於一端也左之
左之旁取逢原之有資右之右之泛應曲當之
無礙動非此之謂乎欲淨理還而心德渾然其
克全仁者也仁者之體主於靜靜豈寂無所感
而絕物哉想其處物為義也彼則安于此而依
之深在物為理也彼則安于此而守之固物之
常變叢於前而吾心之敦厚一義自持無歆羨
也境之順逆變於前而吾心之凝重一理自定
無畔援也肫肫乎自暫至久不因物而有遷坦
===
坦乎由少而老不知誘而物化靜非此之謂乎
是則知者未嘗不靜而其體則主於動仁者未
嘗不動而其體則主於靜此所以其樂有山水
而其效有樂壽也歟抑嘗因是言而求其人若
賜之達而優於從政即知者之動若顏之愚而
三月不違即仁者之靜至吾夫子則合斯二者
而兼全之觀其設教杏壇因材變化何如其知
動厄於陳蔡絃歌自如何如其仁靜要之夫子
一身太極之全體也先儒謂其非體仁知之深
punctuated: 我者無將無迎，因時順理，□泥於一端也。左之左之，旁取逢原之有資；右之右之，泛應曲當之無礙。動非此之謂乎？欲淨理還，而心德渾然，其克全仁者也。仁者之體主於靜，靜豈寂無所感而絕物哉？想其處物為義也，彼則安于此而依之深；在物為理也，彼則安于此而守之固。物之常變叢於前，而吾心之敦厚，一義自持，無歆羨也；境之順逆變於前，而吾心之凝重，一理自定，無畔援也。肫肫乎，自暫至久，不因物而有遷；坦坦乎，由少而老，不知誘而物化。靜非此之謂乎？是則知者未嘗不靜，而其體則主於動；仁者未嘗不動，而其體則主於靜。此所以其樂有山水，而其效有樂壽也歟？抑嘗因是言而求其人，若賜之達而優於從政，即知者之動；若顏之愚而三月不違，即仁者之靜。至吾夫子，則合斯二者而兼全之。觀其設教杏壇，因材變化，何如其知動；厄於陳蔡，絃歌自如，何如其仁靜。要之，夫子一身，太極之全體也。先儒謂其「非體仁知之深
translation_en:
…in my dealings with them, I neither pursue what has gone nor anticipate what is to come, but follow the times and accord with principle, [not?] clinging to a single approach. Turn to the left, turn to the left: there are resources to draw upon from every side, encountering the source wherever one turns. Turn to the right, turn to the right: nothing obstructs responding broadly and fittingly to every particular circumstance. Is this not what is meant by activity?

When desires are purified and principle restored, and the virtue of the mind is an undivided whole, one can fully realize humaneness: such is the humane person. The essential character of the humane person centers on stillness. Yet does stillness mean being inert, insensible to anything, and cut off from things? Consider righteousness as it governs the handling of affairs: the humane person rests securely in it and relies upon it profoundly. Consider principle as it inheres in things: the humane person rests securely in it and holds to it firmly. Constant and changing affairs crowd before him, yet his mind remains sincere and generous; holding himself to righteousness alone, he feels no envious longing. Favorable and adverse circumstances alternate before him, yet his mind remains composed and steady; settled in principle alone, he neither strays nor grasps after anything. Utterly sincere, from a brief interval to a long duration, he does not shift with external things. Entirely at ease, from youth to old age, he knows no enticement that would let external things transform him. Is this not what is meant by stillness?

Thus the wise are never without stillness, but their essential character centers on activity; the humane are never without activity, but their essential character centers on stillness. Is this why their delights are in mountains and waters, and the resulting benefits are joy and longevity? I have also sought, through these words, the people who exemplify them. Ci’s discernment, which made him amply qualified to participate in government, exemplifies the activity of the wise. Yan’s apparent foolishness, together with his not departing from humaneness for three months, exemplifies the stillness of the humane. Our Master, however, united these two and possessed both in their fullness. Consider how he taught at the Apricot Altar, transforming his pupils according to their capacities: how active his wisdom was! When beset by hardship in Chen and Cai, he continued playing the strings and singing with his usual ease: how still his humaneness was! In essence, the Master embodied in his own person the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate. An earlier Confucian scholar said of this: “Without profoundly embodying humaneness and wisdom…”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不能如此形容旨哉言乎
聖人治天下使有菽粟如水火菽粟如水
火而民焉有不仁者乎
鄭琬
考試官敎諭姜批題本不難作者多認
理不定詞率泛冗令人厭觀獨此篇明白切當
而且氣格舂容擺脫塵俗信非穉筆可到執
此可以知子之為政矣
考試官敎諭張批塲中作孟子義佳者
===
絕少此篇信筆胸中寫出聖人治天下化民
成俗之由深得立言本意且才思英發詞
語精健必八桂瓌奇養之有素者也可嘉
可嘉
聖人治世惟有以足民食自有以興民行甚矣
民食治化之所關也聖人有道以足之則民行
之興亦自有不容已者乎想昔孟子之意謂夫
不患世未治而患民心之未仁不患民未仁而
患政制之未善是故聖人者出以一身而撫輿圖
punctuated:
不能如此形容。旨哉，言乎！
「聖人治天下，使有菽粟如水火。菽粟如水火，而民焉有不仁者乎？」
鄭琬
考試官敎諭姜批：題本不難，作者多認理不定，詞率泛冗，令人厭觀。獨此篇明白切當，而且氣格舂容，擺脫塵俗，信非穉筆可到。執此，可以知子之為政矣。
考試官敎諭張批：塲中作孟子義佳者絕少。此篇信筆胸中寫出聖人治天下、化民成俗之由，深得立言本意。且才思英發，詞語精健，必八桂瓌奇、養之有素者也。可嘉，可嘉！
聖人治世，惟有以足民食，自有以興民行。甚矣，民食治化之所關也！聖人有道以足之，則民行之興亦自有不容已者乎！想昔孟子之意，謂夫不患世未治，而患民心之未仁；不患民未仁，而患政制之未善。是故聖人者出，以一身而撫輿圖
translation_en:
…could not have described it in this way. How profound these words are!
“When a sage governs all under Heaven, he ensures that beans and grain are as plentiful as water and fire. When beans and grain are as plentiful as water and fire, how could any of the people fail to be benevolent?”
Zheng Wan
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The topic itself is not difficult, but most writers grasp its principle uncertainly, and their language is generally vague and prolix, making it tiresome to read. This essay alone is clear and apt; moreover, its spirit and style are ample and unhurried, free of commonplace vulgarity. Such an achievement is certainly beyond an immature writer. From this, one can discern how you would conduct government.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Among the essays on the meaning of the Mengzi produced in this examination, good ones are exceedingly rare. In this essay, the writer freely sets down what is in his heart, explaining how a sage governs all under Heaven, transforms the people, and establishes their customs. He profoundly grasps the original intent of the statement. Moreover, his inventive thought is brilliant, and his language refined and vigorous. Surely he is an extraordinary talent of Bagui [Guangxi], long nurtured through cultivation. Admirable, admirable!
When a sage governs the world, he need only possess the means to provide sufficient food for the people, and he will naturally possess the means to elevate their conduct. How deeply the people’s food supply bears upon government and moral transformation! If the sage has a way to make it sufficient, must not the improvement of the people’s conduct follow of itself, irresistibly? I imagine that Mencius’s meaning in former times was this: one should worry not that the world is not yet well governed, but that the people’s hearts are not yet benevolent; one should worry not that the people are not yet benevolent, but that governmental institutions are not yet good. Thus, when a sage comes forth, he, in his own person, brings peace to the realm…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之廣以一人而宰兆民之繁知治世當以大德
也于焉易田薄斂立善政以開民菽粟之源知
為政不在小惠也于焉食時用禮制成規以節
民菽粟之流使其藏於民者源源相繼比閭無
間於族黨如水火之時時常足隨取而隨與也
不云烝民其乃粒乎使其蓄於下者陳陳相因
鄉遂無間於都鄙如水火之在在皆給隨求而
隨得也不云百室其盈止乎夫菽粟如水火則
衣食足而禮義自生俯仰給而廉恥自作將見
===
民之出作入息者一皆興孝興弟篤恩義於綱
常倫理之天民之耕食鑿飲者罔不興禮興讓
惇良心於民彞物則之域仁風行而偷風消閭
閻之下殆有所謂順帝之則者矣求其胥戕而
不仁者何有乎仁俗洽而澆俗泯里巷之間殆
有所謂徧為爾德者矣求其胥殘而不仁者何
得乎吁以民行之興而由於民食之足如此有
天下者可不知所先務哉抑論之民生固不可
無養而民富則不可無教斯二者治天下之本
punctuated: 之廣，以一人而宰兆民之繁，知治世當以大德也，于焉易田薄斂，立善政以開民菽粟之源；知為政不在小惠也，于焉食時用禮，制成規以節民菽粟之流。使其藏於民者源源相繼，比閭無間於族黨，如水火之時時常足，隨取而隨與也，不云「烝民其乃粒」乎？使其蓄於下者陳陳相因，鄉遂無間於都鄙，如水火之在在皆給，隨求而隨得也，不云「百室其盈止」乎？夫菽粟如水火，則衣食足而禮義自生，俯仰給而廉恥自作。將見民之出作入息者，一皆興孝興弟，篤恩義於綱常倫理之天；民之耕食鑿飲者，罔不興禮興讓，惇良心於民彞物則之域。仁風行而偷風消，閭閻之下，殆有所謂「順帝之則」者矣，求其胥戕而不仁者，何有乎？仁俗洽而澆俗泯，里巷之間，殆有所謂「徧為爾德」者矣，求其胥殘而不仁者，何得乎？吁！以民行之興而由於民食之足如此，有天下者可不知所先務哉？抑論之，民生固不可無養，而民富則不可無教，斯二者治天下之本
translation_en:
…in all its vastness, and, as a single person, govern the teeming multitudes. Knowing that ordering the world requires great virtue, the sage accordingly ensures that fields are well cultivated and levies light, establishing good government to open up the sources of the people's beans and grain. Knowing that government does not consist in petty favors, he accordingly regulates eating by the seasons and expenditure by ritual, establishing standing rules to moderate the outflow of the people's beans and grain. Thus the stores kept among the people are continuously replenished, with no disparity between the smaller neighborhood groupings and the larger communities. Like water and fire, they are always sufficient: whenever someone takes some, there is some to give. Is this not what is meant by “The multitudes were thus fed with grain”? Thus the provisions accumulated among the populace pile up, old stores upon old, with no disparity between rural districts or between towns and outlying settlements. Like water and fire, they are available everywhere: whenever someone seeks them, they can be obtained. Is this not what is meant by “The hundred households are full”?

When beans and grain are as plentiful as water and fire, clothing and food are sufficient, and ritual propriety and righteousness arise of themselves. With enough to support parents above and children below, integrity and a sense of shame awaken of themselves. We shall then see the people who go out to work and return to rest all stirred to filial devotion and fraternal respect, strengthening affection and duty within the Heaven-ordained framework of cardinal relationships and ethical obligations. Those who plow for their food and dig wells for their drink will all be stirred to ritual propriety and deference, nurturing their innate moral goodness within the bounds of enduring human norms and the principles governing things.

As benevolent influences spread and habits of moral laxity disappear, among the common households there will surely be what is called “following the rules of the Lord on High.” Where could one find people who cruelly harm one another? As benevolent customs become pervasive and shallow customs vanish, among the village lanes there will surely be what is called “universally practicing your virtue.” Where could one find people who cruelly injure one another? Ah! Since the flourishing of the people's moral conduct depends in this way upon the sufficiency of their food, can those who possess the realm fail to know which task must come first?

Yet, to consider the matter further, the people's livelihood certainly cannot go without material support; and when the people are prosperous, they cannot go without instruction. These two are the foundations of governing the world…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可偏廢也古帝王所以仁民之道率不外此然
論其施為之序則養民尤其急務况戰國之時
民窮財盡救死不贍奚暇治禮義哉故孟子於
此章之論獨歸重於養民之政是雖有所感而
發亦曰教由養立欲君人者先急其本而後驅
之善非謂民食既足遂不教而聽其自化也不
然何昔者陳王道於宣王乃於養民之後而必
曰謹庠序之教申之以孝弟之義觀此可以知
孟子發言之微意矣噫
===
易
外比於賢以從上也
方策
同考試官訓導鄭 批 此題塲中士子易於
下筆而難於整齊其講比賢從上不覺失之
重複獨此卷提掇明白略無贅辭必精於說
易者高薦何忝
考試官教諭姜 批 聖人象傳之意正如
此子獨能闡明之殆熟於本領故也
punctuated:
可偏廢也？古帝王所以仁民之道，率不外此。然論其施為之序，則養民尤其急務。况戰國之時，民窮財盡，救死不贍，奚暇治禮義哉？故孟子於此章之論，獨歸重於養民之政。是雖有所感而發，亦曰教由養立，欲君人者先急其本，而後驅之善，非謂民食既足，遂不教而聽其自化也。不然，何昔者陳王道於宣王，乃於養民之後，而必曰：「謹庠序之教，申之以孝弟之義。」觀此，可以知孟子發言之微意矣。噫！

易
外比於賢，以從上也。
方策

同考試官訓導鄭批：此題塲中士子易於下筆，而難於整齊。其講比賢從上，不覺失之重複。獨此卷提掇明白，略無贅辭，必精於說易者，高薦何忝？

考試官教諭姜批：聖人象傳之意正如此，子獨能闡明之，殆熟於本領故也。
translation_en:
…can either be neglected? The ways by which the ancient emperors and kings treated the people humanely generally went no further than these. Yet, in the order of implementation, providing for the people is the most urgent task. Moreover, during the Warring States period, the people were impoverished and their resources exhausted; they could scarcely save themselves from death. What leisure did they have to attend to ritual and righteousness? Thus, in his discussion in this chapter, Mencius placed particular weight on policies for providing for the people. Although his words arose in response to particular circumstances, he also meant that instruction rests upon material provision: those who would rule others should first attend urgently to this foundation and then lead them toward goodness. He did not mean that, once the people had sufficient food, rulers should dispense with instruction and leave them to transform themselves. Otherwise, why, when he formerly expounded the Kingly Way to King Xuan, did he insist, after discussing provision for the people, on saying: “Attend carefully to instruction in the schools, reinforcing it with the duties of filial piety and respect for elder brothers”? From this we can understand the subtle intent of Mencius’s words. Ah!

Book of Changes
“Joining outwardly with the worthy is the means of following one’s superior.”
Fang Ce

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: Candidates in the examination hall could readily begin writing on this topic, but found it difficult to arrange their arguments coherently. In explaining joining with the worthy and following one’s superior, they unwittingly fell into repetition. This paper alone brings out the essentials clearly, without any superfluous wording. Its author must be accomplished in expounding the Book of Changes. How could recommending him for a high place be undeserved?

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: This is precisely the sage’s meaning in the Commentary on the Images. You alone have been able to elucidate it, presumably because you have a thorough grasp of the fundamentals.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張批〔說理明净〕
象傳論柔爻之進輔於有德以委身於明君也
夫德位兼隆之君臣子難逢之會也四得是君
而外輔之庸有不正而吉也哉昔周公於比之
六四既繫以外比之貞吉之辭矣吾夫子小象
從而申之謂夫比以得賢為貞臣願得君而事
彼六四也以柔正之德當親比之時位居承弼
固已出而比人矣而比得所比以有德者而為
依歸匪人之傷寧復有之身進廟堂固已出而
===
有輔矣而輔得所輔有賢人焉而為倚託失身
之誚誰能加之夫六四之外比於賢如此豈非
以其從上也哉誠以卦之九五剛健而純德邁
等倫矣而崇高是履巍然建極之大君普天之
下尊无二上者焉中正而粹賢超儔類矣而曆
數在躬赫然顯比之令主四海之廣仰惟一人
者焉四之外比正惟其以柔順之德而上輔於
此君光依日月之下所謂夙夜匪懈以事一人
者是已贊化調元何一而不可行者乎正惟其
punctuated:
考試官教諭張批〔說理明净〕

象傳論柔爻之進，輔於有德，以委身於明君也。

夫德位兼隆之君，臣子難逢之會也。四得是君而外輔之，庸有不正而吉也哉？昔周公於比之六四，既繫以外比之貞吉之辭矣。吾夫子小象從而申之，謂夫比以得賢為貞，臣願得君而事。彼六四也，以柔正之德，當親比之時，位居承弼，固已出而比人矣。而比得所比，以有德者而為依歸，匪人之傷寧復有之？身進廟堂，固已出而有輔矣。而輔得所輔，有賢人焉而為倚託，失身之誚誰能加之？夫六四之外比於賢如此，豈非以其從上也哉？誠以卦之九五，剛健而純德，邁等倫矣。而崇高是履，巍然建極之大君，普天之下尊无二上者焉。中正而粹賢，超儔類矣。而曆數在躬，赫然顯比之令主，四海之廣仰惟一人者焉。四之外比，正惟其以柔順之德而上輔於此君，光依日月之下，所謂夙夜匪懈以事一人者是已。贊化調元，何一而不可行者乎？正惟其
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔The exposition of principle is clear and lucid.〕

The Commentary on the Images discusses the yielding line’s advance: it assists one possessed of virtue, thereby committing itself to an enlightened ruler.

A ruler exalted alike in virtue and position offers an opportunity that a subject rarely encounters. When the fourth line finds such a ruler and turns outward to assist him, how could this fail to be correct and auspicious? Formerly, the Duke of Zhou attached to the fourth, yin line of Bi (Holding Together) the words, “Holding together outwardly: constancy brings good fortune.” Our Master Confucius then elaborated upon them in the Lesser Commentary on the Images. His meaning was that holding together takes finding a worthy person as its standard of correctness, and that a subject wishes to find a ruler whom he can serve. That fourth, yin line, with its yielding and correct virtue, encounters a time of close association and occupies a position of supporting and assisting the ruler. It has indeed come forward to associate with another. Moreover, it associates with the proper person, finding its refuge in one possessed of virtue. How could the harm of associating with an unworthy person arise again? It advances into the court and has indeed come forward to offer assistance. Moreover, it assists the proper person, having a worthy man upon whom to rely. Who could reproach it for having committed itself to the wrong person? Since the fourth, yin line thus holds together outwardly with the worthy, is this not because it follows the one above?

Indeed, the fifth, yang line of the hexagram is firm and vigorous, its virtue pure, surpassing its peers. It occupies the loftiest position: a majestic sovereign who establishes the supreme standard, whose supremacy admits no second ruler anywhere under Heaven. Central and correct, wholly worthy, it exceeds all others of its kind. The succession ordained by Heaven rests in its person: a splendid and excellent ruler who manifests the bonds of union, the one person to whom all within the four seas look up. The fourth line’s outward association consists precisely in using its yielding and compliant virtue to assist this ruler above. Gloriously sheltered beneath the sun and moon, it exemplifies the saying, “Morning and night, never slackening, serving the One Man.” In assisting the transforming processes and harmonizing the primal forces, what undertaking could it not carry out? It is precisely because it …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以柔正之臣而順麗乎大明誠同葵藿之傾所
謂忠順不失以事其上者是已立德立功有一
之不得遂者乎是則五之為君間世而一出四
之從五千載而一時得正而吉也顧不宜哉大
抵君臣之分雖相懸君臣之道未始不相須也
故君不得臣則无以行其萬化臣不得君亦无
以展其平生但自古昔以來有其君者未必有
其臣有其臣者未必遇其君相須之殷相值之
難唐虞賡歌所以曠千古而一見也然則四之
===
於五何幸而躬逢夫子於四寧不喜談而樂道
之也哉噫唐虞遠矣求其上下交而成德業者
深有望於
今日
是以明於天之道而察於民之故是興神
物以前民用
李高
同考試官訓導鄭 批 說出聖人作易之由
與教人之意詳盡可錄可錄
punctuated:
以柔正之臣而順麗乎大明，誠同葵藿之傾，所謂忠順不失以事其上者是已。立德立功，有一之不得遂者乎？是則五之為君，間世而一出；四之從五，千載而一時。得正而吉也，顧不宜哉？大抵君臣之分雖相懸，君臣之道未始不相須也。故君不得臣，則无以行其萬化；臣不得君，亦无以展其平生。但自古昔以來，有其君者未必有其臣，有其臣者未必遇其君。相須之殷，相值之難，唐虞賡歌所以曠千古而一見也。然則四之於五，何幸而躬逢！夫子於四，寧不喜談而樂道之也哉？噫！唐虞遠矣，求其上下交而成德業者，深有望於今日。
是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。
李高
同考試官訓導鄭批：說出聖人作易之由與教人之意，詳盡，可錄，可錄。
translation_en:
…as a yielding and upright minister, he obediently attaches himself to the great light, his sincerity like that of sunflowers and mallows inclining toward the sun. This is what is meant by serving one’s superior without failing in loyalty and obedience. In establishing virtue and accomplishing meritorious deeds, could anything remain unfulfilled? Thus a ruler such as the fifth line appears only once in several generations; the fourth line’s following the fifth is an encounter that comes but once in a thousand years. Attaining correctness and good fortune—is this not fitting? Broadly speaking, although ruler and minister stand far apart in rank, their respective ways have always depended upon one another. Hence, without a minister, a ruler has no means to carry out his manifold transforming influences; without a ruler, a minister likewise has no means to realize his lifelong aspirations. Yet since ancient times, the presence of such a ruler has not necessarily meant the presence of such a minister, nor has such a minister necessarily encountered such a ruler. So deeply do they need each other, and so difficult is their meeting: this is why the responsive singing of ruler and ministers in the age of Tang and Yu was a sight seen but once across the ages. How fortunate, then, that the fourth line should personally encounter the fifth! Could the Master fail to speak of the fourth line with delight? Alas! The age of Tang and Yu is distant indeed. For superiors and subordinates to join together and bring virtue and achievement to fruition, we place profound hopes in the present day.
“Therefore, understanding the Way of Heaven and discerning the circumstances of the people, they brought forth the numinous objects to guide the people’s use of them.”
Li Gao
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: “It explains the reasons why the sages made the Book of Changes and their intentions in teaching people. Thorough and complete; worthy of inclusion, worthy of inclusion.”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭姜批題本冠冕而文亦官
樣錄之
考試官教諭張批切實簡當
聖人通天人之理有以肇卜筮之用焉夫一貫
天人聖心之妙契也如是而作為卜筮以教人
易之用豈不大行於天下哉大傳此章專論卜
筮及此謂夫易理既體具於聖心易教必興行
於天下是故天道幽遠而難明者也聖人纖塵
不染有以洞燭其潜庸默運之機若何而變化
===
若何而生成難明者於是乎大明矣民故浩繁
而難察者也聖人內境常清有以周知夫民生
日用之故如何而得失如何而憂虞難察者於
是乎畢察矣夫天道明則知蓍龜靈氣之所鍾
而可興其用民故察則知生民趨避之莫識而
當開其先於是興蓍以筮用之四十有九分揲
掛扐之法以立興龜以卜鑽之七十有二雨霽
蒙驛克之兆以見用静用作作者賴以指迷豐功
於是乎肇啓矣有為有行者資其賛决大業于
punctuated:
考試官教諭姜批：題本冠冕，而文亦官樣，錄之。
考試官教諭張批：切實簡當。
聖人通天人之理，有以肇卜筮之用焉。夫一貫天人，聖心之妙契也。如是而作為卜筮以教人，《易》之用豈不大行於天下哉？《大傳》此章專論卜筮，及此謂夫《易》理既體具於聖心，《易》教必興行於天下。是故天道幽遠而難明者也，聖人纖塵不染，有以洞燭其潜庸默運之機：若何而變化，若何而生成，難明者於是乎大明矣。民故浩繁而難察者也，聖人內境常清，有以周知夫民生日用之故：如何而得失，如何而憂虞，難察者於是乎畢察矣。夫天道明，則知蓍龜靈氣之所鍾，而可興其用；民故察，則知生民趨避之莫識，而當開其先。於是興蓍以筮，用之四十有九，分揲掛扐之法以立；興龜以卜，鑽之七十有二，雨霽蒙驛克之兆以見。用静用作作者賴以指迷，豐功於是乎肇啓矣；有為有行者資其賛决，大業于
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is dignified, and the essay likewise follows the official style. Include it.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Concrete, concise, and apt.”
The sage comprehends the principles of Heaven and humanity and thereby initiates the use of turtle-shell and milfoil divination. To unite Heaven and humanity in a single thread is the wondrous understanding of the sage’s mind. If, on this basis, he establishes divination to instruct people, will not the application of the Book of Changes spread widely throughout the world? This chapter of the Great Commentary deals specifically with divination. At this point it means that, since the principles of the Changes are embodied in the sage’s mind, its teachings must be brought into practice throughout the world.
The Way of Heaven is hidden and remote, difficult to understand. The sage, unstained by the slightest speck of dust, can penetrate its hidden, silently operating workings [?]: how transformation occurs and how things are generated and brought to completion. What was difficult to understand thus becomes fully clear. Human affairs are vast and multitudinous, difficult to discern. The sage’s inner realm remains constantly clear, enabling him to know comprehensively the circumstances of people’s daily lives: how gains and losses arise, and how anxieties and apprehensions arise. What was difficult to discern is thus entirely perceived.
Understanding the Way of Heaven, he knows that milfoil and turtles are where numinous vital energy concentrates, and that their use can be instituted. Discerning human affairs, he knows that people do not understand what to pursue or avoid, and that he must open the way before them. He therefore institutes milfoil divination, using forty-nine stalks and establishing the procedures of dividing, counting, setting aside, and holding the remainders between the fingers. He institutes turtle-shell divination, drilling seventy-two cavities so that the signs called rain, clearing, cloudiness, discontinuity, and crossing appear. Those at rest or undertaking action [?] rely on these to dispel uncertainty; great accomplishments thus begin to unfold. Those who undertake enterprises and carry out actions draw upon their aid in reaching decisions, and great undertakings …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
此乎開先矣是則聖人之通天人而立卜筮如
此則利生民澤後世厥功何如其大哉大抵有
人心之易有造化之易有易書之易神知易貢
之德易之具於聖心者也天道民故之類易之
見於造化者也至於畫卦卜筮易始載於易書
矣非聖心有易无以通乎造化非造化有易无
以會乎聖心非筆之於書則易將自造化聖人
而止耳百姓何以與其能哉此三才合一之道
也學者求易於易不若求於造化求於造化不
===
若求於吾心
書
德日新萬邦惟懷
吳顯宗
同考試官教諭鄭 批 德日新二句是言人
心離合之機至下文懋德建中才是作工夫處
士子多以仲虺勉成湯如此用工殊戾本旨是
篇依傳註敷衍明白而辭理蔚然其必深
於書者歟
punctuated:
此乎開先矣。是則聖人之通天人而立卜筮如此，則利生民、澤後世，厥功何如其大哉！大抵有人心之易，有造化之易，有易書之易。神知易貢之德，易之具於聖心者也；天道民故之類，易之見於造化者也。至於畫卦卜筮，易始載於易書矣。非聖心有易，无以通乎造化；非造化有易，无以會乎聖心；非筆之於書，則易將自造化聖人而止耳，百姓何以與其能哉？此三才合一之道也。學者求易於易，不若求於造化；求於造化，不若求於吾心。

書
德日新，萬邦惟懷。
吳顯宗

同考試官教諭鄭批：「德日新二句，是言人心離合之機；至下文懋德建中，才是作工夫處。士子多以仲虺勉成湯如此用工，殊戾本旨。是篇依傳註敷衍明白，而辭理蔚然，其必深於書者歟？」
translation_en:
…are thus given their beginnings. Such is the way in which the sage comprehends Heaven and humanity and establishes divination by tortoise shell and milfoil. How great, then, is his achievement in benefiting the living people and extending blessings to later generations!

Broadly speaking, there are the Changes within the human heart, the Changes within the transformations of nature, and the Changes within the Book of Changes. The virtues of spiritual understanding and “易貢” [?] are the Changes embodied in the sage’s heart. Such things as the Way of Heaven and the circumstances of the people are the Changes manifested in nature’s transformations. Only with the drawing of hexagrams and divination by tortoise shell and milfoil did the Changes come to be recorded in the Book of Changes. Were the Changes not present in the sage’s heart, he could not comprehend nature’s transformations; were the Changes not present in nature’s transformations, these could not accord with the sage’s heart. Without their being committed to writing, the Changes would extend only as far as nature’s transformations and the sage. How could the common people participate in their efficacy? This is the Way by which the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—are united as one. For students, seeking the Changes in the Book of Changes is less effective than seeking them in nature’s transformations; seeking them in nature’s transformations is less effective than seeking them in one’s own heart.

Book of Documents
“When virtue is renewed daily, the myriad states cherish allegiance.”
Wu Xianzong

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The two clauses beginning ‘When virtue is renewed daily’ speak of the crucial factor determining whether people’s hearts turn away or come together in allegiance. Only in the subsequent passage, ‘Make virtue flourish and establish the Mean,’ does the text address the actual work of cultivation. Examination candidates often interpret this as Zhonghui urging Cheng Tang to apply himself in this way, which seriously conflicts with the original meaning. This essay develops its exposition clearly in accordance with the commentary and annotations, while its language and reasoning are rich and accomplished. Surely its author has a profound understanding of the Book of Documents!”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭姜批新德萬邦懷處發揮
明白
考試官教諭張批人君新德而懷諸侯
此作深合傳意
一人之脩德無間其功羣辟之仰德無間其地
盖德乃繫屬天下之本也人君脩德而能常其
功則諸侯之仰德寧有間乎仲虺勸勉成湯統
御諸侯之道有如此其意若謂君天下以德為
本君德之脩否係萬邦之向背王可不益脩其
===
德而思所以繫其心乎是故奮剛健不息之誠
顧天明命而疏瀹之功視昔為有加雖日孜孜
也持謙冲不滿之心懷帝降衷而澡雪之カ視
昔為彌篤終日乾乾也敬以直内存養于念慮
之微大政如是微言如是渣滓消融而萬象為
之森羅湛然全體之無瑕義以方外省察於事
為之著大廷如是深宮如是邪穢蕩滌而萬景
為之俱新昭然大用之不昧如是則一德有恒
足以收人心之放一德無貳足以合天下之離
punctuated:
考試官教諭姜批：新德萬邦懷處，發揮明白。
考試官教諭張批：人君新德而懷諸侯，此作深合傳意。
一人之脩德無間其功，羣辟之仰德無間其地。盖德乃繫屬天下之本也。人君脩德而能常其功，則諸侯之仰德寧有間乎？仲虺勸勉成湯統御諸侯之道有如此。其意若謂：君天下以德為本，君德之脩否係萬邦之向背，王可不益脩其德而思所以繫其心乎？是故奮剛健不息之誠，顧天明命，而疏瀹之功視昔為有加，雖日孜孜也；持謙冲不滿之心，懷帝降衷，而澡雪之カ視昔為彌篤，終日乾乾也。敬以直内，存養于念慮之微，大政如是，微言如是，渣滓消融而萬象為之森羅，湛然全體之無瑕；義以方外，省察於事為之著，大廷如是，深宮如是，邪穢蕩滌而萬景為之俱新，昭然大用之不昧。如是則一德有恒，足以收人心之放；一德無貳，足以合天下之離
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, School Instructor, comments: The passage on renewing virtue and winning the allegiance of the myriad states is developed clearly.
Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: The ruler renews his virtue and thereby wins the allegiance of the feudal lords. This composition accords closely with the meaning of the commentary.
When the One Man cultivates virtue without interruption in his efforts, the many princes look up to his virtue without distinction of place. For virtue is the foundation for binding all under Heaven together. If the ruler cultivates virtue and can persevere in his efforts, how could there be any exception among the feudal lords in looking up to his virtue? Such was the way of governing the feudal lords that Zhonghui urged upon Cheng Tang. His meaning was as though he said: To rule all under Heaven, one must take virtue as the foundation. Whether the myriad states turn toward their ruler or away from him depends on whether he cultivates his virtue. Can the king fail to cultivate his virtue still further and consider how to bind their hearts to him?
Thus he rouses a sincerity that is vigorous and unceasing, keeps Heaven’s luminous mandate in view, and increases his efforts to cleanse his heart beyond those of former times, being diligent day by day [?]. He maintains a humble heart free from self-satisfaction, cherishes the moral nature bestowed by the Lord on High, and applies himself to purification [?] more earnestly than before, remaining unremittingly vigilant throughout the day. Through reverence he makes his inner self upright, preserving and nurturing it in the subtle workings of thought. He does so in great affairs of government and in the slightest utterances alike. Impurities dissolve, and the myriad forms stand arrayed in their fullness: his whole moral being is limpid and without blemish. Through righteousness he makes his outward conduct correct, examining himself in the manifest workings of affairs and actions. He does so in the great court and in the palace’s inner recesses alike. Depravity and pollution are swept away, and every prospect is renewed: the full operation of his virtue is luminous and unobscured. In this way, constancy in his single virtue suffices to gather in people’s straying hearts; freedom from duplicity in his single virtue suffices to unite all that is divided under Heaven…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬邦雖遠焉有不懷者乎振舉於此而遠者聞
焉思欲望闕廷而納欵鼓舞于風聲之下盖異
地而同心軌範於此而遠者效焉思欲依衮冕
而稽顙沐浴於德教之中盖殊方而一志曰朝
曰覲顒然六服承德之休殆若萬派之必趨乎
東也曰會曰同翕然庶邦丕享之盛殆若衆星
之必拱乎北也夫有天下而為天下君必君德
新而萬邦懷則人心之收放合離其本固有在
而其機亦可畏也王可不思所以盡今日之責
===
而徒為來世之恐哉抑仲虺是篇為釋成湯之
慚而作也愚甞因是竊疑前古聖人順天應人
心事光明顧尤恐恐然有不勝之情不滿之懷
而其輔弼大臣開釋勸諭無慮數百言要之不
過述天命本人情諄諄乎脩德檢身之說終不
敢指其心事之底蘊直謂其必無以破其跼蹐
不寧之心則其在上不似失之迂而在下不似
失之泛乎夫君臣之際關天下古今之大防此
正見有商君臣心之不容已言之不苟發皆出
punctuated:
萬邦雖遠，焉有不懷者乎？振舉於此，而遠者聞焉，思欲望闕廷而納欵，鼓舞于風聲之下，盖異地而同心。軌範於此，而遠者效焉，思欲依衮冕而稽顙，沐浴於德教之中，盖殊方而一志。曰朝曰覲，顒然六服承德之休，殆若萬派之必趨乎東也；曰會曰同，翕然庶邦丕享之盛，殆若衆星之必拱乎北也。夫有天下而為天下君，必君德新而萬邦懷，則人心之收放合離，其本固有在，而其機亦可畏也。王可不思所以盡今日之責，而徒為來世之恐哉？

抑仲虺是篇，為釋成湯之慚而作也。愚甞因是竊疑：前古聖人，順天應人，心事光明，顧尤恐恐然，有不勝之情、不滿之懷，而其輔弼大臣開釋勸諭，無慮數百言，要之不過述天命、本人情，諄諄乎脩德檢身之說，終不敢指其心事之底蘊，直謂其必無，以破其跼蹐不寧之心，則其在上不似失之迂，而在下不似失之泛乎？夫君臣之際，關天下古今之大防。此正見有商君臣，心之不容已，言之不苟發，皆出
translation_en:
…Though the myriad states are distant, how could any fail to cherish allegiance? When the ruler acts with vigor here, those far away hear of it and wish to look toward the palace court and offer their allegiance. Inspired by his influence and reputation, they share one heart despite dwelling in different lands. When he establishes an exemplary standard here, those far away emulate it and wish to draw near his ceremonial robes and crown and bow their foreheads to the ground. Bathed in his virtuous teaching, they share one resolve despite inhabiting different regions. At the spring and autumn audiences, the six zones of submission reverently receive the blessings of his virtue, much as myriad streams inevitably flow eastward. At the occasional and general assemblies, the many states unite in a splendid display of offerings, much as the multitude of stars inevitably pay homage to the north celestial pole. Now, one who possesses all under Heaven and rules as its sovereign must renew his sovereign virtue so that the myriad states cherish allegiance. Whether people’s hearts are gathered in or let stray, united or divided, thus certainly has its root; yet the workings of this process are also to be regarded with awe. Can the king fail to consider how to fulfill his responsibility today and merely fear what later ages will bring?

Now, this piece by Zhong Hui was written to dispel Cheng Tang’s shame. I have ventured, in my ignorance, to entertain a doubt on this account. The sages of antiquity followed Heaven and responded to the people; their intentions and deeds were clear and upright. Yet they remained fearful, feeling unequal to their task and dissatisfied with themselves. Their great assisting ministers offered explanations, encouragement, and counsel amounting to several hundred words. In substance, these merely expounded Heaven’s mandate and took human feelings as their basis, earnestly dwelling on cultivating virtue and keeping oneself in check. They never dared to point directly to the innermost grounds of the ruler’s intentions and deeds and declare outright that he surely had no cause for shame, thereby dispelling his constrained and uneasy state of mind. Does it not seem, then, that those above erred in being overly scrupulous, and those below in being too general? Yet the relationship between ruler and minister bears upon the great safeguards of all under Heaven, in antiquity and today alike. This precisely reveals how the Shang ruler and his minister could not suppress what was in their hearts and would not utter words carelessly: all issued from…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於常情之外者先民謂此心之慚此誥之釋皆
不可無吁旨哉
自朝至于日中昃不遑暇食
朱鵬
同考試官教諭鄭批不遑暇食是言文王
勤政之心雖一食之頃有不遑暇非言文王果於
不食也作者多昧此意此篇說出文王不暇逸之
心明白痛快非有心得者不能到此宜取之以冠
本房
===
考試官教諭姜批文王勤勞之心此作
可想見
考試官教諭張批發出文王無逸之心
時已周於一日心不逸於終食聖王勤政事然
也甚矣聖王圖治之切也一日之周而無終食
之逸其勤於政事也如此哉昔周公舉文王之
無逸以告成王此則言其勤政事意謂有國家
者未有不以勤而興盍不觀我周之文王乎自
朝至于日之中計一日之晷時之更涉悠悠乎
punctuated:
於常情之外者。先民謂此心之慚、此誥之釋，皆不可無。吁，旨哉！

自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食。
朱鵬

同考試官教諭鄭批：不遑暇食，是言文王勤政之心，雖一食之頃有不遑暇，非言文王果於不食也。作者多昧此意，此篇說出文王不暇逸之心，明白痛快，非有心得者不能到此，宜取之以冠本房。

考試官教諭姜批：文王勤勞之心，此作可想見。

考試官教諭張批：發出文王無逸之心。

時已周於一日，心不逸於終食，聖王勤政事然也。甚矣，聖王圖治之切也！一日之周，而無終食之逸，其勤於政事也如此哉！昔周公舉文王之無逸以告成王，此則言其勤政事。意謂有國家者，未有不以勤而興，盍不觀我周之文王乎？自朝至于日之中，計一日之晷，時之更涉，悠悠乎
translation_en:
…beyond ordinary human feeling. Our predecessors said that neither the shame felt in this heart nor the reassurance offered in this proclamation could be dispensed with. Ah, how profound!

“From morning until the sun had passed its zenith, he had no leisure to eat.”
Zhu Peng 朱鵬

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng 鄭, Instructor: “Having no leisure to eat” describes King Wen’s devotion to government: he felt he could not spare even the time needed for a single meal. It does not mean that King Wen was determined to go without food. Writers often miss this meaning. This essay expresses King Wen’s sense that he had no leisure for ease, clearly and forcefully. No one without personal insight could attain this level. It should be selected as the best essay in this examining section.

Comment by Examiner Jiang 姜, Instructor: This composition enables one to picture King Wen’s diligent heart.

Comment by Examiner Zhang 張, Instructor: It brings out King Wen’s resolve to shun ease.

Though time had run through an entire day, his heart took no ease even for the duration of a meal: such was the sage king’s diligence in affairs of government. How earnest was the sage king’s pursuit of good government! Through the course of a whole day, he enjoyed no respite even for a meal. Such was his diligence in governing! Formerly, the Duke of Zhou cited King Wen’s avoidance of ease in admonishing King Cheng; here he spoke of his diligence in government. His meaning was that those who rule a state have never flourished except through diligence. Why not look to King Wen of our Zhou? From morning until midday, reckoning by the sundial’s measure of a day, the hours pass on and on…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
已居一日之半歷時固不淺也自中至于日之
昃計一日之運時之更閱綿綿乎已盡一日之
終歷時固何多也人之大情自謂享有天下孰
不欲珍饈迭舉於移時醉飽為歡於終日文王
之心則以為一政未脩畎畝之艱難係焉一事
未舉閭巷之怨詛關焉求治如渴而憂勤之心
恒存於旦晝之頃視民如傷而惕勵之念每切
於朝夕之間或朝而饔歟為時特轉移也一朝
饔之不遑文王非要譽也精神所運惟欲納庶
===
政於惟和之域汲汲乎規畫之周詳心自有不
遑耳或暮而飧歟為時特奄忽也一暮飧之不
暇文王非矯情也意念所注惟欲措庶事於惟
康之境皇皇乎綜理之微密心自有不暇耳即
一日而一歲一月之日可因而類推舉一食而
一身一家之奉可由而例見文王之勤政事如
此今王為文王之文孫而嗣有文王之大業烏
可不思所以法文王以慰其在天之靈哉抑周
公斯言特文王無逸中之一節耳然要之君人
punctuated: 已居一日之半，歷時固不淺也。自中至于日之昃，計一日之運，時之更閱，綿綿乎已盡一日之終，歷時固何多也！人之大情，自謂享有天下，孰不欲珍饈迭舉於移時，醉飽為歡於終日？文王之心則以為一政未脩，畎畝之艱難係焉；一事未舉，閭巷之怨詛關焉。求治如渴，而憂勤之心恒存於旦晝之頃；視民如傷，而惕勵之念每切於朝夕之間。或朝而饔歟？為時特轉移也。一朝饔之不遑，文王非要譽也。精神所運，惟欲納庶政於惟和之域，汲汲乎規畫之周詳，心自有不遑耳。或暮而飧歟？為時特奄忽也。一暮飧之不暇，文王非矯情也。意念所注，惟欲措庶事於惟康之境，皇皇乎綜理之微密，心自有不暇耳。即一日而一歲一月之日可因而類推，舉一食而一身一家之奉可由而例見。文王之勤政事如此，今王為文王之文孫，而嗣有文王之大業，烏可不思所以法文王，以慰其在天之靈哉？抑周公斯言，特文王無逸中之一節耳。然要之，君人
translation_en:
…half the day has already passed: the time elapsed is certainly not short. From noon until the sun declines, reckon the course of a day: as the hours pass in succession, the whole day draws to its close. How much time has indeed elapsed! It is common human feeling that, once one considers oneself possessor of all under Heaven, one wishes to have delicacies served in succession for hours on end, taking pleasure in drinking and eating one's fill throughout the day. Yet King Wen thought that if a single measure of government remained unattended to, the hardships of those working the fields depended upon it; if a single undertaking remained unaccomplished, the complaints and curses of the village lanes were bound up with it. He thirsted for good government, and his anxious diligence persisted through the daylight hours. He cared for the people as though they were injured, and his resolve to remain vigilant and exert himself was keen from morning to evening.

Might he take his morning meal? It would require only a brief interval. Yet when he had no leisure for that morning meal, King Wen was not seeking praise. All his mental energies were directed toward bringing the many affairs of government into harmony. Intent upon making his plans comprehensive and thorough, he naturally felt that he had no leisure. Might he take his evening meal? It would require only a fleeting moment. Yet when he had no time for that evening meal, King Wen was not affecting sentiments he did not feel. His thoughts were concentrated solely upon bringing all affairs into a state of well-being. Anxiously attending to the subtle details of their overall management, he naturally felt that he had no time.

From this one day, one may infer by analogy how he spent the days of a year or a month; from this one meal, one may discern how he approached the provision for his own person and his household. Such was King Wen's diligence in government. The present king is King Wen's cultivated descendant and has inherited King Wen's great enterprise. How could he fail to consider how to emulate King Wen and thereby console his spirit in Heaven? Yet these words of the Duke of Zhou concern only one aspect of King Wen's refusal to indulge in ease. Nevertheless, in essence, for those who rule over others…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者之大法亦孰有要于此者乎向使時君世主
深體而力行之必不至窮口腹之欲流連光景
萬事之所由必理萬民之所由必治召太和迎
善氣壽國脉而享長年盖有必然者噫有周八
百年有道之長孰謂不自文王一食之頃有不
遑暇中來哉
詩
文王受命有此武功既伐于崇作邑于豐
文王烝哉
===
王珵
同考試官教諭方批場中士子率於受命
武功處體貼欠真且發揮安民意不出獨此篇
認理精到措詞豐麗宜錄以冠本房
同考試官學正陳批就安民上說出聖人
遷豐之心痛快可取
考試官教諭姜批理明詞暢其善說詩
者
考試官教諭張批議論新竒文氣奪目
punctuated:
者之大法，亦孰有要于此者乎？向使時君世主深體而力行之，必不至窮口腹之欲，流連光景。萬事之所由必理，萬民之所由必治，召太和，迎善氣，壽國脉而享長年，盖有必然者。噫！有周八百年有道之長，孰謂不自文王一食之頃有不遑暇中來哉？

詩

文王受命，有此武功。既伐于崇，作邑于豐。文王烝哉！

王珵

同考試官教諭方批：場中士子率於受命、武功處體貼欠真，且發揮安民意不出。獨此篇認理精到，措詞豐麗，宜錄以冠本房。

同考試官學正陳批：就安民上說出聖人遷豐之心，痛快可取。

考試官教諭姜批：理明詞暢，其善說詩者。

考試官教諭張批：議論新竒，文氣奪目。
translation_en:
…among the great principles for those who rule, what could be more essential than this? Had the rulers of successive ages deeply understood it and earnestly put it into practice, they would surely never have indulged their appetites to the utmost or idled their days away. All affairs would necessarily have been duly ordered, and all the people properly governed. They would have summoned supreme harmony, welcomed auspicious influences, prolonged the life of the state, and enjoyed long years themselves: these would surely have been the results. Ah! Who could say that the Zhou dynasty’s eight hundred years of enduring, principled rule did not spring from King Wen’s inability to spare even the time for a single meal?

Book of Odes

“King Wen received the Mandate and accomplished these martial deeds. Having attacked Chong, he built a city at Feng. How great was King Wen!”

Wang Cheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: Most candidates in the examination hall failed to grasp accurately the passages about receiving the Mandate and martial achievements; moreover, they could not bring out the intention of bringing peace to the people. This essay alone apprehends the principle with precision and expresses it in rich and elegant language. It should be selected for inclusion and placed first among the essays in this examining room.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: By focusing on bringing peace to the people, this essay brings out the sage’s intention in moving to Feng. Its exposition is forceful and satisfying, and merits selection.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Its reasoning is clear and its expression fluent. Here is someone skilled at interpreting the Odes.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Its arguments are fresh and original, and the vigor of its prose is dazzling.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖人奉天伐暴而即有事於遷都此可見其克
君也盖伐暴畢而遷都繼舉所以為安民計也
聖人以之其克君也何如哉此詩言文王遷豐
之事意謂維我文王一德之敬止布而為遹求
厥寧之心上帝於是乎聿懷一德之小心運而
為遹觀厥成之念皇天於是乎黙眷啓之詢仇
也則得專征伐昭然大命之有歸啓之去暴也
則載授鈇鉞居然成命之誕膺天命既受天討
===
斯行聲罪於倡亂之崇加兵於肆釁之國是伐
是肆鋤強梗於三旬之餘武功丕著於當時是
絶是忽除讒邪於一掃之後罪人斯得於授首
崇侯既伐則民歸日衆舊邑不能以盡容人心
咸歸則國勢浸盛新都不容於不作于焉相厥
山川而作邑于豐城池廟寢殆將煥剸度於一
新于焉審其向背而建都于豐朝市祖社殆將
鼎規模於肇造舉國生靈盡携而東下民於此
乎王勃勃乎興王之氣象矣五廟鍾虡悉卷而
punctuated: 聖人奉天伐暴，而即有事於遷都，此可見其克君也。盖伐暴畢而遷都繼舉，所以為安民計也。聖人以之，其克君也何如哉！此詩言文王遷豐之事，意謂維我文王，一德之敬止，布而為遹求厥寧之心，上帝於是乎聿懷；一德之小心，運而為遹觀厥成之念，皇天於是乎黙眷。啓之詢仇也，則得專征伐，昭然大命之有歸；啓之去暴也，則載授鈇鉞，居然成命之誕膺。天命既受，天討斯行。聲罪於倡亂之崇，加兵於肆釁之國，是伐是肆，鋤強梗於三旬之餘，武功丕著於當時；是絶是忽，除讒邪於一掃之後，罪人斯得於授首。崇侯既伐，則民歸日衆，舊邑不能以盡容；人心咸歸，則國勢浸盛，新都不容於不作。于焉相厥山川，而作邑于豐，城池廟寢殆將煥剸度於一新；于焉審其向背，而建都于豐，朝市祖社殆將鼎規模於肇造。舉國生靈盡携而東，下民於此乎王，勃勃乎興王之氣象矣！五廟鍾虡悉卷而
translation_en:
The sage obeyed Heaven in attacking a tyrant and immediately undertook the relocation of his capital. Here we can see his competence as a ruler. For when the campaign against tyranny was finished, the relocation followed: this was his plan for bringing peace to the people. The sage acted upon this—how capable a ruler he was! This ode recounts King Wen’s relocation to Feng. Its meaning is that our King Wen’s reverence, grounded in his undivided virtue, extended into a determination to seek peace for his people; the Lord on High therefore cherished him. His cautious attentiveness, grounded in that same virtue, worked itself into a resolve to see his undertaking completed; August Heaven therefore watched over him in silence. Heaven prompted him to consult his allies, and he obtained authority to undertake punitive campaigns on his own: it was manifest where the great Mandate had come to rest. Heaven prompted him to eliminate tyranny and bestowed upon him the axes of military authority: he thus fully received the established Mandate. Having received Heaven’s Mandate, he carried out Heaven’s punishment.

He proclaimed the offenses of Chong, which had instigated disorder, and brought arms against the state that wantonly provoked conflict. He attacked and assailed it, rooting out the powerful and recalcitrant in a little over thirty days; his martial achievement shone forth in his age. He cut off and destroyed it, sweeping away the slanderous and wicked at a stroke; the guilty man was brought to account and surrendered his head. Once the lord of Chong had been attacked, the people came over in increasing numbers each day, and the old settlement could no longer accommodate them all. As all hearts turned to him, the state’s strength steadily grew, and a new capital had to be built. Thereupon he surveyed the mountains and rivers and established a settlement at Feng. Its walls, moats, temples, and residential halls would display a wholly renewed design [?]. Thereupon he examined the site’s orientation and established his capital at Feng. Its court, markets, ancestral temples, and altars of the soil would establish a grand pattern at their founding [?]. He led the entire population of the realm eastward, and there the common people acknowledged him as king: how vigorous was the rising royal enterprise! The bells and bell stands of the five ancestral temples were all packed up and …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
行萬邦於此乎向駸駸乎一統之規模矣夫然
豈不為克君乎吾見崇侯伐而豐邑成非但拓
不拔之鴻基也而所以求厥寧者有其所文王
父母斯民信乎招徠之有道矣尚何有弗克耶
豐邑成而人心繫非但開無前之偉績也而所
以觀厥成者有其漸文王君臨億兆誠哉撫綏
之有方矣尚何有或斁耶吁方奉命以除暴而
即遷都以安民文王之克君如此詩人述而美
之宜矣大抵天以安民為心而文王乃安民之
===
===
主故伐崇雖所以奉天亦所以安民遷豐雖所
以安民亦所以奉天要皆有不容已者固非逞
私憤利土地之為也此所以重光乎先世繼述
之託大裕乎後世集統之事至武王而天下歸
周皇王維辟良有以哉後世若蠶食六國既非
本於奉天營朝宮渭南亦非本於安民其於君
道之得失較然矣噫周以八百秦以二世不為
無所自云
薄言震之莫不震疊懷柔百神及河喬嶽
punctuated:
行，萬邦於此乎向，駸駸乎一統之規模矣。夫然，豈不為克君乎？吾見崇侯伐而豐邑成，非但拓不拔之鴻基也，而所以求厥寧者有其所。文王父母斯民，信乎招徠之有道矣，尚何有弗克耶？豐邑成而人心繫，非但開無前之偉績也，而所以觀厥成者有其漸。文王君臨億兆，誠哉撫綏之有方矣，尚何有或斁耶？吁！方奉命以除暴，而即遷都以安民，文王之克君如此，詩人述而美之宜矣。大抵天以安民為心，而文王乃安民之主，故伐崇雖所以奉天，亦所以安民；遷豐雖所以安民，亦所以奉天。要皆有不容已者，固非逞私憤、利土地之為也。此所以重光乎先世繼述之託，大裕乎後世集統之事。至武王而天下歸周，皇王維辟，良有以哉！後世若蠶食六國，既非本於奉天；營朝宮渭南，亦非本於安民。其於君道之得失較然矣。噫！周以八百，秦以二世，不為無所自云。

薄言震之，莫不震疊。懷柔百神，及河喬嶽。
translation_en:
…were taken along, and the myriad states turned toward him: the framework of a unified realm was rapidly taking shape. Was this not truly fulfilling the role of ruler? I observe that when the Marquis of Chong had been defeated and the settlement at Feng completed, this established more than an unshakable foundation for greatness: it also provided a place in which the people could seek peace. King Wen acted as father and mother to these people. Truly, he knew how to draw them to him. How could there have been any failure to fulfill his role? When Feng was completed and the people’s hearts were bound to him, this inaugurated more than an unprecedented achievement: it also furnished successive stages through which its completion could be witnessed. King Wen ruled over the countless multitudes. Truly, he knew how to comfort and pacify them. How could there have been any weariness? Ah! Having obeyed the mandate to eliminate violence, he immediately moved the capital to bring peace to the people. Such was King Wen’s fulfillment of his role as ruler; fitting indeed that the poet should recount and praise it.

Heaven’s purpose is, broadly speaking, to bring peace to the people, and King Wen was precisely the ruler who brought them peace. Thus, although attacking Chong served Heaven, it also brought peace to the people; although moving to Feng brought peace to the people, it also served Heaven. In essence, both were actions that could not be left undone. They certainly did not arise from venting private anger or coveting territory. This is why he added renewed glory to the charge inherited from his ancestors to carry on their work, and amply prepared the undertaking of his successors in completing the dynasty’s unification. When King Wu’s time came, all under Heaven submitted to Zhou. “The august king is indeed the sovereign”—there was good reason for this! In later ages, the piecemeal annexation of the six states was not grounded in service to Heaven; nor was the construction of the imperial palace south of the Wei River grounded in bringing peace to the people. Success and failure in the way of rulership are clearly apparent here. Alas! That Zhou lasted eight hundred years and Qin only two generations was not without its causes.

“He exerted his awe-inspiring might upon them; none failed to tremble and submit. He conciliated the hundred spirits, including those of the Yellow River and the lofty peaks.”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
陳策
同考試官教諭方批此作以朝會祭告作主
意深得本旨且議論雋永筆力清勁飽經中得
此誠奇才也健羨健羨
同考試官學正陳批頌題似易實難作者
多窘澁滯晦此篇體認明白發揮殆盡故録
考試官教諭姜批辭理俱優傑作也
考試官教諭張批作頌題有理致
朝羣后而無不服祭羣神而無不格天眷周王
===
然也盖巡守而朝會祭告有天下者之首務也
周王一舉而人神兩受其職謂非天眷之有在
乎此巡守而朝會祭告之樂歌也意謂我周王
膺上天右序之命舉一代巡守之典則所以致
驗於人神者當何如耶是故以朝會言之獻琛
效贄於方岳諸侯非一職也今則正朔一之制
度同之略示警省於衆志俾知姬運方亨而耳
目為之一新政令考之風俗齊之薄示震動於
人心俾知曆數有在而觀聽為之一改但見庶
punctuated:
陳策

同考試官教諭方批：此作以朝會祭告作主意，深得本旨，且議論雋永，筆力清勁。飽經中得此，誠奇才也。健羨，健羨！

同考試官學正陳批：頌題似易實難，作者多窘澁滯晦。此篇體認明白，發揮殆盡，故録。

考試官教諭姜批：辭理俱優，傑作也。

考試官教諭張批：作頌題，有理致。

朝羣后而無不服，祭羣神而無不格，天眷周王然也。盖巡守而朝會祭告，有天下者之首務也。周王一舉而人神兩受其職，謂非天眷之有在乎？此巡守而朝會祭告之樂歌也。意謂我周王膺上天右序之命，舉一代巡守之典，則所以致驗於人神者當何如耶？是故以朝會言之，獻琛效贄於方岳，諸侯非一職也。今則正朔一之，制度同之，略示警省於衆志，俾知姬運方亨，而耳目為之一新；政令考之，風俗齊之，薄示震動於人心，俾知曆數有在，而觀聽為之一改。但見庶
translation_en:
Chen Ce 陳策

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: This composition takes audiences with the feudal lords and sacrificial announcements as its central theme, thoroughly grasping the passage’s essential meaning. Its arguments have enduring richness, and its writing is lucid and vigorous. To find this among those steeped in the Classics [?]—truly an extraordinary talent! How admirable, how admirable!

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Topics from the Hymns seem easy but are actually difficult. Writers often become constrained, awkward, labored, and obscure. This essay understands the subject clearly and develops its meaning almost exhaustively; hence its inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Excellent in both expression and reasoning—a masterwork.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: A treatment of a Hymns topic that possesses coherence and depth of reasoning.

He holds audience with the assembled lords, and none fails to submit; he sacrifices to the assembled spirits, and none fails to come. Heaven’s favor toward the king of Zhou makes this so. For a ruler who possesses all under Heaven, conducting inspection tours, holding audiences, and making sacrificial announcements are foremost duties. Through a single undertaking, the king of Zhou brings both men and spirits to receive their proper offices. Can one say that Heaven’s favor has no particular object?
