Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Have you perhaps devoted yourself to the study of writing and mastered its methods? How thoroughly you understand its essentials!

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張批書法隨世異制而揮
染因人異趣要之取其心畫之正不徒藝焉而
已此策能悉之用録以示夫故意取妍者
聖賢之開物成務莫大乎字之作聖賢之
作字代繩一根乎心之理盖文非字則弗
傳字非理則無本故作文而有其字則動
於此而應於彼自有以成天下之務作字
而根於理則理無窮而字無窮自足以資
萬世之用小則可以潤乎身大則可以濟
===
乎世是字學之所關也豈淺淺哉請因明
問而陳之自夫太極既判之初兩儀始奠
之候言其俗則顓蒙而質朴之未散言其
政則結繩而號令之未施于時則字未之
有也迨夫河出圖洛出書伏羲因之以畫
卦而字之點畫於是乎胚胎矣然八卦雖
畫而文猶未著蒼頡繼之則據理以造書
而聲音以諧形體以正字於是乎大明矣
由是經以之傳道以之載史以之而不失
punctuated:
考試官教諭張批：書法隨世異制，而揮染因人異趣。要之，取其心畫之正，不徒藝焉而已。此策能悉之，用録以示夫故意取妍者。
聖賢之開物成務，莫大乎字之作。聖賢之作字代繩，一根乎心之理。盖文非字則弗傳，字非理則無本。故作文而有其字，則動於此而應於彼，自有以成天下之務；作字而根於理，則理無窮而字無窮，自足以資萬世之用。小則可以潤乎身，大則可以濟乎世。是字學之所關也，豈淺淺哉？請因明問而陳之。
自夫太極既判之初，兩儀始奠之候，言其俗，則顓蒙而質朴之未散；言其政，則結繩而號令之未施。于時則字未之有也。迨夫河出圖，洛出書，伏羲因之以畫卦，而字之點畫於是乎胚胎矣。然八卦雖畫，而文猶未著。蒼頡繼之，則據理以造書，而聲音以諧，形體以正，字於是乎大明矣。由是經以之傳，道以之載，史以之而不失
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The forms of calligraphy change with the age, and the handling of brush and ink varies with each person's inclinations. What matters, ultimately, is the rectitude of these delineations of the heart, rather than artistic skill alone. This policy essay fully explains this point. It is therefore selected for inclusion to instruct those who deliberately strive for prettiness.
Of all the ways in which sages and worthies have brought understanding to things and accomplished affairs, none is greater than the creation of written characters. When sages and worthies created characters to replace knotted cords, they rooted them entirely in the principle inherent in the heart. For compositions cannot be transmitted without characters, and characters have no foundation without principle. Thus, when compositions are made and characters are available for them, an impulse here elicits a response there, naturally providing the means to accomplish the world's affairs. When characters are created with their roots in principle, principle is inexhaustible and so too are characters, naturally sufficing to serve the needs of all generations. On a small scale, they can refine one's person; on a large scale, they can benefit the world. Such are the concerns of the study of characters: how could they be trivial? Allow me to set them forth in response to your illuminating question.
At the beginning, when the Supreme Ultimate had first divided and the Two Modes of yin and yang had just become established, customs were simple and unknowing, their original plainness still intact; government employed knotted cords, and commands had yet to be issued. At that time, written characters did not yet exist. Then the Yellow River brought forth the Chart, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing. Fuxi drew upon these to draw the trigrams, and the dots and strokes of characters were thereby conceived. Yet although the Eight Trigrams had been drawn, writing had not yet become manifest. Cangjie followed him, creating writing on the basis of principle, harmonizing its sounds and setting its forms aright. Written characters thus became fully manifest. Hence the classics were transmitted through them, the Way was conveyed through them, and through them the histories did not lose …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其書事以之而不遺其記百官之政賴此
以舉萬民之情賴此以通上而堯舜禹湯
文武之爲君詞命賴此以渙頒下而皐陶
伊傅周召之爲臣王命賴此以出納是則
字之用於天下也不其大歟及周嗣世宣
王中興而史籀有大篆之作顧篆書之體
雖創於一時而科斗之文猶存乎自古奈
之何世入於秦吾道之厄燔燒之禍既熾
科斗之文不傳李斯變大篆而爲小篆斯
===
之罪不容誅也然而小篆之所存猶有蒼
史之遺意豈可以其人而遂泯其善歟程
邈變小篆而爲隸書邈之隸亦非優也然
而秦人厭篆之繁難喜隸之省經豈非滅
詩書而專任吏之過歟漢襲秦弊欲縮之
以簡便未免失之疎而西京之教寂無所
聞者有自來也晉矯漢失欲華之以姿媚
不免失之縱而清談之風習以成俗者有
由然也是皆世與道違字與時變無足議
punctuated: 其書，事以之而不遺其記。百官之政賴此以舉，萬民之情賴此以通。上而堯舜禹湯文武之爲君，詞命賴此以渙頒；下而皐陶伊傅周召之爲臣，王命賴此以出納。是則字之用於天下也，不其大歟？及周嗣世，宣王中興，而史籀有大篆之作。顧篆書之體雖創於一時，而科斗之文猶存乎自古。奈之何世入於秦，吾道之厄，燔燒之禍既熾，科斗之文不傳！李斯變大篆而爲小篆，斯之罪不容誅也。然而小篆之所存，猶有蒼史之遺意，豈可以其人而遂泯其善歟？程邈變小篆而爲隸書，邈之隸亦非優也。然而秦人厭篆之繁難，喜隸之省經，豈非滅《詩》《書》而專任吏之過歟？漢襲秦弊，欲縮之以簡便，未免失之疎，而西京之教寂無所聞者，有自來也。晉矯漢失，欲華之以姿媚，不免失之縱，而清談之風習以成俗者，有由然也。是皆世與道違，字與時變，無足議
translation_en:
…their written accounts, and events thereby do not go unrecorded. The administration of the hundred officials depends upon writing to be carried out, and the sentiments of the myriad people depend upon it to be communicated. Above, rulers such as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu relied upon it to promulgate their pronouncements far and wide; below, ministers such as Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao relied upon it to transmit royal commands. Is not the usefulness of writing throughout the world indeed great?

When the Zhou succeeded to rule, and King Xuan brought about a restoration, Scribe Zhou devised the large-seal script. Yet although the form of seal script was created at a particular time, tadpole writing had survived from antiquity. Alas, when the age passed into Qin, our Way suffered calamity: the disaster of book burning raged, and tadpole writing ceased to be transmitted! Li Si transformed large-seal into small-seal script; even execution could not atone for his crime. Nevertheless, what survives in small-seal script still preserves something of the legacy of the scribe Cang Jie. How could we obliterate its merits simply because of the man who made it?

Cheng Miao transformed small-seal script into clerical script; Miao’s clerical script was likewise no improvement. Yet the people of Qin disliked the complexity and difficulty of seal script and delighted in the economy of clerical script [?]. Was this not the fault of destroying the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents and relying exclusively upon administrative clerks? The Han inherited the abuses of Qin and sought to abbreviate writing for simplicity and convenience, but could not avoid the fault of carelessness. Thus there was a longstanding cause for the utter absence of any reputation for teaching in the Western Han. The Jin sought to correct the failings of the Han and to embellish writing with graceful charm, but could not avoid the fault of unrestrained freedom. Thus there was a reason why the fashion for Pure Conversation became an established custom. In all these cases, the age departed from the Way, and writing changed with the times; there is nothing worth discussing…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也若夫王次中爲楷書此楷之始魏鍾胡
爲行書此行之始張芝承杜崔諸人之工
而愈妙於草書此草書之始蔡邕覩皇都
匠人之巧而刻意於飛白此飛白之始然
要其歸則之數體者皆適於述作之用究
其本則楷與行者尤切於日用之常學之
者其可不知所先務哉夫字也者原於心
之理發於心之用得之則令聞廣譽施於
身廓之則格君輔國鳴於世曷不觀諸古
===
人乎張伯英得執筆之五妙而草聖之名
見稱於當世王逸少得永字之八法而蘭
亭之書加重於貞觀宓子賤能掣肘善書
正其言而使之言而魯君遂爲之感悟非
格君之善者乎柳公權謂用筆在心心正
則筆正而憲宗即爲之改容非諷諫之良
者乎之數子者以字學而成天下之事也
不其大歟雖然亦有要矣善乎程子曰某
作字時甚敬非要字好即此是學夫敬也
punctuated:
也。若夫王次中爲楷書，此楷之始；魏鍾胡爲行書，此行之始；張芝承杜崔諸人之工，而愈妙於草書，此草書之始；蔡邕覩皇都匠人之巧，而刻意於飛白，此飛白之始。然要其歸，則之數體者皆適於述作之用；究其本，則楷與行者尤切於日用之常。學之者，其可不知所先務哉？夫字也者，原於心之理，發於心之用。得之則令聞廣譽施於身，廓之則格君輔國鳴於世。曷不觀諸古人乎？
張伯英得執筆之五妙，而草聖之名見稱於當世；王逸少得永字之八法，而蘭亭之書加重於貞觀。宓子賤能掣肘善書，正其言而使之言，而魯君遂爲之感悟，非格君之善者乎？柳公權謂用筆在心，心正則筆正，而憲宗即爲之改容，非諷諫之良者乎？之數子者，以字學而成天下之事也，不其大歟？雖然，亦有要矣。善乎程子曰：「某作字時甚敬，非要字好，即此是學。」夫敬也
translation_en:
…indeed. As for Wang Cizhong’s creation of regular script, this was the beginning of regular script; Zhong and Hu of Wei created running script, marking its beginning; Zhang Zhi inherited the skill of Du, Cui, and others and achieved still greater subtlety in cursive script—this was the beginning of cursive script; Cai Yong observed the ingenuity of craftsmen in the imperial capital and devoted himself to developing “flying white” script—this was its beginning. Yet, considering their ultimate purpose, these several forms all serve the needs of written composition; examining their fundamentals, regular and running scripts are especially pertinent to everyday use. Can those who study them fail to know what they should attend to first? Writing originates in the principles of the mind and issues from its activity. Mastering it brings a fine reputation and widespread renown to oneself; extending it enables one to rectify the ruler and assist the state, winning distinction in the world. Why not look to the ancients?
Zhang Boying mastered the five subtleties of holding the brush and was acclaimed in his own day as the “Sage of Cursive Script.” Wang Yishao mastered the eight methods embodied in the character yong 永, and his Orchid Pavilion calligraphy gained still greater esteem during the Zhenguan reign. Mi Zijian was able to tug at the elbows of those skilled in writing, rectify their words, and cause them to speak [?], so that the ruler of Lu was moved to understanding. Was this not an excellent instance of rectifying a ruler? Liu Gongquan said that using the brush depends upon the mind: when the mind is upright, the brush is upright. Xianzong immediately changed his expression. Was this not a fine instance of indirect remonstrance? These men used the study of writing to accomplish affairs in the world. Was this not something great? Nevertheless, there is also an essential point. Well did Master Cheng say: “When I write characters, I am deeply reverent. It is not that I seek fine handwriting; this itself is learning.” Now, reverence…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者所以求放心明義理而爲學之所當先
也使學字者誠能閑邪以存其敬持敬以
養其心慾無不去而體以之全理無不窮
而知以之致將見投筆以施於字不求其
工而自工因字而見於爲不求其應而自
應即吾前所謂周天下之用而成天下之
事者不過此心之轉移耳愚也於字願學
而未能譬之射焉將執此以爲的不識執
事然之否也
===
第四問
李高
同考試官訓導鄭 批漢唐財用嬴縮之由
今日理財處置之宜條答亹亹卓有定見此豈但務於窮
經者乎
考試官教諭姜 批 理財正
今日要務非識時務者不能有此畫籌
考試官教諭張 批 財賦一策正欲觀士
子酌古準今有用之學場中敷演問目了
punctuated:
者，所以求放心、明義理，而爲學之所當先也。使學字者誠能閑邪以存其敬，持敬以養其心，慾無不去而體以之全，理無不窮而知以之致，將見投筆以施於字，不求其工而自工；因字而見於爲，不求其應而自應。即吾前所謂周天下之用而成天下之事者，不過此心之轉移耳。愚也於字願學而未能，譬之射焉，將執此以爲的，不識執事然之否也？

第四問
李高

同考試官訓導鄭批：「漢唐財用嬴縮之由，今日理財處置之宜，條答亹亹，卓有定見。此豈但務於窮經者乎？」

考試官教諭姜批：「理財，正今日要務，非識時務者不能有此畫籌。」

考試官教諭張批：「財賦一策，正欲觀士子酌古準今有用之學。場中敷演問目，了
translation_en:
…is the means of recovering the wayward mind and clarifying moral principles, and must therefore come first in learning. If those who study calligraphy can truly ward off evil to preserve their reverence, and maintain reverence to nurture their minds, they will eliminate every desire and thereby preserve the wholeness of their fundamental nature; they will exhaustively investigate every principle and thereby bring their knowledge to its fullest extent. Then, when they take up the brush [?] and apply themselves to writing, their calligraphy will become accomplished without their seeking accomplishment. When this manifests itself in action through their calligraphy, their actions will accord with circumstances without their seeking such accord. What I spoke of earlier—meeting all the world’s practical needs and accomplishing its affairs—is nothing more than the workings of this mind. As for myself, I wish to study calligraphy but have not yet mastered it. To draw an analogy with archery, I intend to take this as my target. I do not know whether you, sir, approve.

Fourth Question
Li Gao

Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor, comments: “On the reasons for surpluses and shortfalls in the finances of the Han and Tang, and on appropriate measures for managing finances today, he responds point by point with sustained diligence and displays remarkably firm judgments. Can this be someone who merely devotes himself to exhaustive study of the Classics?”

Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Managing finances is precisely an urgent task today. Only someone who understands the affairs of the time could devise such plans.”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
無完言此策區處時宜切當非特取其記憶
也錄之以備司
國計者之一畫
為國莫要於理財理財莫先於節用盖財
用者生人之本有國之常經不可一日而
無者也故易載裒多益寡書稱懋遷有無
然非有以節之則所謂取之盡錙銖用之
如泥沙雖盡括天下之所出恐亦有不足
於國之用者此為國者固以理財為要而
===
理財又以節用為先誠萬世不易之定論
也理財之說古今談之盡矣愚不能復有
說也請借明問所舉漢唐之事而紬繹以
對夫漢高之興當始皇頭會箕斂之後唐
室之起承煬帝窮奢極侈之餘故文帝太
宗之紹統宜乎國用不足矣然文帝則躬
脩節儉勸課農桑宫室苑囿車騎服御無
所增益有不便輒弛以利民是其務為節
用在漢之諸君未能或之先也太宗則去
punctuated:
無完言。此策區處時宜切當，非特取其記憶也。錄之以備司國計者之一畫。

為國莫要於理財，理財莫先於節用。盖財用者，生人之本，有國之常經，不可一日而無者也。故《易》載「裒多益寡」，《書》稱「懋遷有無」。然非有以節之，則所謂「取之盡錙銖，用之如泥沙」，雖盡括天下之所出，恐亦有不足於國之用者。此為國者固以理財為要，而理財又以節用為先，誠萬世不易之定論也。理財之說，古今談之盡矣，愚不能復有說也。請借明問所舉漢唐之事，而紬繹以對。夫漢高之興，當始皇頭會箕斂之後；唐室之起，承煬帝窮奢極侈之餘。故文帝、太宗之紹統，宜乎國用不足矣。然文帝則躬脩節儉，勸課農桑，宫室苑囿、車騎服御，無所增益；有不便，輒弛以利民。是其務為節用，在漢之諸君，未能或之先也。太宗則去
translation_en:
…not a single complete statement. This policy essay proposes measures that are appropriate to present circumstances; it was selected for more than the candidate’s powers of recall. It is recorded here to furnish those responsible for the state’s finances with a possible course of action.

In governing a state, nothing is more essential than managing its finances; in managing finances, nothing takes precedence over restraining expenditure. Financial resources are the foundation of the people’s livelihood and a constant necessity of state: they cannot be dispensed with for even a day. Thus the Book of Changes records, “Reduce what is abundant and augment what is scarce,” and the Book of Documents speaks of “diligently exchanging what one has for what one lacks.” Yet without measures to restrain expenditure, there will be what is called “exacting every last fraction, then spending it like mud and sand.” Even if everything produced under Heaven were gathered in, I fear it would still fall short of the state’s needs. Hence managing finances is indeed essential to governing a state, while restraining expenditure takes precedence in managing finances. This is truly a settled principle that will remain unchanged for ten thousand generations.

The principles of financial management have been exhaustively discussed, in antiquity and today. In my humble view, I can add nothing further. Allow me instead to draw out the implications of the events of the Han and Tang cited in your illuminating question and offer my reply. The rise of Gaozu of Han followed the First Emperor’s exactions, assessed by counting heads and collected by the basketful; the rise of the Tang ruling house came in the aftermath of Emperor Yang’s utmost extravagance and luxury. Thus, when Emperor Wen and Taizong respectively succeeded to the throne, it was only to be expected that state funds would be insufficient. Yet Emperor Wen personally practiced frugality and encouraged and supervised agriculture and sericulture. He made no additions to his palaces, parks, carriages, horses, clothing, or personal furnishings. Whenever a measure burdened the people, he relaxed it for their benefit. Such was his dedication to restraining expenditure that none of the Han rulers could surpass him. Taizong, for his part, eliminated…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
奢省費輕徭薄賦選用廉吏使民衣食有
餘自不爲盜是其恭儉之政在唐之諸君
亦未有與之竝也夫用節則費省費省則
國富雖寬恤之詔屢下征榷之令不行亦
何害其國用之有餘乎至於武帝德宗承
數世之積累固宜國用有餘也然武帝則
外事四夷内興工役故常賦不足而榷酒
酤筭舟車造緡錢之法興矣德宗則不能
推誠待物尊賢使能故兩河用兵月費百
===
===
萬府庫之積不支數月而稅間架除陌錢
括商錢之法起矣即是而觀則其盈虛消
息之間夫豈專在於下哉我
太祖有天下取民之制一倣于古田賦之外惟
有商稅凡漢唐苛刻之政一切罷去
神謀遠慮所以惠澤斯民培養元氣者至矣既
而永樂間歲之所入不足所出故一時權
宜俯從臣下之請乃有戸口食鹽有坑冶
採鑄有鈔關設置有竹木榷取初猶暫行
punctuated:
奢、省費、輕徭、薄賦，選用廉吏，使民衣食有餘，自不爲盜。是其恭儉之政，在唐之諸君，亦未有與之竝也。夫用節則費省，費省則國富，雖寬恤之詔屢下，征榷之令不行，亦何害其國用之有餘乎？至於武帝、德宗，承數世之積累，固宜國用有餘也。然武帝則外事四夷，内興工役，故常賦不足，而榷酒酤、筭舟車、造緡錢之法興矣。德宗則不能推誠待物，尊賢使能，故兩河用兵，月費百萬，府庫之積不支數月，而稅間架、除陌錢、括商錢之法起矣。即是而觀，則其盈虛消息之間，夫豈專在於下哉？
我太祖有天下，取民之制，一倣于古。田賦之外，惟有商稅，凡漢唐苛刻之政，一切罷去。神謀遠慮，所以惠澤斯民、培養元氣者至矣。既而永樂間，歲之所入不足所出，故一時權宜，俯從臣下之請，乃有戸口食鹽，有坑冶採鑄，有鈔關設置，有竹木榷取，初猶暫行。
translation_en:
…curbed extravagance, reduced expenditure, lightened labor service, and lowered taxes. He selected incorrupt officials for service, ensuring that the people had ample clothing and food and therefore naturally refrained from theft. Among the rulers of the Tang, none equaled his government in reverence and frugality. When spending is restrained, expenses diminish; when expenses diminish, the state grows wealthy. Even if edicts granting relief are repeatedly issued and orders imposing levies and monopolies are not implemented, how could this prevent a surplus in state finances? As for Emperor Wu of the Han and Emperor Dezong of the Tang, they inherited the accumulations of several generations, so their resources should certainly have been more than sufficient. Yet Emperor Wu campaigned abroad against the peoples of the four quarters and undertook construction projects at home. Ordinary tax revenues consequently proved insufficient, and measures were introduced to monopolize liquor sales, tax boats and carts, and mint cash [?]. Dezong could not treat others with genuine sincerity, honor the worthy, or employ the capable. Consequently, military operations in the Lianghe region cost a million each month, and the treasury’s reserves could not sustain even several months. Thus arose taxes assessed on the bays of buildings, transaction taxes on cash payments, and the seizure of merchants’ funds. Viewed in this light, could the fullness or depletion, growth or decline of state resources depend solely on those below?
When our Taizu gained All under Heaven, he modeled his system of levies upon the people entirely on antiquity. Apart from the land tax, there were only commercial taxes; all the harsh fiscal measures of the Han and Tang were abolished. His sagacious planning and far-reaching foresight were consummate in bestowing benefits upon the people and nurturing the fundamental vitality of the realm. Later, during the Yongle reign, annual receipts fell short of expenditure. As a temporary expedient, the emperor condescended to accept his ministers’ requests. Thereupon came household salt assessments, mining and the casting of metal, the establishment of paper-money customs stations, and monopoly levies on bamboo and timber. At first these were still implemented only temporarily…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今著爲令盖立法之初雖未爲不善而今
之奉行者恐未肯悉體
朝廷本意也則
今日之理財者可不思所以寬恤之哉盖地
力之生物有大數人力之成物有大限取
之有度用之有節則常足取之無度用之
無節則常不足此所以必欲節用以止財
之流不可横斂以傷財之源也宋之名賢
若蘇轍有曰所謂豐財者非求財而益之
===
也去事之所以害財者而已矣事之害財
者三曰冗吏曰冗兵曰冗費三冗既去天
下之財得以日生而無害是亦豈非節用
之意哉盖斜封墨敕額外羡增所謂冗吏
也列屯坐食老弱不練所謂冗兵也横恩
濫賜之溢出脩飾營造之泛興禱祀游玩
之紛舉所謂冗費也三者之中冗費爲甚
誠能節用則不耗財於無益之事不費財
於無用之地不施財於無功之人而國用
punctuated:
今著爲令。盖立法之初，雖未爲不善，而今之奉行者，恐未肯悉體朝廷本意也。則今日之理財者，可不思所以寬恤之哉？盖地力之生物有大數，人力之成物有大限。取之有度，用之有節，則常足；取之無度，用之無節，則常不足。此所以必欲節用以止財之流，不可横斂以傷財之源也。
宋之名賢若蘇轍有曰：「所謂豐財者，非求財而益之也，去事之所以害財者而已矣。事之害財者三：曰冗吏，曰冗兵，曰冗費。三冗既去，天下之財得以日生而無害。」是亦豈非節用之意哉？盖斜封墨敕，額外羡增，所謂冗吏也；列屯坐食，老弱不練，所謂冗兵也；横恩濫賜之溢出，脩飾營造之泛興，禱祀游玩之紛舉，所謂冗費也。三者之中，冗費爲甚。誠能節用，則不耗財於無益之事，不費財於無用之地，不施財於無功之人，而國用
translation_en:
…now they have been established as standing regulations. Although these measures were not ill-conceived when first instituted, those who administer them today may be unwilling to give full consideration to the court’s original intentions. Can those who manage public finances today, then, fail to consider how to ease the people’s burdens and bring them relief? The earth’s capacity to produce things has an overall limit, and human labor’s capacity to make things has an overall limit. If resources are taken in due measure and used with restraint, there will always be enough; if they are taken without measure and used without restraint, there will never be enough. This is why expenditure must be restrained to check the outflow of wealth, and why excessive exactions must not be allowed to damage its source.
Among the renowned worthies of the Song, Su Zhe said: “What is called enriching the public finances does not mean seeking wealth and adding to it. It means only removing those things that damage it. Three things damage wealth: redundant officials, redundant troops, and redundant expenditure. Once these three redundancies are removed, the wealth of the realm can grow daily without harm.” Is this not also the meaning of restraint in expenditure? Appointments made through irregular, slant-sealed documents and edicts in black ink, and increases beyond the authorized establishment, constitute what is called redundant officialdom. Troops stationed in garrisons who draw rations while idle, the old and weak who receive no training, constitute what are called redundant troops. An overflow of arbitrary favors and indiscriminate grants, the unchecked undertaking of embellishment and construction, and the frequent staging of prayers, sacrifices, excursions, and amusements constitute what is called redundant expenditure. Of these three, redundant expenditure is the gravest. If expenditure can truly be restrained, wealth will not be squandered on unprofitable undertakings, spent where it serves no purpose, or bestowed on people who have rendered no service; and the resources for the state’s needs…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之充自足以却虜禦戎矣尚何有於充國孔
明之患哉若舍此而別求富國足用之術則
不過桑弘羊蠹國壞民之爲固非有神運
天雨之法也愚也繩樞草舍之人井蛙甕
雞之見固不知所謂理財亦不知所謂國
計所知者紙上陳言易與大學而已不曰
節以制度不傷財不害民乎又不曰生財
有大道乎是故始終爲執事陳之惟執事
矜其愚恕其狂斐進而教之幸也
===
第五問
譚才養
同考試官教諭方批不意書生中有習知
兵事如吾子者尚囊括底蘊以俟他日鎖鑰
北門
同考試官學正陳批條答無遺末復歸重得
人亦確論也經生如此其文事武備者耶
考試官教諭姜批善答足見學識
考試官教諭張批事實不遺且有斷制
punctuated:
之充，自足以却虜禦戎矣，尚何有於充國、孔明之患哉？若舍此而別求富國足用之術，則不過桑弘羊蠹國壞民之爲，固非有神運天雨之法也。愚也，繩樞草舍之人，井蛙甕雞之見，固不知所謂理財，亦不知所謂國計。所知者，紙上陳言，《易》與《大學》而已。不曰「節以制度，不傷財，不害民」乎？又不曰「生財有大道」乎？是故始終爲執事陳之，惟執事矜其愚，恕其狂斐，進而教之，幸也。

第五問
譚才養

同考試官教諭方批：「不意書生中有習知兵事如吾子者，尚囊括底蘊，以俟他日鎖鑰北門。」

同考試官學正陳批：「條答無遺，末復歸重得人，亦確論也。經生如此，其文事武備者耶？」

考試官教諭姜批：「善答，足見學識。」

考試官教諭張批：「事實不遺，且有斷制。」
translation_en:
…the abundance of state resources would itself suffice to repel the invaders and resist hostile peoples. What grounds would remain for the anxieties of Chongguo and Kongming? If one abandons this and seeks some other technique for enriching the state and ensuring sufficient resources, it would amount to nothing more than Sang Hongyang’s practices of consuming the state’s wealth and ruining the people. There is certainly no method by which spirits transport wealth or Heaven rains it down.

I am a foolish man living in a thatched dwelling with rope-hinged doors, whose outlook is that of a frog in a well or a chicken in a jar. I certainly do not understand what is called managing wealth, nor what is called state finance. All I know are old sayings on paper—the Book of Changes and the Great Learning, nothing more. Does the former not say, “Regulate expenditure through institutions and measures, without damaging wealth or harming the people”? And does the latter not say, “There is a great way to produce wealth”? Thus I have set these principles before you throughout. I would count myself fortunate if you would take pity on my ignorance, forgive my rash and ill-considered words, and admit me to receive your instruction.

Fifth Question
Tan Caiyang

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “I did not expect to find among scholars one as well versed in military affairs as you. May you fully master their underlying principles, awaiting the day when you serve as the lock and key of the northern gate.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He answers point by point, omitting nothing, and at the end returns to placing primary importance on obtaining the right men. This too is a sound judgment. Is a student of the Classics such as this one equipped for both civil affairs and military preparedness?”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “An excellent answer, amply demonstrating learning and discernment.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “He omits none of the facts and precedents, and also exercises decisive judgment.”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知安危之相為倚伏則
國家於兵法當振舉於平時知文武之相為
倚用則學者於兵法當備陳於
今日蓋乆安而危不防則危必作隆文而武
弗繼則武必衰皆非保邦長治之良圖文
武並行不悖之全策也此其所以未事之
先當求夫將為有能之將兵為有制之兵
而臨事之日庶幾將得士心兵識將意近
足以保安天下遠足以流芳後世若漢之
===
諸葛宋之名將乃可以語此而我
國朝選將材定武舉則又安不忘危文不廢
武超百王而獨邁者政不必以兵為諱也
執事發策首逮於此其亦慮關廟廊而憂
先天下者乎愚請復其萬一兵果可言耶
古人有曰先王耀德不觀兵吾不得而知
也兵果不可言耶古人又曰兵者生民之
大本吾亦不得而知也要之治世雖未嘗
好戰也亦未嘗忘戰也既未嘗好兵也亦
punctuated: 知安危之相為倚伏，則國家於兵法當振舉於平時；知文武之相為倚用，則學者於兵法當備陳於今日。蓋乆安而危不防，則危必作；隆文而武弗繼，則武必衰。皆非保邦長治之良圖、文武並行不悖之全策也。此其所以未事之先，當求夫將為有能之將、兵為有制之兵，而臨事之日，庶幾將得士心、兵識將意，近足以保安天下，遠足以流芳後世。若漢之諸葛、宋之名將，乃可以語此。而我國朝選將材、定武舉，則又安不忘危、文不廢武，超百王而獨邁者，政不必以兵為諱也。執事發策，首逮於此，其亦慮關廟廊而憂先天下者乎？愚請復其萬一。兵果可言耶？古人有曰：「先王耀德不觀兵。」吾不得而知也。兵果不可言耶？古人又曰：「兵者，生民之大本。」吾亦不得而知也。要之，治世雖未嘗好戰也，亦未嘗忘戰也；既未嘗好兵也，亦
translation_en:
Knowing that security and peril harbor one another, the state should give vigorous attention to military methods in times of peace; knowing that civil and military pursuits depend upon one another in practice, scholars should fully set forth military methods today. For if prolonged peace leaves peril unguarded against, peril will surely arise; if civil pursuits flourish but military preparedness does not keep pace, military strength will surely decline. Neither is a sound plan for preserving the realm and securing lasting order, nor a comprehensive policy under which civil and military pursuits proceed together without conflict. Thus, before trouble arises, we must seek capable commanders and properly regulated troops, so that when action becomes necessary, commanders may command their soldiers’ loyalty and soldiers may understand their commanders’ intentions. In the near term, this will suffice to keep all under Heaven secure; in the long term, it will leave a fragrant reputation to posterity. Only such men as Zhuge of the Han and the celebrated generals of the Song can be spoken of in these terms. Our own dynasty selects men of military talent and has established the military examinations: secure, it does not forget peril; cultivating civil pursuits, it does not neglect military affairs. In this it surpasses the hundred kings and advances unrivaled. There is certainly no need to make military affairs a taboo subject.

You, sir, have issued policy questions and addressed this matter first. Surely your thoughts concern the imperial court, and you take upon yourself the cares of all under Heaven before others do? I venture to offer a reply touching on a fraction of the matter. May military affairs indeed be discussed? An ancient said, “The former kings displayed their virtue; they did not parade their troops.” I cannot tell. May military affairs indeed not be discussed? Another ancient said, “Arms are the great foundation of the people’s livelihood.” Again, I cannot tell. In essence, although an age of good government has never delighted in warfare, neither has it ever forgotten warfare; although it has never delighted in arms, neither …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未嘗去兵也然而兵屬於將將統乎兵而
君又擇乎將君不擇將是以國予敵也將
不練兵是以主予敵也甚矣兵將之間容
可忽耶兵將之論容可已耶虞舜惟其明
是也故當四方風動之時而在內則明射
侯以為教養之術在外則奮武衛以為備
禦之防汲汲然惟恐兵之未練固不聞以
兵為諱也武王惟其明是也故當四海永
清之時而於春夏則有振旅茇舍之名於
===
秋冬則有治兵大閱之法汲汲然惟恐兵
之未練亦不聞以兵為諱也我
孝宗敬皇帝惟心舜武之心也故開求將之科
而創試材之式我
皇上惟心
先帝之心也故求將材於天下而定武舉於
京師統兵衛國計出萬全久安長治其盛矣
哉蓋嘗聞之武侯矣所謂將材有八如道
德齊禮仁將也而又義禮智信無一而不
punctuated:
未嘗去兵也。然而兵屬於將，將統乎兵，而君又擇乎將。君不擇將，是以國予敵也；將不練兵，是以主予敵也。甚矣！兵將之間，容可忽耶？兵將之論，容可已耶？虞舜惟其明是也，故當四方風動之時，而在內則明射侯，以為教養之術；在外則奮武衛，以為備禦之防。汲汲然惟恐兵之未練，固不聞以兵為諱也。武王惟其明是也，故當四海永清之時，而於春夏則有振旅、茇舍之名，於秋冬則有治兵、大閱之法。汲汲然惟恐兵之未練，亦不聞以兵為諱也。
我孝宗敬皇帝惟心舜武之心也，故開求將之科，而創試材之式。我皇上惟心先帝之心也，故求將材於天下，而定武舉於京師。統兵衛國，計出萬全；久安長治，其盛矣哉！
蓋嘗聞之武侯矣，所謂將材有八，如道德齊禮，仁將也，而又義禮智信無一而不
translation_en:
…nor have they ever dispensed with arms. Yet soldiers are subordinate to generals, generals command soldiers, and the ruler in turn selects the generals. If the ruler fails to select his generals properly, he hands his state over to the enemy; if a general fails to train his soldiers, he hands his sovereign over to the enemy. How grave this is! Can the relationship between soldiers and generals possibly be neglected? Can discussion of soldiers and generals possibly cease? Shun of Yu understood this. Thus, when his influence stirred all quarters like the wind, at home he promoted target archery as a means of instruction and cultivation; abroad he mustered armed guards as a precaution against attack. He strove urgently, fearing only that his soldiers were insufficiently trained. Certainly, we do not hear that he treated military matters as taboo. King Wu understood this. Thus, when all within the Four Seas enjoyed lasting peace, in spring and summer there were exercises called “marshalling the troops” and “encamping in the fields,” and in autumn and winter there were procedures for “training the troops” and the “grand review.” He too strove urgently, fearing only that his soldiers were insufficiently trained. Nor do we hear that he treated military matters as taboo.
Our Emperor Xiaozong Jing took the hearts of Shun and King Wu as his own. He therefore established an examination to seek generals and instituted a procedure for testing their abilities. Our reigning emperor takes the late emperor’s heart as his own. He therefore seeks men with the talents of generals throughout the realm and has established the military examinations at the capital. In commanding troops and defending the state, his plans provide for every eventuality. How magnificent are this enduring peace and lasting good government!
I have heard from the teachings of the Marquis of Wu that there are eight types of talent in generals. For example, one who leads through virtue and brings order through ritual propriety is a benevolent general; moreover, in righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness, there is not one respect in which he does not…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
全好賢從諫大將也而短兵長射無往而
不利者是已若夫貪求妬賢好佞荒淫之
類兹非八弊歟所謂將德有五如廉節孝
悌可以勵俗而揚名信義力行可以交友
而立功者是已若夫謀不能料是非亂不
能正刑法之類兹非八惡歟所謂將善有
五知敵之形勢與夫進退虛實之道知天
時人事與夫山川夷險之勢者是已若夫
議欲共而謀欲密衆欲靜而心欲一兹
===
非四欲歟夫具是材全是德備是善充是
欲而其曰惡曰弊無一毫存焉其為將也
非天下之全將而何哉自夫兵言之所謂
兵强有四君政脩也臣陳力也民服教也
兵從令也是已而其兵義者王兵應者勝
兵忿者亡兵貪者死兵驕者敗兹非五戒
歟所謂武德有七制亂也耀德也時動也
守成脩備也勤政興利也是已而其曰輕
曰慢曰盜曰欺與背曰亂與誤兹非七禁
punctuated:
全。好賢從諫，大將也，而短兵長射，無往而不利者是已。若夫貪求、妬賢、好佞、荒淫之類，兹非八弊歟？所謂將德有五，如廉節孝悌，可以勵俗而揚名；信義力行，可以交友而立功者是已。若夫謀不能料是非，亂不能正刑法之類，兹非八惡歟？所謂將善有五，知敵之形勢與夫進退虛實之道，知天時人事與夫山川夷險之勢者是已。若夫議欲共而謀欲密，衆欲靜而心欲一，兹非四欲歟？夫具是材，全是德，備是善，充是欲，而其曰惡曰弊，無一毫存焉，其為將也，非天下之全將而何哉？

自夫兵言之，所謂兵强有四，君政脩也，臣陳力也，民服教也，兵從令也，是已。而其兵義者王，兵應者勝，兵忿者亡，兵貪者死，兵驕者敗，兹非五戒歟？所謂武德有七，制亂也，耀德也，時動也，守成脩備也，勤政興利也，是已。而其曰輕、曰慢、曰盜、曰欺，與背、曰亂、與誤，兹非七禁
translation_en:
…complete in every respect. One who esteems worthy men and accepts remonstrance is a great general; he succeeds wherever he goes, whether fighting with short weapons or shooting at long range. As for greed, jealousy of the worthy, fondness for flatterers, debauchery, and the like, are these not among the eight failings? There are said to be five virtues of a general: integrity, moral steadfastness, filial piety, and brotherly respect can improve customs and bring renown; trustworthiness, righteousness, and diligent practice can win friends and establish merit. As for being unable to judge right and wrong in planning, or unable to set punishments and laws in order amid disorder, are these not among the eight evils? There are said to be five excellences of a general: knowing the enemy’s disposition and strategic circumstances, and the principles of advance and retreat, weakness and strength; and knowing heavenly timing and human affairs, and the configuration of mountains and rivers, whether level or rugged. As for wishing deliberations to be shared but plans to be secret, the troops to be calm and their minds united, are these not the four desiderata? If a man possesses these talents, perfects these virtues, commands these excellences, and fulfills these desiderata, while retaining not the slightest trace of those evils and failings, what could he be but a consummate general of the realm?

Speaking of military forces, there are said to be four sources of strength: the ruler’s government is well ordered, ministers exert their abilities, the people submit to instruction, and soldiers obey commands. Moreover, righteous warfare brings true kingship; warfare undertaken in response to aggression brings victory; warfare driven by anger brings ruin; warfare driven by greed brings death; and warfare driven by arrogance brings defeat. Are these not the five admonitions? There are said to be seven martial virtues: suppressing disorder, displaying virtue, acting at the proper time, preserving achievements, maintaining preparations, attending diligently to government, and promoting benefits. As for recklessness, negligence, theft, deceit, betrayal, disorder, and error—the wording of this list is uncertain [?]—are these not the seven prohibitions…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
歟所謂兵勢有三五星合度天勢也險易
殊形地勢也主聖將賢人勢也是已而其
事機作而不能應勢機動而不能圖情機
發而不能行者非三機歟夫以有是强兼
是德乘是勢而於所謂戒與機者無有一
事忽焉其為兵也非天下之全兵而何哉
若我廣右固幅員之荒服也交廣之界限
也犬羊之出沒也金革之交鳴也山川之
險阻也我
===
祖宗亦以此為軫轄而嚴總帥於要衝執事亦
以此為鎖鑰而詢先代之名將夫所謂奮
揚威武而擊曹成之寇者非黃齊歟忠義
果敢而戢儂賊之兵者非梁仲保歟歐陽
脩薦其智畧可任將軍者張守約也狄青
薦其驍勇而破儂賊者黃逵也文武兼全
則有陳本道焉一代名將則有楊文廣焉
嗚呼才不易生將不易名戎不易制功不
易立而數君子卒能建不世之奇績垂不
punctuated:
歟？所謂兵勢有三：五星合度，天勢也；險易殊形，地勢也；主聖將賢，人勢也，是已。而其事機作而不能應，勢機動而不能圖，情機發而不能行者，非三機歟？夫以有是强，兼是德，乘是勢，而於所謂戒與機者，無有一事忽焉，其為兵也，非天下之全兵而何哉？
若我廣右，固幅員之荒服也，交廣之界限也，犬羊之出沒也，金革之交鳴也，山川之險阻也。我祖宗亦以此為軫轄，而嚴總帥於要衝。執事亦以此為鎖鑰，而詢先代之名將。夫所謂奮揚威武而擊曹成之寇者，非黃齊歟？忠義果敢而戢儂賊之兵者，非梁仲保歟？歐陽脩薦其智畧可任將軍者，張守約也；狄青薦其驍勇而破儂賊者，黃逵也。文武兼全，則有陳本道焉；一代名將，則有楊文廣焉。嗚呼！才不易生，將不易名，戎不易制，功不易立，而數君子卒能建不世之奇績，垂不
translation_en:
…are they not? The so-called three strategic advantages in warfare are these: the five planets aligning in their proper courses constitute the advantage of Heaven; the differing configurations of difficult and easy terrain constitute the advantage of Earth; and a sagely ruler with worthy generals constitutes the human advantage. Yet when an opportunity arising from events presents itself, one cannot respond; when an opportunity arising from the strategic situation shifts, one cannot devise a plan; and when an opportunity arising from circumstances emerges, one cannot act—do these not concern the three kinds of opportunity? Possessing these strengths, combining these virtues, and taking advantage of these conditions, while neglecting nothing concerning the aforementioned cautions and opportunities—what could such an army be but the most complete army under Heaven?
Our Guangyou is indeed a remote outer domain of the realm, the borderland between Jiao and Guang, a place where “dogs and sheep” come and go, where weapons and armor clash, and where mountains and rivers present formidable obstacles. Our imperial ancestors likewise regarded this region as a linchpin and firmly established supreme military command at its strategic points. You, too, regard it as a strategic gateway and therefore inquire about the renowned generals of earlier ages. Was it not Huang Qi who displayed martial might and struck the bandits led by Cao Cheng? Was it not Liang Zhongbao who, loyal, righteous, resolute, and courageous, quelled the forces of the Nong rebels? The man whom Ouyang Xiu recommended as sufficiently intelligent and resourceful to serve as a general was Zhang Shouyue; the man whom Di Qing recommended for his valor and who defeated the Nong rebels was Huang Kui. For someone fully accomplished in both civil and military affairs, there was Chen Bendao; for a renowned general of his age, there was Yang Wenguang. Alas! Talent is not easily born; a general’s reputation is not easily won; armed forces are not easily controlled; and achievements are not easily established. Yet these gentlemen ultimately accomplished extraordinary feats rarely seen in any age and left behind …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
世之偉名雖其將才將德將善之足稱者
固未純乎諸葛之所云也而皆千夫之特
萬人之雄矣其兵强武德兵勢之足法者
亦未必純乎諸葛之所云也而皆節制之
師勇銳之卒矣執事有懷於前而又有望
於後乃曰側陋之中豈無非熊伏龍而深
知擇將用兵之畧者是亦問陶朱於三家
之市求忠信於十室之邑雖然兵民本一
塗文武非二道而前人固有以攻刺擊殺
===
之事非儒其衣冠者所可能也愚竊謂鳴
條之師誰爲之牧野之師誰爲之東山之
師又誰爲之則夫山鳴谷應之間固未必
無鷹揚虎嘯之士也然則將之爲將何以
擇之不拘於門望也不拘於地理也而得
一傑然於庸將之中者則知其爲才之小
得一傑然於才將之中者則知其爲才之
大而又窮之言辭以觀其變與之簡牒以
觀其誠明白顯問以觀其德使之以財以
punctuated:
世之偉名。雖其將才、將德、將善之足稱者，固未純乎諸葛之所云也，而皆千夫之特、萬人之雄矣。其兵强、武德、兵勢之足法者，亦未必純乎諸葛之所云也，而皆節制之師、勇銳之卒矣。執事有懷於前，而又有望於後，乃曰：「側陋之中，豈無非熊、伏龍，而深知擇將用兵之畧者？」是亦問陶朱於三家之市，求忠信於十室之邑。雖然，兵民本一塗，文武非二道，而前人固有以攻刺擊殺之事非儒其衣冠者所可能也。
愚竊謂：鳴條之師，誰爲之？牧野之師，誰爲之？東山之師，又誰爲之？則夫山鳴谷應之間，固未必無鷹揚虎嘯之士也。然則將之爲將，何以擇之？不拘於門望也，不拘於地理也。而得一傑然於庸將之中者，則知其爲才之小；得一傑然於才將之中者，則知其爲才之大。而又窮之言辭以觀其變，與之簡牒以觀其誠，明白顯問以觀其德，使之以財以
translation_en:
…an extraordinary name for posterity. Although their praiseworthy abilities, virtues, and strengths as commanders did not wholly conform to what Zhuge Liang described, they were nevertheless outstanding among a thousand men, heroes among ten thousand. Although the strength of their troops, their martial virtue, and their disposition of forces that merit emulation likewise may not have wholly conformed to what Zhuge Liang described, theirs were nevertheless disciplined armies and brave, keen troops. You, honored examiners, cherish the men of the past and also place hopes in those to come. Thus you ask: “Among men living in humble obscurity, might there not be a ‘Not-a-Bear’ or a ‘Hidden Dragon’—men like Jiang Ziya or Zhuge Liang—who profoundly understand the strategies of selecting commanders and employing troops?” This is like seeking a Tao Zhu in a market of three households, or seeking loyalty and trustworthiness in a settlement of ten households. Nevertheless, soldiers and civilians fundamentally follow one path; civil and military affairs are not two separate ways. Yet some men of earlier times indeed held that attacking, stabbing, striking, and killing were beyond the abilities of those dressed in Confucian caps and robes.
In my humble view: who led the army at Mingtiao? Who led the army at Muye? And who led the army at Dongshan? Surely, amid the sounding mountains and answering valleys, there may well be men who soar like eagles and roar like tigers. How, then, should commanders be selected for command? Do not be constrained by family prestige; do not be constrained by place of origin. If one finds a man who stands out among ordinary commanders, one knows that his talent is of the lesser order; if one finds a man who stands out among talented commanders, one knows that his talent is of the greater order. Furthermore, press him to the limits in discussion to observe his adaptability; give him written documents to observe his sincerity; question him plainly and openly to observe his virtue; entrust him with wealth in order to…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
觀其廉試之以色以觀其貞凡於諸葛之
所尚者尚之所懲者懲之如此而曰將不
得人未之聞也借曰專制閫外皆膏粱之
流運籌帷幄者非韜畧之輩真兒戲耳何
有於擇將兵之為兵又何以用之必先明
之物采辨之等列以昭其尊卑貴賤順之
少長習之威儀以申其孝弟忠信而又於
未戰則養其財將戰則養其力既戰則養
其氣既勝則養其心凡於諸葛之所用者
===
用之所革者革之如此而曰兵不得人未
之聞也借曰散於州縣者籍為營壘之符
游於田畝者律以卒伍之令亦虛文耳抑
何有於用兵愚於此又有說焉論兵非難
論將為難得良將非難得良相為難未有
將得人而兵非其兵者也亦未有相得人
而將非其將者也故韓信之拜將由於蕭
何趙充國之進計本於魏相將顧不係於
相耶有方叔則不患師干之不試有吉甫
punctuated: 觀其廉，試之以色，以觀其貞。凡於諸葛之所尚者尚之，所懲者懲之。如此而曰將不得人，未之聞也。借曰專制閫外皆膏粱之流，運籌帷幄者非韜畧之輩，真兒戲耳，何有於擇將？兵之為兵，又何以用之？必先明之物采，辨之等列，以昭其尊卑貴賤；順之少長，習之威儀，以申其孝弟忠信。而又於未戰則養其財，將戰則養其力，既戰則養其氣，既勝則養其心。凡於諸葛之所用者用之，所革者革之。如此而曰兵不得人，未之聞也。借曰散於州縣者籍為營壘之符，游於田畝者律以卒伍之令，亦虛文耳，抑何有於用兵？愚於此又有說焉：論兵非難，論將為難；得良將非難，得良相為難。未有將得人而兵非其兵者也，亦未有相得人而將非其將者也。故韓信之拜將由於蕭何，趙充國之進計本於魏相，將顧不係於相耶？有方叔則不患師干之不試，有吉甫
translation_en:
…to observe his integrity; test him with feminine beauty to observe his constancy. Esteem whatever Zhuge Liang esteemed, and censure whatever he censured. With this approach, I have never heard of a failure to find suitable men as generals. If, however, those exercising independent command in the field are all sons of privilege, and those devising strategies within the command tent possess no military expertise, this is truly child's play. What does it amount to as a means of selecting generals?

As for soldiers, how should they be employed? First make their insignia clear and distinguish their ranks, so that their relative standing and status are manifest. Order them according to seniority and train them in dignified conduct, thereby reinforcing their filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness. Before battle, nurture their material resources; when battle approaches, nurture their strength; once battle is engaged, nurture their spirit; after victory, nurture their resolve. Employ whatever Zhuge Liang employed, and abolish whatever he abolished. With this approach, I have never heard of a failure to obtain suitable soldiers. If, however, men scattered throughout the prefectures and counties are merely entered on registers as credentials for the military camps, and those working in the fields are subjected to the regulations of the ranks, this too is empty paperwork. What does it amount to as a means of employing troops?

I, in my ignorance, have a further observation on this matter. Assessing soldiers is not difficult; assessing generals is difficult. Obtaining good generals is not difficult; obtaining a good chief councilor is difficult. Never has the right man been chosen as general without his soldiers being fit for their role; nor has the right man been chosen as chief councilor without the generals being fit for theirs. Thus Han Xin's appointment as general came through Xiao He, and Zhao Chongguo's submission of his plan depended upon Wei Xiang. Do generals not, then, depend upon chief councilors? With Fang Shu, there is no fear that the army will fail to prove its prowess; with Ji Fu…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
正德癸酉瀛應聘預廣右校
試由岳陽浮洞庭觀衡岳迤
邐入安道寔桂嶺第一程也
立馬四望萬山在目而草木
叢密遼廓眇忽竊喜踪跡未
半天下倏得竒觀夙願亦足
===
少償不兩舍許抵清湘則風
景更熾而長松古栢夾道綿
三百里餘其霜皮溜雨黛色
參天有偃盖蛟龍形者有躚
徙鶴翅廻者又有錯落龍鱗
出者且風韻颼颺若奏笙簧
掩竽籟而勝益竒至桂林則
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

正德癸酉，瀛應聘預廣右校試，由岳陽浮洞庭，觀衡岳，迤邐入安道，寔桂嶺第一程也。立馬四望，萬山在目，而草木叢密，遼廓眇忽。竊喜踪跡未半天下，倏得竒觀，夙願亦足少償。不兩舍許，抵清湘，則風景更熾，而長松古栢夾道，綿三百里餘。其霜皮溜雨，黛色參天，有偃盖蛟龍形者，有躚徙鶴翅廻者，又有錯落龍鱗出者。且風韻颼颺，若奏笙簧，掩竽籟，而勝益竒。至桂林，則
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the guiyou year of the Zhengde reign [1513], I, Ying, accepted an invitation to participate in examining candidates in Guangyou [Guangxi]. From Yueyang I sailed across Lake Dongting, viewed Mount Heng, and wound my way onto the road through An [?], truly the first stage into the mountains of Guangxi. Reining in my horse, I gazed in every direction: countless mountains lay before my eyes, thick with trees and undergrowth, their vast expanses fading into the distance. I privately rejoiced that, although my travels had not yet covered half the realm, I had suddenly encountered such extraordinary scenery, enough to fulfill a little of my long-held wish.

Within scarcely two stages of travel, I reached Qingxiang, where the scenery grew still more luxuriant. Tall pines and ancient cypresses lined the road for over three hundred li. Rain streamed down their frost-weathered bark, and their dark green crowns towered into the sky. Some spread their canopies in the shapes of dragons; some swayed like the wheeling wings of cranes [?]; others displayed overlapping patterns like dragons’ scales. Moreover, the wind sighed and whistled through them, as though playing reed mouth organs, surpassing the sounds of pipes and flutes and making the scene still more remarkable. Upon reaching Guilin, …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
山峭拔如畫水清而駛松栢
益茂蓋山川之秀産乎異材
者如此於戲地靈人杰固也
鍾於物者且然人生其間豈
無光明俊偉之習卓犖魁竒
之才文章德行之士可以名
世者乎及得士之文讀之不
===
豐贍而平淡則清勁而飄逸
雖所造有淺深醇疵不同然
養之正詞之順氣之充槩有
足觀者柳子厚嘗恠陽德之
炳燿獨發於紛葩瓌麗而罕
鍾乎人是方恐兼有之也雖
然松栢之可愛者豈直瀛前
punctuated: 山峭拔如畫，水清而駛，松栢益茂。蓋山川之秀，産乎異材者如此。於戲！地靈人杰，固也。鍾於物者且然，人生其間，豈無光明俊偉之習、卓犖魁竒之才、文章德行之士，可以名世者乎？及得士之文讀之，不豐贍而平淡，則清勁而飄逸。雖所造有淺深醇疵不同，然養之正、詞之順、氣之充，槩有足觀者。柳子厚嘗恠陽德之炳燿，獨發於紛葩瓌麗，而罕鍾乎人，是方恐兼有之也。雖然，松栢之可愛者，豈直瀛前
translation_en:
…the mountains rise steeply, like a painting; the waters are clear and swift; and the pines and cypresses grow still more luxuriantly. Such is the way the finest qualities of mountains and rivers produce extraordinary timber. Ah! That a spiritually potent land produces outstanding people is surely true. If these qualities are concentrated even in material things to such a degree, how could the people born among them lack luminous and noble dispositions, exceptional and extraordinary talents, or men whose literary accomplishments and moral conduct could win renown in their age?

When I obtained the candidates’ writings and read them, they were either rich and ample yet plain and understated, or lucid and vigorous yet free-flowing. Although their attainments differed in depth, purity, and flaws, their upright cultivation, fluent expression, and fullness of vital energy generally offered much worth admiring. Liu Zihou once wondered why the radiant power of yang manifested itself only in abundant blossoms and magnificent beauty, yet was seldom concentrated in human beings. This region, I venture to think, possesses both.

Nevertheless, are pines and cypresses lovable merely for what Ying [?] previously …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所狀者哉有心也記禮者稱
之後凋也孔子取之必有以
也今夫貞心勁質禦攘氷霜
剛也四時一貫榮悴不易常
也畝毒以蔽行道無苦仁也
蔦與女蘿上有兎絲義也雖
春陽氣王不與羣木鬭榮謙
===
也凡此數德可比君子及乎
將用大可以柱明堂棟大廈
次之為榱為桷非若樗櫟之
竟老山林耳矣然則諸士子
歷階而升其亦松栢之有資
於世用者乎而其自處所宜
比德松栢殷勤封殖為他日
punctuated: 所狀者哉？有心也。記禮者稱之，後凋也；孔子取之，必有以也。今夫貞心勁質，禦攘氷霜，剛也；四時一貫，榮悴不易，常也；畝毒以蔽，行道無苦，仁也；蔦與女蘿，上有兎絲，義也；雖春陽氣王，不與羣木鬭榮，謙也。凡此數德，可比君子。及乎將用，大可以柱明堂、棟大廈，次之為榱、為桷，非若樗櫟之竟老山林耳矣。然則諸士子歷階而升，其亦松栢之有資於世用者乎？而其自處，所宜比德松栢，殷勤封殖，為他日
translation_en:
…merely what was described above? They possess an inner resolve. The recorder of rites praises them for withering late; Confucius’s esteem for them must have its reasons. Their steadfast hearts and sturdy substance withstand ice and frost: this is firmness. They remain consistent through the four seasons, unchanged by flourishing or decline: this is constancy. They provide shelter [?], sparing travelers hardship: this is benevolence. Ivy and trailing vines, with dodder growing upon them: this is righteousness. Though the spring sun’s vital force flourishes, they do not compete with the other trees in splendor: this is humility. All these virtues may be compared to those of a gentleman.

When put to use, the largest can serve as pillars of the Hall of Enlightenment or ridgepoles of great buildings; the next in size can become rafters and roof timbers. They are unlike the ailanthus and oak, which merely grow old in the mountain forests. Thus, as these examination candidates ascend the steps, are they not also like pines and cypresses that contribute to the practical needs of the world? In their own conduct, they should emulate the virtues of pine and cypress, diligently tending and nurturing themselves, to become, in days to come…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廊廟器則於地之靈可謂無
負矣不然是亦凡草木而已
奚取焉事竣謹書此列于左
湖廣衡州府耒陽縣儒學教
諭姜瀛謹序
punctuated:
廊廟器，則於地之靈可謂無負矣。不然，是亦凡草木而已，奚取焉？事竣，謹書此列于左。
湖廣衡州府耒陽縣儒學教諭姜瀛謹序。
translation_en:
…instruments of service at court; then they may be said not to have failed the numinous potency of this land. Otherwise, they would be merely ordinary plants and trees—what would commend them? Upon completion of the proceedings, I respectfully wrote this and set it down to the left.
Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Ying, Instructor of the Confucian School of Leiyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
皇上嗣大歷服改元之八年是為
正德癸酉天下當大比以取
士也於是廣西巡按監察御
史朱志榮謀于總督兩廣右都
御史林廷選總鎮太監潘忠總
兵武定侯郭勛咸謂此
===
國家致治之事莫有大焉者鉅
細之務具載甲令盍豫飭所
司如令行之而鎮守太監陳
彬副總兵金堂相與贊襄益
力巡按御史以責任尤專也
遂博訪儒紳之有名行者移
檄禮聘司鑑衡之任比及期
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

皇上嗣大歷服，改元之八年，是為正德癸酉，天下當大比以取士也。於是廣西巡按監察御史朱志榮謀于總督兩廣右都御史林廷選、總鎮太監潘忠、總兵武定侯郭勛，咸謂：「此國家致治之事，莫有大焉者。鉅細之務，具載甲令，盍豫飭所司如令行之？」而鎮守太監陳彬、副總兵金堂相與贊襄益力。巡按御史以責任尤專也，遂博訪儒紳之有名行者，移檄禮聘，司鑑衡之任。比及期，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth year after His Majesty inherited the great imperial charge [?] and changed the reign title—the guiyou year of Zhengde [1513]—the triennial examinations were due to be held throughout the realm to select men for service. Accordingly, Zhu Zhirong, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor for Guangxi, consulted Lin Tingxuan, Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi and Right Censor-in-Chief; Pan Zhong, Eunuch Grand Defender; and Guo Xun, Regional Commander and Marquis of Wuding. All agreed: “Among the affairs through which the state achieves good government, none is greater than this. Every matter, large and small, is fully set out in the statutes. Why not instruct the responsible offices in advance to proceed according to those statutes?” Chen Bin, the Eunuch Defender, and Jin Tang, the Vice Regional Commander, joined in supporting the undertaking with still greater effort.

Since the Regional Inspector bore particularly direct responsibility, he made extensive inquiries to find scholarly gentlemen distinguished for their reputation and conduct, dispatched official communications, and courteously invited them to undertake the work of assessing the candidates. When the appointed time arrived …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乃入院主監臨之事而以左
布政使夏暹右參政蔚春為
提調副使陳陽僉事孫徵為
監試其考試則奎偕教諭姜
瀛同考試則學正陳獻教諭
鄭悰杜子新方珩訓導鄭鳴也
至於右布政使周進隆左參政
===
李綱右參政陸徵左參議楊
瑋右參議左唐按察使方良永
副使翁茂南張弘宜僉事薛金都
指揮同知彭鐸又皆恊心防
範於外蓋斯事重且大亦弗
敢以弗預而少有弗虔也既
鎖院廼合提督學校副使劉
punctuated: 乃入院主監臨之事，而以左布政使夏暹、右參政蔚春為提調，副使陳陽、僉事孫徵為監試。其考試則奎偕教諭姜瀛，同考試則學正陳獻、教諭鄭悰、杜子新、方珩、訓導鄭鳴也。至於右布政使周進隆、左參政李綱、右參政陸徵、左參議楊瑋、右參議左唐、按察使方良永、副使翁茂南、張弘宜、僉事薛金、都指揮同知彭鐸，又皆恊心防範於外。蓋斯事重且大，亦弗敢以弗預而少有弗虔也。既鎖院，廼合提督學校副使劉
translation_en:
…then he entered the examination compound to undertake the duties of Supervising Official. Xia Xian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Yu Chun 蔚春, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner, were appointed Proctors; Chen Yang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Sun Zheng, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, were appointed examination monitors. Kui 奎 served as Examiner together with Jiang Ying, a School Instructor. The Associate Examiners were Chen Xian, a School Director; Zheng Cong, Du Zixin, and Fang Heng, School Instructors; and Zheng Ming, an Assistant Instructor.

Meanwhile, Zhou Jinlong, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Li Gang, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Lu Zheng, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Yang Wei, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zuo Tang, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Fang Liangyong, Surveillance Commissioner; Weng Maonan and Zhang Hongyi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Xue Jin, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Peng Duo, Vice Regional Military Commissioner, all worked together to maintain safeguards outside the compound. For this undertaking was weighty and momentous: they dared not show the slightest lack of reverence merely because they were not directly participating.

Once the compound had been locked, there were then assembled those whom Liu, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner charged with supervising schools…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
台所簡應試之士八百有奇
如式三試而校閱之得其文
之中式者殊多而僅取如額
數第其甲乙揭榜以示仍梓
為錄并刻其文之優者進
呈於
上而傳諸四方錄有序奎當承乏
===
乃言曰廣西古百粤地也居
荆楚西南距
京師殊僻遠其人物之見於史
牒者自漢以後漸盛入
國朝迄今尤彬彬輩出而名公
碩輔德業聞望後先相繼與
中州等矣是豈無所自耶竊
punctuated:
台所簡應試之士八百有奇，如式三試而校閱之，得其文之中式者殊多，而僅取如額數，第其甲乙，揭榜以示。仍梓為錄，并刻其文之優者，進呈於上，而傳諸四方。錄有序，奎當承乏，乃言曰：
「廣西，古百粤地也。居荆楚西南，距京師殊僻遠。其人物之見於史牒者，自漢以後漸盛。入國朝迄今，尤彬彬輩出，而名公碩輔，德業聞望，後先相繼，與中州等矣。是豈無所自耶？竊
translation_en:
…the more than eight hundred candidates selected by [Liu] Tai were assembled, examined in three sessions according to the prescribed procedure, and their papers evaluated. Very many of their compositions met the required standard, but only the allotted number of candidates were accepted. They were ranked in order of merit, and a list was posted to announce the results. A record was then printed from woodblocks, together with the finest of their compositions, for presentation to His Majesty and circulation throughout the realm. The record required a preface, and I, Kui, being charged with this duty for want of someone better qualified, thereupon said:
“Guangxi was anciently the land of the Baiyue. It lies southwest of Jing and Chu, exceptionally remote from the capital. From the Han onward, increasing numbers of its people appeared in historical records. Since the founding of our dynasty down to the present, cultivated and accomplished men have emerged in particular abundance. Eminent dignitaries and great ministers, distinguished by their virtue, achievements, renown, and standing, have succeeded one another, equaling those of the Central Plains. Could this have come about without a cause? I humbly…”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
嘗攷之我
祖宗開基銳意於敦崇教化敻與
前代不同彼漢興雖文武並
用然歷四世至孝武元朔而
後太學始興有宋固號稱崇
儒右文也亦至仁宗慶曆而
後有州郡之學惟我
===
聖祖即位之明年遂
詔天下立府州縣學以養育人
材又明年遂
詔天下設科以起懷材抱德之
士至十七年乃定今制以取
士其儲養簡拔振作人材之
意若汲汲焉惟恐後者
punctuated: 嘗攷之，我祖宗開基，銳意於敦崇教化，敻與前代不同。彼漢興，雖文武並用，然歷四世，至孝武元朔而後太學始興。有宋固號稱崇儒右文也，亦至仁宗慶曆而後有州郡之學。惟我聖祖即位之明年，遂詔天下立府州縣學，以養育人材；又明年，遂詔天下設科，以起懷材抱德之士。至十七年，乃定今制以取士。其儲養、簡拔、振作人材之意，若汲汲焉，惟恐後者。
translation_en: …I have examined this matter. When our imperial ancestors founded the dynasty, they devoted themselves resolutely to promoting moral instruction, differing markedly from earlier dynasties. Although the Han employed both civil and military means when it arose, four reigns elapsed, and only in the Yuanshuo era of Emperor Xiaowu did the Imperial University begin to flourish. The Song was certainly renowned for honoring Confucian learning and giving precedence to literary culture, yet schools in prefectures were established only in the Qingli era of Emperor Renzong. Our sagely founding emperor, however, in the year following his accession, issued an edict ordering the establishment of schools in prefectures, subprefectures, and counties throughout the realm to nurture talent. In the following year, he issued another edict instituting examinations throughout the realm to bring forth men possessing talent and virtue. In the seventeenth year, he established the present system for selecting men for office. His determination to cultivate, select, and invigorate talented men was so urgent that he seemed to fear only being too late.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承益隆繼述故論其養之
也有明經之師有廩餼之供
有給復之令而又有憲臣以
董正於上其取之也有刻錄
之傳有錫宴之榮有勸駕之
典而又有敘用之格以激厲
於其間蓋其所以崇尚而歆
===
艶之使之漸磨造就以自趨
於成德達材之域者無弗至
故百餘年來薄海内外人才
之生咸感發奮厲競自洗濯
以效用有古黎獻風廣西雖
僻遠其風化所及固不異也
則人才之盛宜哉然自昔而
punctuated: 列聖相承，益隆繼述。故論其養之也，有明經之師，有廩餼之供，有給復之令，而又有憲臣以董正於上；其取之也，有刻錄之傳，有錫宴之榮，有勸駕之典，而又有敘用之格以激厲於其間。蓋其所以崇尚而歆艶之，使之漸磨造就，以自趨於成德達材之域者，無弗至。故百餘年來，薄海内外，人才之生，咸感發奮厲，競自洗濯以效用，有古黎獻風。廣西雖僻遠，其風化所及，固不異也，則人才之盛宜哉！然自昔而
translation_en:
Successive sage emperors carried on this legacy, increasingly honoring and advancing their predecessors’ work. Thus, as regards their nurturing of scholars, there are teachers versed in the Classics, provisions of grain stipends, and orders granting exemption from service obligations; moreover, censorial officials oversee and rectify matters from above. As regards their selection of scholars, there are printed examination records for circulation, the honor of imperially bestowed banquets, and ceremonies encouraging successful candidates to proceed to the next examination; moreover, there are regulations for appointment to office to spur them onward. Indeed, nothing has been left undone to esteem scholarship and make it an object of eager admiration, so that scholars may gradually refine themselves and develop their abilities, advancing of their own accord toward perfected virtue and fully realized talent.
Thus, for more than a hundred years, wherever talented men have arisen throughout the realm and beyond, to the shores of the seas, all have been inspired to exert themselves, striving to purify themselves so as to render service, in the spirit of the worthy men of antiquity. Although Guangxi is remote, it is no different in receiving this moral influence. How fitting, then, that talent should flourish there! Yet, considering matters from former times onward …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
觀其用於世者雖所遇不同
要皆馳聲樹績有可述而志
者或不然則其所養有未至
故見惑於他岐守變於初志
中道而不能自立耳夫鈞是
人也鈞是化也而人品頓殊
如此亦獨何哉余為是懼用
===
以此告諸士之既見錄者以
究其終并勵未見錄者之志
俾益厚自養以待時而與前
哲匹休此固同有事塲屋者
之意而非余之私也
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣
儒學教諭張奎謹序
punctuated:
觀其用於世者，雖所遇不同，要皆馳聲樹績，有可述而志者。或不然，則其所養有未至，故見惑於他岐，守變於初志，中道而不能自立耳。夫鈞是人也，鈞是化也，而人品頓殊如此，亦獨何哉？余為是懼，用以此告諸士之既見錄者，以究其終，并勵未見錄者之志，俾益厚自養，以待時而與前哲匹休。此固同有事塲屋者之意，而非余之私也。
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學教諭張奎謹序。
translation_en:
…when we consider those who have served in the world, although their circumstances differed, they generally all won renown and established achievements worthy of recounting and recording. If some did not, it was because their self-cultivation remained incomplete: they were led astray by other paths, departed from their original resolve, and could not stand firm midway through their course. They are equally human and have received the same civilizing influence; why, then, should their character differ so sharply? Apprehensive about this, I offer these words to the scholars who have already been selected, so that they may carry their endeavors through to the end. I also encourage the aspirations of those not yet selected, that they may deepen their self-cultivation while awaiting their opportunity and equal the glory of earlier worthies. This is indeed the intention of all who share responsibility for the examination, and not merely my own private view.
Preface respectfully composed by Zhang Kui, Instructor of the Confucian School of Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili).

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
道盛德至善民之不能忘也
知者動仁者靜
聖人治天下使有菽粟如水火菽粟如水
火而民焉有不仁者乎
易
外比於賢以從上也
六四安節亨象曰安節之亨承上道也九
===
五甘節吉往有尚象曰甘節之吉居位
中也
是以明於天之道而察於民之故是興神
物以前民用
繫辭焉而命之動在其中矣
書
五月南巡守至于南岳如岱禮八月西巡
守至于西岳如初十有一月朔巡守至
于北岳如西禮歸格于藝祖用特五載
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
道盛德至善，民之不能忘也。
知者動，仁者靜。
聖人治天下，使有菽粟如水火。菽粟如水火，而民焉有不仁者乎？

易
外比於賢，以從上也。
六四，安節，亨。象曰：「安節之亨，承上道也。」九五，甘節，吉，往有尚。象曰：「甘節之吉，居位中也。」
是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。
繫辭焉而命之，動在其中矣。

書
五月南巡守，至于南岳，如岱禮。八月西巡守，至于西岳，如初。十有一月朔巡守，至于北岳，如西禮。歸格于藝祖，用特。五載
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
This speaks of flourishing virtue and utmost goodness, which the people cannot forget.
The wise are active; the benevolent are still.
When a sage governs all under Heaven, he ensures that beans and grain are as plentiful as water and fire. When beans and grain are as plentiful as water and fire, how could any of the people fail to be benevolent?

Book of Changes
To ally oneself outwardly with the worthy is thereby to follow those above.
Six in the fourth place: Being at ease with restraint brings success. The Image says: “Success through being at ease with restraint comes from following the way of those above.” Nine in the fifth place: Finding sweetness in restraint brings good fortune; going forward brings esteem. The Image says: “Good fortune through finding sweetness in restraint comes from occupying the central position.”
Thus, understanding the Way of Heaven and discerning the circumstances of the people, they brought forth sacred objects to guide the people in their use.
They attached statements to them to give direction, and movement was contained therein.

Book of Documents
In the fifth month, he made a tour of inspection southward, reaching the Southern Sacred Peak, where he performed rites like those at Daizong. In the eighth month, he made a tour of inspection westward, reaching the Western Sacred Peak, where he did as before. In the eleventh month, he made a tour of inspection northward, reaching the Northern Sacred Peak, where he performed rites like those in the west. On returning, he went to the temple of his accomplished ancestor and offered a single bull. Every five years …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
一巡守羣后四朝敷奏以言明試以功
車服以庸
德日新萬邦惟懷
自朝至于日中昃不遑暇食
則克宅之克由繹之
詩
葛之覃兮施于中谷維葉莫莫是刈是濩
為絺為綌服之無斁
我有嘉賓鼓瑟吹笙吹笙鼓簧承筐是將
===
文王受命有此武功既伐于崇作邑于豐
文王烝哉
薄言震之莫不震疊懷柔百神及河喬嶽
春秋
公及邾儀父盟于蔑隱公元年
公次于滑莊公三年
同盟于亳城北會于蕭魚俱襄公十一年
城楚丘僖公二年公至自晉昭公十六年
禮記
punctuated:
一巡守，羣后四朝，敷奏以言，明試以功，車服以庸。
德日新，萬邦惟懷。
自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食。
則克宅之，克由繹之。
詩
葛之覃兮，施于中谷，維葉莫莫。是刈是濩，為絺為綌，服之無斁。
我有嘉賓，鼓瑟吹笙。吹笙鼓簧，承筐是將。
文王受命，有此武功。既伐于崇，作邑于豐。文王烝哉！
薄言震之，莫不震疊。懷柔百神，及河喬嶽。
春秋
公及邾儀父盟于蔑，隱公元年。
公次于滑，莊公三年。
同盟于亳城北，會于蕭魚，俱襄公十一年。
城楚丘，僖公二年。公至自晉，昭公十六年。
禮記
translation_en:
…one tour of inspection; the assembled lords attended court four times. They presented their reports in words, their achievements were clearly assessed, and carriages and robes were bestowed according to merit.

His virtue was renewed daily, and the myriad states cherished him.

From morning until the sun had passed its zenith, he had no leisure to eat.

Then he could establish himself in it and carry it forward.

Book of Odes

How the kudzu vines stretch, spreading into the valley, their leaves luxuriant! They are cut and boiled, made into fine cloth and coarse cloth, to be worn without weariness.

I have honored guests; we play the zither and blow the reed pipes. Blowing the pipes and sounding their reeds, we present baskets of gifts.

King Wen received the Mandate and achieved these martial deeds. Having attacked Chong, he built a city at Feng. How glorious was King Wen!

He displayed his might, and none failed to tremble in awe. He conciliated the hundred spirits, including those of the Yellow River and the lofty mountains.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The duke and Yifu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie. First year of Duke Yin.

The duke encamped at Hua. Third year of Duke Zhuang.

They jointly covenanted north of Bocheng; they met at Xiaoyu. Both in the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.

They fortified Chuqiu. Second year of Duke Xi. The duke returned from Jin. Sixteenth year of Duke Zhao.

Book of Rites

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
班朝治軍涖官行法非禮威嚴不行
故國有禮官有御事有職禮有序
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節
爲上可望而知也爲下可述而志也
第貳場
論
居天下之廣居
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢定振窮養老之令詔文帝元年
===
擬唐以張玄素爲銀青光禄大夫誥貞觀
十四年
擬宋理宗經筵進朱熹通鑑綱目表嘉熙
元年
判語五條
上言大臣德政
錢糧互相覺察
縱放軍人歇役
主守不覺失囚
punctuated:
班朝治軍、涖官行法，非禮威嚴不行。
故國有禮，官有御，事有職，禮有序。
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。
爲上可望而知也，爲下可述而志也。

第貳場
論：居天下之廣居。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢定振窮養老之令詔，文帝元年。
擬唐以張玄素爲銀青光禄大夫誥，貞觀十四年。
擬宋理宗經筵進朱熹通鑑綱目表，嘉熙元年。
判語五條：
上言大臣德政。
錢糧互相覺察。
縱放軍人歇役。
主守不覺失囚。
translation_en:
In ordering ranks at court, governing armies, administering offices, and enforcing laws, awe-inspiring authority cannot be exercised without ritual propriety.
Thus, the state has its rites, offices have their governing rules, affairs have their assigned duties, and rites have their proper sequence.
Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great rites share their measured order.
Those above can be understood by observing them; those below can be recorded and remembered through accounts of their conduct.

Second Session
Discourse: “To dwell in the broad dwelling of all under Heaven.”
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [科, “category,” is doubtful here].
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han establishing orders to relieve the destitute and support the elderly. First year of Emperor Wen’s reign.
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang appointing Zhang Xuansu Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon. Fourteenth year of Zhenguan.
Compose a memorial in the manner of the Song presenting Zhu Xi’s Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian Gangmu) at Emperor Lizong’s Classics Colloquium. First year of Jiaxi.
Five legal judgments:
Submitting statements to the throne praising the virtuous administration of high officials.
Mutual scrutiny in matters of money and grain.
Allowing soldiers to leave their duties and cease service.
Custodians failing to detect the escape of prisoners.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
脩理橋梁道路
第叁場
策五道
問書謂監于先王成憲其永無愆詩謂不
愆不忘率由舊章蓋言祖宗之當法也
伏覩我
太宗文皇帝嘗諭羣臣曰兹予繼承天位恪遵
成憲
仁宗昭皇帝亦嘗諭侍臣曰守成之主動法
===
祖宗斯鮮過舉大哉
王言誠萬世人君之龜鑑也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸奄有萬邦垂憲立法盡
善盡美固有非臣下所能周知亦有非
言語所能形容者姑舉
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書所載君道之大者如聖
孝也聖學也敬天也仁民也求言也聽
納也用賢也勤政也謹戒也節儉也而
皇祖之懿德美行過古帝王遠甚然於前數者
punctuated:
脩理橋梁道路。

第叁場
策五道

問：書謂「監于先王成憲，其永無愆」，詩謂「不愆不忘，率由舊章」，蓋言祖宗之當法也。伏覩我太宗文皇帝嘗諭羣臣曰：「兹予繼承天位，恪遵成憲。」仁宗昭皇帝亦嘗諭侍臣曰：「守成之主，動法祖宗，斯鮮過舉。」大哉，王言！誠萬世人君之龜鑑也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，奄有萬邦，垂憲立法，盡善盡美，固有非臣下所能周知，亦有非言語所能形容者。姑舉宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》所載君道之大者，如聖孝也，聖學也，敬天也，仁民也，求言也，聽納也，用賢也，勤政也，謹戒也，節儉也。而皇祖之懿德美行，過古帝王遠甚，然於前數者，
translation_en:
Repairing bridges and roads.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Book of Documents says, “Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without fault.” The Book of Odes says, “Neither erring nor forgetting, follow the old rules.” These statements mean that one should take the imperial ancestors as models. We humbly observe that our Emperor Taizong Wen once instructed his ministers: “Now that I have succeeded to the throne of Heaven, I reverently abide by the established statutes.” Emperor Renzong Zhao likewise once instructed his attendant ministers: “If a ruler who preserves an inherited achievement models his every action on his ancestors, he will seldom act amiss.” How great are these royal words! They are truly a guiding mirror for rulers of all ages.

We reflect with profound reverence upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, who rose like a dragon in the Huai region and came to possess the myriad states. The statutes he handed down and the laws he established were perfect in every respect. Certainly, there are aspects that his subjects cannot fully comprehend, and others that words cannot adequately describe. Let us merely cite the principal aspects of the ruler’s Way recorded in the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), imperially composed by Emperor Xuanzong Zhang: sagely filial piety, sagely learning, reverence for Heaven, benevolence toward the people, soliciting counsel, hearing and accepting advice, employing the worthy, diligence in government, vigilance and caution, and frugality. The imperial ancestor’s splendid virtues and admirable conduct far surpassed those of the emperors and kings of antiquity. Yet, with regard to the several aspects just mentioned …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可歷指其實歟抑
今日法
祖之所當先者何在歟諸士子莊誦
聖訓有年請敬陳之毋曰日用由之而不知也
問文章所以傳世政事所以澤物君子所
當尚也三代以上文章政事之兼具者
固毋容議矣姑舉三代以下文章政事
言之夫以四百年之漢文章莫若董仲
舒何以政事不聞於當時三百年之唐
===
文章莫若韓退之何以政事不著于後
世宋之周程張朱皆有文章之名世者
也何以政事僅小試而不大著歟之數
君子者果但有文章而無政事歟抑別
有其故歟論者類謂有文章而無政事
則為腐儒有政事而無文章則為俗吏
然自漢唐宋以來不有文章而措之政
事大有足紀者果可目為俗吏歟不有
政事而發為文章亦有可稱者果可目
punctuated:
可歷指其實歟？抑今日法祖之所當先者何在歟？諸士子莊誦聖訓有年，請敬陳之，毋曰日用由之而不知也。
問：文章所以傳世，政事所以澤物，君子所當尚也。三代以上文章政事之兼具者，固毋容議矣。姑舉三代以下文章政事言之。夫以四百年之漢，文章莫若董仲舒，何以政事不聞於當時？三百年之唐，文章莫若韓退之，何以政事不著于後世？宋之周程張朱，皆有文章之名世者也，何以政事僅小試而不大著歟？之數君子者，果但有文章而無政事歟？抑別有其故歟？論者類謂有文章而無政事，則為腐儒；有政事而無文章，則為俗吏。然自漢唐宋以來，不有文章而措之政事，大有足紀者，果可目為俗吏歟？不有政事而發為文章，亦有可稱者，果可目
translation_en:
…Can you enumerate concrete instances of these virtues? Or what should take precedence today in following the ancestral example? You candidates have solemnly recited the sagely instructions for years. Please set forth your answers respectfully; do not say that you follow them daily without understanding them.
Question: Literary writing is the means of transmitting one's legacy to later generations; government service is the means of extending benefits to others. Both should be esteemed by the gentleman. Those who combined literary accomplishment and governmental achievement in the Three Dynasties and earlier surely need no discussion. Let us consider these two accomplishments after the Three Dynasties. Throughout the four hundred years of the Han, none surpassed Dong Zhongshu in literary writing. Why, then, were his governmental achievements unheard of in his own time? Throughout the three hundred years of the Tang, none surpassed Han Tuizhi in literary writing. Why, then, were his governmental achievements not renowned in later generations? The Song scholars Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu all won renown in their age through their writings. Why were their abilities in government tried only on a small scale, without conspicuous achievements? Did these gentlemen [?] truly possess only literary ability and no ability in government? Or was there some other reason? Commentators commonly say that a man with literary accomplishment but no governmental achievement is a pedantic scholar, while one with governmental achievement but no literary accomplishment is a vulgar functionary. Yet, from the Han, Tang, and Song onward, those who lacked literary accomplishment but applied themselves to government achieved much worthy of record: can they really be called vulgar functionaries? Those who had no governmental achievements but expressed themselves in writing also produced work worthy of praise: can they really be called…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
為腐儒歟抑果全才之難得歟今之所
取法又果安在歟諸士子力學有年發
為文章行將施諸政事願悉陳之毋隱
問字學之關於天下也大矣所以傳經載
道述史記事治百官察萬民而貫通三
才者也始於伏羲之畫卦成於蒼頡之
造書而其所以畫者何因造者何據擊
壤康衢之播其聲二典三謨之傳於世
上而堯舜禹湯文武之為君所以出令
===
者下而臯陶伊傅周召之為臣所以行
君之令而致之民者曾外於此道歟秦
之何燔燒之禍既熾科斗之文不傳有
變大篆而為小篆者有厭篆書而為隸
書者有縮之以簡便華之以姿媚者有
為楷書為行書為草書為飛白者其創
始也各有其人其是非也皆有定在可
詳辯歟夫字者心之畫也人之賢否見
焉治之隆替寓焉古之人執筆而得五
punctuated:
為腐儒歟？抑果全才之難得歟？今之所取法又果安在歟？諸士子力學有年，發為文章，行將施諸政事，願悉陳之，毋隱。

問：字學之關於天下也大矣，所以傳經載道、述史記事、治百官、察萬民，而貫通三才者也。始於伏羲之畫卦，成於蒼頡之造書，而其所以畫者何因，造者何據？擊壤、康衢之播其聲，二典、三謨之傳於世，上而堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之為君，所以出令者，下而臯陶、伊、傅、周、召之為臣，所以行君之令而致之民者，曾外於此道歟？秦之何燔燒之禍既熾，科斗之文不傳，有變大篆而為小篆者，有厭篆書而為隸書者，有縮之以簡便、華之以姿媚者，有為楷書、為行書、為草書、為飛白者。其創始也各有其人，其是非也皆有定在，可詳辯歟？夫字者，心之畫也。人之賢否見焉，治之隆替寓焉。古之人執筆而得五
translation_en:
…be deemed pedantic scholars? Or is it truly difficult to find men of comprehensive talent? Where, then, should we now seek our models? You candidates have devoted years to study and expressed your learning in literary compositions; soon you will apply it to government affairs. Please set out your views fully, withholding nothing.

Question: The study of written characters has great significance for all under Heaven. Through writing, the classics are transmitted and the Way is conveyed, history is composed and events recorded, the hundred officials are governed and the myriad people observed; it connects the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. It began with Fuxi’s drawing of the trigrams and reached completion with Cangjie’s creation of writing. Yet what prompted those drawings, and on what basis was writing created? The songs of “Striking the Ground” and “The Thoroughfare” spread their sounds, and the “Two Canons” and “Three Counsels” were transmitted to later generations. Above, rulers such as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu issued commands; below, ministers such as Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao carried out their rulers’ commands and conveyed them to the people. Did any of this ever fall outside the way of writing?

Once the calamity of book burning under the Qin had raged [?], the tadpole script ceased to be transmitted. Some transformed large-seal script into small-seal script; some, dissatisfied with seal script, produced clerical script. Some abbreviated writing for simplicity and convenience, while others embellished it with grace and charm. Some created standard script, running script, cursive script, or flying-white script. Each originated with a particular person, and their merits and faults each admit of definite judgment. Can you distinguish these in detail?

Written characters are the delineation of the mind. A person’s worthiness or unworthiness is revealed in them, and the flourishing or decline of government is embodied in them. Among the ancients were those who took up the brush and attained the five…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
妙者當時擅草聖之名一字而得八法
者後世加珍藏之重或因掣肘善書之
一事而主為之感悟或因用筆在心之
一言而君為之改容其所繫於家國天
下也亦甚重矣然則其要果何在歟諸
士子游藝有素於此必知之詳矣願明
以告我
問易曰何以聚人曰財是財者誠為國之
命萬事之本國之所以安危事之所以
===
成敗恒必由之也顧其盈虛消息之間
乃有大可疑者請借漢唐之事論之盖
漢室初興天下既定民無盖藏自天子
不能具醇駟將相或乘牛車財力可謂
屈矣然文帝紹統而不見以理財為事
但見今年復民半歲租明年除田之租
稅若太宗之在唐其孜孜恤民亦有然
者凡其所以刻取苛斂如筭舟車榷酒
酤稅間架除陌錢借商錢之類至武帝
punctuated:
妙者，當時擅草聖之名；一字而得八法者，後世加珍藏之重。或因掣肘善書之一事，而主為之感悟；或因用筆在心之一言，而君為之改容。其所繫於家國天下也，亦甚重矣。然則其要果何在歟？諸士子游藝有素，於此必知之詳矣，願明以告我。
問：易曰：「何以聚人？曰財。」是財者，誠為國之命、萬事之本。國之所以安危，事之所以成敗，恒必由之也。顧其盈虛消息之間，乃有大可疑者，請借漢唐之事論之。盖漢室初興，天下既定，民無盖藏，自天子不能具醇駟，將相或乘牛車，財力可謂屈矣。然文帝紹統，而不見以理財為事，但見今年復民半歲租，明年除田之租稅。若太宗之在唐，其孜孜恤民，亦有然者。凡其所以刻取苛斂，如筭舟車、榷酒酤、稅間架、除陌錢、借商錢之類，至武帝
translation_en:
…the five marvels won, in their own day, the reputation of a sage of cursive script; those who mastered the eight methods through a single character were accorded the honor of being treasured by later generations. In one instance, the incident of tugging at the elbow of someone skilled in writing brought a ruler to a realization; in another, the remark that using the brush rests in the heart caused a sovereign’s expression to change. The implications for the family, the state, and all under Heaven are indeed profound. Where, then, does the essential point truly lie? You candidates have long cultivated the arts and must understand this matter thoroughly. I hope you will explain it clearly to me.
Question: The Book of Changes says: “How does one gather people together? Through wealth.” Wealth is truly the lifeblood of the state and the foundation of all affairs. The security or peril of the state and the success or failure of its undertakings invariably depend upon it. Yet the waxing and waning of wealth present matters that invite considerable doubt. Let us discuss them through events of the Han and Tang dynasties. When the Han ruling house first arose and the realm had been pacified, the people had no reserves. Even the Son of Heaven could not assemble a team of four horses of matching color, and generals and chief ministers sometimes rode in ox carts. Financial resources could certainly be called exhausted. Yet when Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, we do not find him making fiscal management his concern. We see only that one year he exempted the people from half a year’s land tax, and the next abolished the land tax. Emperor Taizong of the Tang likewise showed such tireless concern for the people. As for harsh exactions and oppressive levies—such as taxes on boats and carts, the monopoly on the sale of liquor, taxes assessed on the bays of buildings, deductions from cash transactions, and forced loans from merchants—these appeared only with Emperor Wu…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德宗而後見焉夫漢文唐宗宜其不足
而乃有餘武帝德宗宜其有餘而乃不
足其故何耶
國家財賦之制一倣于古量入為出固未嘗
乏也夫何比年以來司農之藏少府之
用或至告匱將欲務為寬恤乎則軍國
之需無以給將欲肆加征榷乎則意外
之虞亦當慮古人有謂豐財之道當去
其害財者而有三冗之說其果然歟其
===
於
今日之理財亦有所裨否歟昔趙充國計河
湟得三百斛可以制羌人不敢動諸葛
亮用兵如神而以糧道不繼屢出無功
方
今四方已寧實
皇上盛德固無事乎用師也然有備無患又
國家所當預講而博籌者爾諸生懷奇有素
願言漢唐所以有餘不足之故而及
punctuated:
德宗而後見焉。夫漢文、唐宗，宜其不足而乃有餘；武帝、德宗，宜其有餘而乃不足，其故何耶？

國家財賦之制，一倣于古，量入為出，固未嘗乏也。夫何比年以來，司農之藏、少府之用，或至告匱？將欲務為寬恤乎，則軍國之需無以給；將欲肆加征榷乎，則意外之虞亦當慮。古人有謂豐財之道當去其害財者，而有三冗之說，其果然歟？其於今日之理財，亦有所裨否歟？昔趙充國計河湟，得三百斛，可以制羌人不敢動；諸葛亮用兵如神，而以糧道不繼，屢出無功。方今四方已寧，實皇上盛德，固無事乎用師也。然有備無患，又國家所當預講而博籌者。爾諸生懷奇有素，願言漢唐所以有餘不足之故，而及
translation_en:
…and Dezong before these practices appeared. Emperor Wen of Han and Emperor Taizong of Tang ought to have had insufficient resources, yet they had a surplus; Emperor Wu and Emperor Dezong ought to have had a surplus, yet their resources were insufficient. What accounts for this?

The state's system of revenue and taxation follows ancient practice throughout, determining expenditure according to income; indeed, resources were never lacking. Why, then, in recent years have the stores of the Grand Minister of Agriculture and the funds available to the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues sometimes been reported exhausted? If we seek to concentrate on easing the people's burdens, we lack the means to meet military and state requirements; if we seek to impose additional levies and monopoly taxes freely, we must also consider the danger of unforeseen trouble. The ancients said that the way to enrich the treasury was to remove whatever impaired its resources, and spoke of the “three redundancies.” Is this indeed so? Might this also benefit the management of finances today? Formerly, Zhao Chongguo, in making plans for the He-Huang region, obtained three hundred hu of grain [?], enabling him to hold the Qiang in check so that they dared not stir. Zhuge Liang conducted military operations with almost divine skill, yet because his grain supply routes could not be maintained, his repeated expeditions achieved nothing. Today, all quarters of the realm are at peace, truly owing to His Majesty's abundant virtue, and there is certainly no occasion to employ armies. Nevertheless, preparedness averts calamity: this too is something the state ought to discuss beforehand and plan for comprehensively. You students have long possessed exceptional talents. I ask you to explain why resources were sufficient or insufficient under the Han and Tang, and to extend your discussion to…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今日理財之宜用以聞於司國計者當亦有
所酌處於其間矣
問兵凶戰危固非學者之所常言至於禦
暴禁亂之策亦學者之所當究心者姑
與論其一二兵所以衛國必屬之於將
將所以統兵必務於得人是強兵要在
乎擇將也審矣先正云賢材居上士卒
處下人安其業是以無敵我
孝宗敬皇帝臨御之日開科以求將材儀式首
===
制迨今
皇上嗣大歷服用廷臣議定儀式每每欲萃天
下之優於將材者于
京師為統兵衛國計誠萬世不刊之
盛典也夫將之論不一而兵之論亦不一故
將有八材而何又有八弊歟將德有五
而何又有八惡歟將善有五而何又有
四欲歟兵強有四而何又有五戒歟武
德有七而何又有七禁歟兵勢有三而
punctuated:
今日理財之宜，用以聞於司國計者，當亦有所酌處於其間矣。
問：兵凶戰危，固非學者之所常言；至於禦暴禁亂之策，亦學者之所當究心者。姑與論其一二。兵所以衛國，必屬之於將；將所以統兵，必務於得人。是強兵要在乎擇將也，審矣。先正云：「賢材居上，士卒處下，人安其業，是以無敵。」我孝宗敬皇帝臨御之日，開科以求將材，儀式首制。迨今皇上嗣大歷服，用廷臣議定儀式，每每欲萃天下之優於將材者于京師，為統兵衛國計，誠萬世不刊之盛典也。夫將之論不一，而兵之論亦不一。故將有八材，而何又有八弊歟？將德有五，而何又有八惡歟？將善有五，而何又有四欲歟？兵強有四，而何又有五戒歟？武德有七，而何又有七禁歟？兵勢有三，而
translation_en:
…the appropriate ways to manage finances today, so that these may be brought to the attention of those responsible for state finances. They should then find matters among your proposals to weigh and act upon.
Policy question: Arms are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is perilous; these are certainly not subjects that scholars ordinarily discuss. Yet strategies for resisting violence and suppressing disorder are also matters to which scholars ought to devote their minds. Let us discuss one or two of these. Troops serve to defend the state and must be entrusted to generals; generals serve to command troops, and every effort must be made to secure suitable men. It is therefore clear that the key to strengthening an army lies in selecting its generals. A worthy predecessor said: “When worthy and talented men occupy the higher positions, and officers and soldiers occupy the lower, each is secure in his occupation; hence they are invincible.” During the reign of our Emperor Xiaozong Jing, examinations were instituted to seek talent for generalship, and their procedures were first established. Now that His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial mandate, he has adopted procedures deliberated upon and settled by his court officials, repeatedly seeking to gather at the capital those throughout the realm who excel in talent for generalship, as a means of providing for the command of troops and the defense of the state. This is truly a magnificent institution, to stand unaltered for ten thousand generations. There is more than one account of generalship, and likewise more than one account of military affairs. Thus, generals have eight talents; why, then, are there also eight failings? Generals have five virtues; why are there also eight evils? Generals have five strengths; why are there also four things they should desire? There are four ways in which an army is strong; why are there also five cautions? There are seven martial virtues; why are there also seven prohibitions? There are three forms of strategic advantage, and…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
何又有三機歟顧廣西百粤用武之地
猺獞出没之鄉先世有自奮威武而擊
曹成之寇者有忠義勇敢而戢儂賊之
兵者有歐陽脩薦其智略可任將軍者
有狄青薦其驍勇而破儂賊者有稱其
為文武兼全者有稱其為一代名將者
可歷指其人歟果將材將德將善之足
錄歟果兵强武德兵勢之足法歟諸士
子佩服
===
聖訓景仰前哲於將兵必知之詳於名賢必考
之精側陋之中豈無非熊伏龍而深知
擇將用兵之略者乎我懷若人適其有
遇用將轉而薦之于
上庶竭區區以人事君之忠
punctuated: 何又有三機歟？顧廣西百粤，用武之地，猺獞出没之鄉。先世有自奮威武而擊曹成之寇者，有忠義勇敢而戢儂賊之兵者，有歐陽脩薦其智略可任將軍者，有狄青薦其驍勇而破儂賊者，有稱其為文武兼全者，有稱其為一代名將者，可歷指其人歟？果將材、將德、將善之足錄歟？果兵强、武德、兵勢之足法歟？諸士子佩服聖訓，景仰前哲，於將兵必知之詳，於名賢必考之精。側陋之中，豈無非熊、伏龍而深知擇將用兵之略者乎？我懷若人，適其有遇，用將轉而薦之于上，庶竭區區以人事君之忠。
translation_en:
…why, then, are there also three critical opportunities? Consider Guangxi, the land of the Hundred Yue: a region for military operations, where the Yao and Tong peoples appear and disappear. In earlier generations, there was one who displayed martial prowess on his own initiative and attacked Cao Cheng’s bandits; one who, with loyalty, righteousness, courage, and daring, subdued the forces of the rebel Nong; one whom Ouyang Xiu recommended as possessing the intelligence and strategic ability to serve as a general; and one whom Di Qing recommended for his valor, who defeated the rebel Nong. There was one praised as accomplished in both civil and military affairs, and one acclaimed as a renowned general of his age. Can you identify each of these men in turn? Did they indeed possess abilities, virtues, and strengths as commanders worthy of recording? Did they indeed offer models of military strength, martial virtue, and strategic disposition worthy of emulation?

You candidates take the sagely instructions to heart and revere the worthies of the past. You must therefore possess detailed knowledge of commanders and warfare and have studied eminent worthies closely. Among those living in humble obscurity, might there not be a ‘Non-Bear’ or a ‘Crouching Dragon’—a Taigong or a Zhuge Liang—with a profound understanding of how to select commanders and employ troops? I long for such men. Should I happen to encounter them, I intend in turn to recommend them to the throne, hoping thereby to fulfill my humble loyalty in serving my ruler by presenting worthy men.

同考試官教諭方批大學一題最為冠冕
塲中士子體貼不真率多蹈襲此作認理
精到且氣充文贍無一陳腐語宜録以式
後學
同考試官學正陳批傳註自明白作者多
冗泛可厭惟此篇親切有味無一長語其必
深於理學者
考試官教諭姜批就理說辭發明透徹
千篇一律中僅得此卷亟當付諸梓也
考試官教諭張批明明德止至善之實
必如此咏嘆乃足
傳者釋詩言君子所得之極而所感之深也蓋

其感民之不忘殆自有不容已者乎傳者引淇
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

道盛德至善民之不能忘也。

王珵

同考試官教諭方批：「大學一題最為冠冕，塲中士子體貼不真，率多蹈襲。此作認理精到，且氣充文贍，無一陳腐語，宜録以式後學。」

考試官教諭張批：「明明德、止至善之實，必如此咏嘆乃足。」
