title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
間盖必本思惟之眷顧發而為禮貌之慇懃根
意念之懇切形而為恩遇之隆重表裏一致而
不飾之以偽迨見為臣者瞻顏色而知其所存
吾君之視我以手足者固瞭然於心目之間望
容貌而知其所蘊吾君之寄我以耳目者已洞
然於形迹之表是非臆度也誠之見信於其臣
者然耳謂非人君待臣之誠可乎若夫臣位乎
下其分若天淵宜不可述而志也然其所以事
夫君者厥職允脩而心無自欺厥業克崇而志
===
靡有懈盖必言焉有物而堅秉一念之精忠行
焉有恪而貞守一己之雅操始終一轍而不文
之以欺迨見為君者嘉其志而明著其美鞠躬
盡瘁之成勳不徒見之稱揚將勒之金石而不
磨歆其心而論譔其德矢心竭力之就緒非徒
形之美慕將施之鼎彝而不泯是非溢美也誠
之感孚於其君者然耳謂非人臣事君之誠可
乎夫君臣之相與不離於一誠如此此所以上
下交而成一德之盛也歟嗟夫君臣一體也上
punctuated: 間。盖必本思惟之眷顧，發而為禮貌之慇懃；根意念之懇切，形而為恩遇之隆重。表裏一致，而不飾之以偽。迨見為臣者瞻顏色而知其所存，吾君之視我以手足者，固瞭然於心目之間；望容貌而知其所蘊，吾君之寄我以耳目者，已洞然於形迹之表。是非臆度也，誠之見信於其臣者然耳。謂非人君待臣之誠，可乎？若夫臣位乎下，其分若天淵，宜不可述而志也。然其所以事夫君者，厥職允脩而心無自欺，厥業克崇而志靡有懈。盖必言焉有物，而堅秉一念之精忠；行焉有恪，而貞守一己之雅操。始終一轍，而不文之以欺。迨見為君者嘉其志而明著其美，鞠躬盡瘁之成勳，不徒見之稱揚，將勒之金石而不磨；歆其心而論譔其德，矢心竭力之就緒，非徒形之美慕，將施之鼎彝而不泯。是非溢美也，誠之感孚於其君者然耳。謂非人臣事君之誠，可乎？夫君臣之相與不離於一誠如此，此所以上下交而成一德之盛也歟！嗟夫！君臣一體也，上
translation_en:
…no estrangement. The ruler must ground his attentive regard in his thoughts and express it through courteous and solicitous treatment; he must root his intentions in earnestness and manifest them through generous favor. His outward conduct and inward feelings are consistent, without any adornment of falsehood. Thus his ministers, observing his expression, recognize what is in his mind: that their ruler regards them as his hands and feet is plainly apparent to their minds and eyes. Looking upon his countenance, they recognize what he holds within: that their ruler entrusts them with serving as his ears and eyes is already evident in his outward bearing. This is no conjecture; it is simply that his sincerity has won his ministers’ trust. Can this be called anything other than a ruler’s sincerity in treating his ministers?
As for the minister, whose position is below, the difference in standing between him and his ruler is like that between heaven and the depths. It might seem that he could not be spoken of and commemorated. Yet in serving his ruler, he faithfully discharges his duties without deceiving himself, and advances his work without allowing his resolve to slacken. His words must have substance, and he must firmly maintain his single-minded, pure loyalty; his actions must be reverent, and he must steadfastly preserve his upright personal conduct. He follows the same course from beginning to end, without embellishing it with deception. Thus the ruler commends his resolve and makes his excellence manifest. His achievements in bowing himself to his task and exhausting all his strength will not merely receive praise: they will be inscribed on metal and stone, never to be effaced. The ruler admires his heart and sets down an account of his virtue. What he has accomplished by pledging his heart and exerting all his strength will not merely evoke admiration: it will be recorded on sacrificial vessels, never to disappear. This is no excessive praise; it is simply that his sincerity has moved his ruler and won his trust. Can this be called anything other than a minister’s sincerity in serving his ruler?
When ruler and ministers associate with one another in this way, never departing from sincerity alone, is this not what enables those above and below to unite and achieve the flourishing condition of sharing a single virtue? Ah! Ruler and ministers form one body; those above…

text:

而志則上惑上下疑惑而能有為於天下未之
有也故唐虞之世曰都曰俞于一堂之上君臣

之所能及也然成王聖君也周公聖臣也猶不

曰君使臣以禮臣事君以忠

下一心也。若上不可望而知，則下疑；下不可述而志，則上惑。上下疑惑而能有為於天下，未之有也。故唐虞之世，曰都曰俞，于一堂之上，君臣相得，若家人父子然。宜其治隆俗美，而非後世之所能及也。然成王聖君也，周公聖臣也，猶不免於東土之避，則後世宜若之何？殆必如孔子曰：「君使臣以禮，臣事君以忠。」

translation_en:
… those above and below are of one mind. If the ruler cannot be understood through observation, those below become doubtful; if the ministers’ deeds cannot be recounted and recorded, the ruler becomes perplexed. Never have rulers and ministers beset by doubt and perplexity been able to accomplish anything in the realm. Thus, in the age of Tang and Yu, expressions of approval and assent rang out within a single hall; ruler and ministers enjoyed a mutual understanding like that of fathers and sons within a family. It was fitting that their government should flourish and their customs be admirable, beyond anything later ages could attain. Yet King Cheng was a sage ruler and the Duke of Zhou a sage minister, and still the latter could not avoid withdrawing to the eastern lands. What, then, should later generations do? Surely they must follow Confucius’s words: “The ruler employs his ministers according to ritual propriety; ministers serve their ruler with loyalty.”

“Dwelling in the Broad Dwelling of the World”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The principle of the ‘broad dwelling’ is exceedingly vast and most difficult to write about. This essay proceeds with sustained vigor for well over a thousand words, yet every word and every sentence addresses the topic. It seems effortless, arising naturally from an intuitive grasp. title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
高古認理親切措詞滂沛僅見此篇得士如子
可以貢之於
上矣
以至大無形之居而屬之大丈夫能居焉當于
其心與理而求之也何則居而有形則居為有
限不能出宇宙之外居之小者也乃若居之其
體無形其大無外有囊括宇宙之具盖大之至
可以居名而不可以居求者苟本自其心與理
而求之吾見茫昧恍忽卒至於莫可致詰之地
===
何能得其大之的而見其居之安真有以度越
於尋常萬萬也哉天下之廣居者何仁是也
即所謂理也無形之居也居之至大可以居名
而不可以居求者也居之者何大丈夫之心也
大丈夫弘是心而居此廣居則天地萬物皆吾
胷中物矣回視區區功利之徒直妾婦耳何足
以語此噫大哉孟子斯言邃於道之言也即其
言而求其所以言盖非但闢景春之陋見實所
以牖當時之人心非但牖當時之人心實所以
punctuated:
高古，認理親切，措詞滂沛，僅見此篇。得士如子，可以貢之於上矣。

以至大無形之居，而屬之大丈夫能居焉，當于其心與理而求之也。何則？居而有形，則居為有限，不能出宇宙之外，居之小者也。乃若居之其體無形，其大無外，有囊括宇宙之具，盖大之至，可以居名而不可以居求者。苟本自其心與理而求之，吾見茫昧恍忽，卒至於莫可致詰之地，何能得其大之的，而見其居之安，真有以度越於尋常萬萬也哉？天下之廣居者何？仁是也，即所謂理也，無形之居也，居之至大，可以居名而不可以居求者也。居之者何？大丈夫之心也。大丈夫弘是心而居此廣居，則天地萬物皆吾胷中物矣。回視區區功利之徒，直妾婦耳，何足以語此？噫！大哉，孟子斯言！邃於道之言也。即其言而求其所以言，盖非但闢景春之陋見，實所以牖當時之人心；非但牖當時之人心，實所以
translation_en:
…lofty and antique in conception, intimate and precise in grasping principle, and abundant in expression: only this essay meets these standards. Having obtained a scholar like you, we may recommend him to the throne.

When a dwelling of utmost vastness, without physical form, is assigned to the great man as something he can inhabit, we must seek its meaning in his mind and in principle. Why? If a dwelling has physical form, it is bounded and cannot extend beyond the universe: it is a small dwelling. But a dwelling whose substance is formless and whose vastness has no bounds possesses the capacity to encompass the universe. It is vast in the utmost degree: it may be called a dwelling, but cannot be sought as a physical dwelling. If one seeks it on the basis of one's mind and principle [?], I foresee obscurity and confusion, ending in a realm where nothing can be examined or questioned. How could one then grasp precisely wherein its vastness lies and perceive the peace of dwelling there, truly surpassing the ordinary ten thousandfold?

What is the spacious dwelling of all under Heaven? It is benevolence: what we call principle, a dwelling without form. It is the vastest of dwellings, which may be called a dwelling but cannot be sought as a physical dwelling. What inhabits it? The mind of the great man. When the great man expands this mind and inhabits this spacious dwelling, Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things all lie within his breast. Looking back upon those petty pursuers of achievement and profit, they are merely concubines and wives. How could they be worthy of discussing this? Ah, how great are these words of Mengzi! They are words profound in the Way. If we examine his words and seek why he uttered them, they were surely intended not merely to refute Jing Chun's narrow views, but to enlighten the minds of the people of his time; not merely to enlighten the minds of the people of his time, but indeed to…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
自任吾道之深不得已而發此言也請畢其說
道器之判久矣愚聞之形而上者謂之道形而
下者謂之器立人之道曰仁與義仁固道之大
也形而上者也初不滯於形而可以器名者也
孟子以仁為天下之廣居不幾指器為道混道
器於無別而道也器也將可比而同之乎吁有
是哉聖賢立言各有攸當泥其言而不究其旨
其不悖聖賢之本意者幾希仁道至大不可名
貌天下之廣居盖亦本仁道之全體擬議彷彿
===
以不可限量之名而名其不可名貌者耳非滯
於形也詎可徇其名不究其實致泥於道器之
說而謂仁非天下之廣居耶何也天地生物流
行不息之心而人生得之以為心焉即仁也即
資始之乾元資生之坤元也善之長也合天下
之理而一之者也貫天下之人與物而無間者
也歛之不盈一掬放之則包四海彌六合舉天
下而莫能加者具於性分為無形之居盖居極
天下之廣而廣莫有廣焉者也是廣居也藏於
punctuated: 自任吾道之深，不得已而發此言也。請畢其說。道器之判久矣。愚聞之，形而上者謂之道，形而下者謂之器。立人之道曰仁與義。仁固道之大也，形而上者也，初不滯於形而可以器名者也。孟子以仁為天下之廣居，不幾指器為道，混道器於無別，而道也器也，將可比而同之乎？吁！有是哉？聖賢立言，各有攸當。泥其言而不究其旨，其不悖聖賢之本意者幾希。仁道至大，不可名貌。天下之廣居，盖亦本仁道之全體，擬議彷彿，以不可限量之名而名其不可名貌者耳，非滯於形也。詎可徇其名，不究其實，致泥於道器之說，而謂仁非天下之廣居耶？何也？天地生物流行不息之心，而人生得之以為心焉，即仁也，即資始之乾元、資生之坤元也，善之長也，合天下之理而一之者也，貫天下之人與物而無間者也。歛之不盈一掬，放之則包四海，彌六合，舉天下而莫能加者，具於性分，為無形之居。盖居極天下之廣，而廣莫有廣焉者也。是廣居也，藏於
translation_en: …his profound commitment to taking responsibility for our Way compelled him to utter these words. Allow me to complete the explanation. The distinction between the Way and concrete things has long been established. I have heard it said: “What is above physical form is called the Way; what is below physical form is called a concrete thing.” And: “The way of humanity is established through benevolence and righteousness.” Benevolence is indeed the greatness of the Way; it is above physical form. From the outset, it is not confined to form such that it could be called a concrete thing. When Mengzi calls benevolence “the spacious dwelling of the world,” does he not come close to identifying a concrete thing as the Way, confusing the two until no distinction remains, so that the Way and concrete things may be equated? Ah! Could this be so? When sages and worthies formulate their teachings, each expression has its appropriate application. Those who cling to their words without examining their meaning rarely avoid contradicting their original intent. The way of benevolence is supremely great and cannot be named or pictured. “The spacious dwelling of the world” is simply an approximate analogy based on the entire substance of the way of benevolence: a name signifying something immeasurable is used to name what cannot be named or pictured. It does not confine benevolence to physical form. How could one follow the name without examining the reality, become mired in distinctions between the Way and concrete things, and then assert that benevolence is not the spacious dwelling of the world? Why is this so? The heart by which Heaven and Earth generate living things, flowing ceaselessly, is what human beings receive at birth as their own heart: this is benevolence. It is the primal power of Qian, from which all things receive their beginning, and the primal power of Kun, from which all things receive life. It is the foremost of all goodness, uniting all the principles of the world into one and pervading all people and things without interruption. Gathered in, it does not fill a single handful; released, it encompasses the Four Seas and fills the six directions. Nothing in the whole world can surpass it. Inherent in our endowed nature, it constitutes a dwelling without physical form. This dwelling reaches the utmost spaciousness in the world, with nothing more spacious than it. This spacious dwelling is concealed within…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
大始隱於渾淪天開地闢而人生焉此居固已
弘博融漾巍巍乎凌日星而摩霄漢崢嶸於天
地間矣培植于唐虞脩復于夏商粉飾潤澤於
文武周孔歷春秋而戰國相攘相奪風靡波蕩
加之為我之楊兼愛之墨自立門户從旁竊據
此居之在天下幾於決裂覆墜非復舊物所幸
衛之有人而彼不得肆其說柰之何世變江河
愈趨愈下不入於異端則趨於功利遂使儀衍
之徒得以横行天下售縱横捭闔之說摇唇鼓
===
舌求逞一日之快設藩籬立町畦分尓我限疆
界羣天下之人卑卑瑣瑣不知廣居為何事相
率而入於小丈夫之域肯堂者誰歟肯構者誰
歟勤垣墉而塗塈茨者誰歟堂堂廣居門墻掃
迹莽然一荒丘也不有大丈夫誰則居之大丈
夫何如而居之也其氣清其質粹其心純一而
無為其意不云乎仰而觀乾吾父也吾廣居之
資始俯而察坤吾母也吾廣居之資生天地之塞
吾廣居之槖籥天地之帥吾廣居之根柢惜曰不
punctuated:
大始，隱於渾淪，天開地闢而人生焉，此居固已弘博融漾，巍巍乎凌日星而摩霄漢，崢嶸於天地間矣。培植于唐虞，脩復于夏商，粉飾潤澤於文武周孔。歷春秋而戰國，相攘相奪，風靡波蕩；加之為我之楊、兼愛之墨，自立門户，從旁竊據，此居之在天下幾於決裂覆墜，非復舊物。所幸衛之有人，而彼不得肆其說。柰之何世變江河，愈趨愈下，不入於異端，則趨於功利，遂使儀衍之徒得以横行天下，售縱横捭闔之說，摇唇鼓舌，求逞一日之快，設藩籬，立町畦，分尓我，限疆界。羣天下之人卑卑瑣瑣，不知廣居為何事，相率而入於小丈夫之域。肯堂者誰歟？肯構者誰歟？勤垣墉而塗塈茨者誰歟？堂堂廣居，門墻掃迹，莽然一荒丘也。不有大丈夫，誰則居之？
大丈夫何如而居之也？其氣清，其質粹，其心純一而無為。其意不云乎：「仰而觀乾，吾父也，吾廣居之資始；俯而察坤，吾母也，吾廣居之資生。天地之塞，吾廣居之槖籥；天地之帥，吾廣居之根柢。」惜曰：「不
translation_en:
…in the Great Beginning, concealed within primordial undifferentiation. When Heaven opened and Earth unfolded and human beings came into existence, this dwelling was already vast, expansive, and all-embracing, towering above sun and stars, brushing the celestial heights, and standing majestically between Heaven and Earth. It was cultivated in the ages of Tang and Yu, restored under Xia and Shang, and adorned and enriched by Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. Through the Spring and Autumn period and into the Warring States, men encroached upon and despoiled one another, swept along like grass before the wind or tossed by waves. Added to this were Yang Zhu’s doctrine of acting for oneself and Mo Di’s doctrine of impartial care: they established their own schools and furtively encroached upon this dwelling from the side. Its existence in the world came close to being torn apart and overthrown, leaving it no longer what it had been. Fortunately, someone defended it, so that those men could not give their doctrines free rein. Yet what could be done when the changing world, like rivers flowing onward, descended ever lower? Those who did not enter heterodoxy pursued achievement and profit. Thus men such as Zhang Yi and Gongsun Yan were able to range unchecked throughout the world, peddling doctrines of vertical and horizontal alliances and the arts of diplomatic persuasion, wagging their lips and tongues to seek the gratification of a single day. They erected fences, marked out plots, distinguished you from me, and imposed boundaries. The people of the world became petty and trifling, unaware of what the spacious dwelling meant, and led one another into the domain of lesser men. Who was willing to build the hall? Who was willing to raise its frame? Who would labor over its walls, plaster it, and thatch its roof? Of that stately, spacious dwelling, the gates and walls had vanished without a trace: it was nothing but a desolate, overgrown mound. Without a great man, who could dwell there?
What must a great man be like to dwell there? His vital energy is clear, his constitution refined, and his heart pure, undivided, and free of contrived action. Does he not think thus: “Looking upward, I behold Qian, Heaven: it is my father, the source from which my spacious dwelling takes its beginning. Looking downward, I examine Kun, Earth: it is my mother, the source from which my spacious dwelling receives life. That which fills Heaven and Earth is the bellows of my spacious dwelling; that which commands Heaven and Earth is its root and foundation.” He says with regret [?]: “If one does not…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
體乾父坤母之心曠此廣居而弗居焉天地民
物將判乎與我不相管攝不相聯屬朋分角立
不能融為一家之春則天地不才之子也悖德
之子也天地之所以生我者何如賦我者何如
委重而責成於我者何如顧自暴自棄而卒之
自小如此焉忍乎不忍乎於是體乾元資始之
心以為心法坤元資生之德以為德講貫於廣
居者有素涵養於廣居者有本操存而踐履於
廣居者有依闢其門升其堂入其室始之以灑
===
掃應對而終之以精義入神之妙先之以格致
誠正而後之以聖神功化之極聲色貨利土木
甲兵異端邪說交攻羣擾抵隙投閒欲為吾廣
居之害焉者蓋種種也一屏而逐之根株悉拔
邪穢盡滌使之降伏退聽無一得肆其害於吾
之廣居而吾得以安居其間褒衣博帶吾廣居
之衣冠言動也闊步長趨吾廣居之升降俛仰
也周情孔思帝驟王馳吾廣居之經綸康濟也
一視而同仁天下吾廣居一家也大觀而無我
punctuated: 體乾父坤母之心，曠此廣居而弗居焉，天地民物將判乎與我不相管攝，不相聯屬，朋分角立，不能融為一家之春，則天地不才之子也，悖德之子也。天地之所以生我者何如？賦我者何如？委重而責成於我者何如？顧自暴自棄，而卒之自小如此，焉忍乎？不忍乎？於是體乾元資始之心以為心，法坤元資生之德以為德。講貫於廣居者有素，涵養於廣居者有本，操存而踐履於廣居者有依。闢其門，升其堂，入其室，始之以灑掃應對，而終之以精義入神之妙；先之以格致誠正，而後之以聖神功化之極。聲色貨利、土木甲兵、異端邪說，交攻羣擾，抵隙投閒，欲為吾廣居之害焉者，蓋種種也。一屏而逐之，根株悉拔，邪穢盡滌，使之降伏退聽，無一得肆其害於吾之廣居，而吾得以安居其間。褒衣博帶，吾廣居之衣冠言動也；闊步長趨，吾廣居之升降俛仰也；周情孔思，帝驟王馳，吾廣居之經綸康濟也。一視而同仁，天下吾廣居一家也；大觀而無我
translation_en:
…embody the heart of Qian as father and Kun as mother, leaving this spacious dwelling vacant and failing to inhabit it, then Heaven and Earth, the people and all things will become severed from me, without mutual oversight or connection. Divided into factions and standing opposed, they will be unable to unite in the springtime warmth of one family. I would then be an unworthy child of Heaven and Earth, a child who violates their virtue. What was the purpose for which Heaven and Earth gave me life? What have they endowed me with? What weighty charge have they entrusted to me, holding me responsible for its fulfillment? Yet I would cast myself away and abandon myself, ultimately diminishing myself like this. Could I bear it? Could I not?

Thus I take as my own heart the heart of Qian’s primal power, from which all things receive their beginning, and model my virtue on the virtue of Kun’s primal power, from which all things receive life. My study and thorough understanding within the spacious dwelling have long been established; my nurturing of myself within it has a foundation; and my preservation of the moral mind and practical conduct within it have something on which to rely. I open its gate, ascend its hall, and enter its inner chamber. I begin with sprinkling and sweeping, answering and responding, and conclude with the subtle mastery of refining moral principles and penetrating the numinous. I start with investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind, and proceed to the ultimate achievements and transforming influence of sagehood and spiritual perfection.

Music and sensual pleasures, wealth and profit, construction projects and warfare, heterodox doctrines and perverse teachings—all attack together and create disorder, exploiting cracks and seeking openings. The things that would harm my spacious dwelling are indeed manifold. I reject and expel them all, uprooting every root and stem and washing away all perversity and impurity. I make them submit, withdraw, and obey, so that none can inflict its harm upon my spacious dwelling, and I can dwell peacefully within it. Loose robes and broad sashes are the dress, speech, and conduct of my spacious dwelling. Broad strides and long, quick steps are its ascending and descending, bowing and looking up. The sentiments of the Duke of Zhou and the thoughts of Confucius, hastening along the paths of the ancient emperors and kings, are its ordering of affairs and its work of bringing peace and relief. Regarding everyone equally and extending benevolence to all, I take all under Heaven as one family in my spacious dwelling. Viewing things comprehensively and without self…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中國吾廣居一人也天下之民老者少者愚闇
者强梁者柔懦者顛連而無告者吾廣居之同
胞也衣之食之教之治之裁之引之無一而不
囿之廣居之中天下之物飛者走者潜者躍者
形色而夭喬者吾廣居之黨與也撙之節之愛
之養之對而育之無一而不納諸廣居之內以
四海則咸熙也以六合則同春也達而在上居
此廣居而與民由之一堯之其仁如天也舜之其
德好生也湯之克仁文之止仁也窮而在下居此
===
廣居而獨善其身一孔之安仁也顏之不違仁也
夷齊之求仁得仁也富貴不能淫此廣居貧賤不
能移此廣居威武不能屈此廣居軒軒磊磊光
明俊偉天地可叅化育可賛為往聖繼絕學為
萬世開太平真有以拓吾廣居之規模仰副天
地所以付畀之重與其所以責望之厚不愧不
怍挺乎振古之人豪天地間一克肖子也所謂
大丈夫者其事業如此其氣象如此視彼淺襟
狹量管見鄙識持捭闔睢詐之術鼓唇吻而懼
punctuated: 中國，吾廣居一人也。天下之民，老者、少者、愚闇者、强梁者、柔懦者、顛連而無告者，吾廣居之同胞也。衣之、食之、教之、治之、裁之、引之，無一而不囿之廣居之中。天下之物，飛者、走者、潜者、躍者、形色而夭喬者，吾廣居之黨與也。撙之、節之、愛之、養之，對而育之，無一而不納諸廣居之內。以四海則咸熙也，以六合則同春也。達而在上，居此廣居而與民由之，一堯之其仁如天也，舜之其德好生也，湯之克仁、文之止仁也。窮而在下，居此廣居而獨善其身，一孔之安仁也，顏之不違仁也，夷齊之求仁得仁也。富貴不能淫此廣居，貧賤不能移此廣居，威武不能屈此廣居。軒軒磊磊，光明俊偉，天地可叅，化育可賛，為往聖繼絕學，為萬世開太平，真有以拓吾廣居之規模，仰副天地所以付畀之重與其所以責望之厚，不愧不怍，挺乎振古之人豪，天地間一克肖子也。所謂大丈夫者，其事業如此，其氣象如此。視彼淺襟狹量、管見鄙識，持捭闔睢詐之術，鼓唇吻而懼
translation_en:
…The people of the Central Realm are as one person within my spacious dwelling. All the people under Heaven—the old and the young, the ignorant and benighted, the forceful and overbearing, the weak and timid, and those suffering hardship with no one to appeal to—are my siblings within this spacious dwelling. I clothe and feed them, teach and govern them, regulate and guide them, leaving none outside its bounds. All things under Heaven—those that fly, run, swim beneath the waters, or leap, and plants of varied forms and colors, low-growing or tall—are my companions within this spacious dwelling. I exercise restraint and moderation in using them, cherish and nourish them, and nurture them according to their needs, leaving none outside this spacious dwelling. Throughout the Four Seas, all flourish; throughout the six directions, all share one spring.

When successful and occupying high office, one inhabits this spacious dwelling and follows the Way together with the people: this is one with Yao, whose benevolence was like Heaven; Shun, whose virtue cherished life; Tang, who was capable of benevolence; and King Wen, who rested in benevolence. When thwarted and in a lowly position, one inhabits this spacious dwelling and perfects oneself alone: this is one with Confucius, who was at ease in benevolence; Yan Hui, who did not depart from benevolence; and Boyi and Shuqi, who sought benevolence and attained it. Wealth and rank cannot corrupt this spacious dwelling; poverty and low status cannot dislodge it; force and might cannot make it yield. Lofty and upright, radiant and outstanding, one can stand alongside Heaven and Earth and assist their transforming and nurturing work, carry on the interrupted learning of the sages of the past, and inaugurate Great Peace for all generations. One can truly enlarge the scope of this spacious dwelling, looking upward to fulfill the weighty trust bestowed by Heaven and Earth and the profound expectations they place upon one. Without shame or remorse, one stands forth as a heroic figure of all antiquity, a son between Heaven and Earth who truly takes after his parents. Such are the achievements and such is the bearing of the one called a great man. Compare him with those of shallow sympathies and narrow capacity, restricted vision and mean understanding, who employ techniques of political manipulation and deceit [?], wagging their lips to intimidate…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸侯直淺淺小丈夫者之為耳烏可挈而與之
同日語哉抑孟子斯言或者謂恐近於兼愛之
說此蓋不知孟子抑豈善讀孟子者乎理一而
分殊程朱之論備矣居天下之廣居理之一也
由此而天下之正位立焉天下之大道行焉品
級隆殺施為緩急固自有截然而不可紊者存
焉蓋分之殊也後此而有橫渠西銘之作其意
蓋本諸此先儒謂西銘為原道之宗祖愚謂孟
子蓋西銘之宗祖歟噫不有先覺孰開我人千
===
載之下豈無以心感心而自任大丈夫之事業
者乎謹論
表
擬宋理宗經筵進朱熹通鑑綱目表〔嘉熈元年〕
胡縉
同考試官訓導鄭批典實詳明而且老成
渾厚表之佳者
考試官教諭姜批表有典則可取
punctuated:
諸侯，直淺淺小丈夫者之為耳，烏可挈而與之同日語哉？抑孟子斯言，或者謂恐近於兼愛之說，此蓋不知孟子，抑豈善讀孟子者乎？理一而分殊，程朱之論備矣。居天下之廣居，理之一也；由此而天下之正位立焉，天下之大道行焉，品級隆殺、施為緩急，固自有截然而不可紊者存焉，蓋分之殊也。後此而有橫渠《西銘》之作，其意蓋本諸此。先儒謂《西銘》為《原道》之宗祖，愚謂《孟子》蓋《西銘》之宗祖歟！噫！不有先覺，孰開我人？千載之下，豈無以心感心而自任大丈夫之事業者乎？謹論。
表
擬宋理宗經筵進朱熹《通鑑綱目》表〔嘉熈元年〕
胡縉
同考試官訓導鄭批：典實詳明，而且老成渾厚，表之佳者。
考試官教諭姜批：表有典則，可取。
translation_en:
…the feudal lords: this is merely the conduct of petty men of shallow understanding. How could they be placed alongside him and spoken of in the same breath? Yet some may say that these words of Mencius seem dangerously close to the doctrine of universal love. Such people do not understand Mencius; how could they be skilled readers of his work? Principle is one, but its particular manifestations differ: Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi have discussed this fully. To dwell in the broad dwelling of the world exemplifies the unity of principle. From this, the correct position in the world is established and the great Way of the world is followed. Distinctions of rank, greater and lesser degrees of observance, and the relative urgency of actions assuredly have clear boundaries that cannot be confused. These exemplify differentiation in particular manifestations. Later, Hengqu composed the Western Inscription, whose meaning surely derives from this. Earlier Confucian scholars called the Western Inscription the progenitor of Inquiry into the Way. I venture to say that the Mencius is the progenitor of the Western Inscription! Alas! Without those who awaken first, who would enlighten us? A thousand years later, could there be no one whose heart responds to theirs and who takes upon himself the undertaking of a great man? Respectfully submitted as a discourse.
Memorial
A memorial composed as if submitting Zhu Xi’s Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror at a Classics Colloquium before Emperor Lizong of the Song 〔First year of Jiaxi〕
Hu Jin
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: “The classical references are substantial, detailed, and clear; moreover, the writing is mature, ample, and substantial. This is an excellent memorial.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The memorial follows established literary standards and merits acceptance.”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張批駢儷有體必長於四
六者
伏以
道載諸經妙彌綸之化於萬世事存乎史
昭鑒戒之法於百王政雖獨斷於
宸聰識必有資於舊典故學求古訓賢君復殷
世之太平而好問用中聖帝開虞朝之盛
治若近世朱熹之綱目本歷代名儒之纂
脩起自烈王之戊寅訖於世宗之顯德大
===
書分注正統表年其綱則法春秋而兼採
羣史之長其目則倣左氏而并稽諸儒之粹
蓋合千數百年之行事著為五十九卷之
成書凡國家之興衰可開卷而盡得凡制
度之損益可觸目而周知詳備非李燾之
長編簡要刪司馬之通鑑誠典刑之總會
冊牘之淵林也恭惟
〇〇〇〇
體居離正
punctuated:
考試官教諭張批：駢儷有體，必長於四六者。

伏以：道載諸經，妙彌綸之化於萬世；事存乎史，昭鑒戒之法於百王。政雖獨斷於宸聰，識必有資於舊典。故學求古訓，賢君復殷世之太平；而好問用中，聖帝開虞朝之盛治。若近世朱熹之《綱目》，本歷代名儒之纂脩，起自烈王之戊寅，訖於世宗之顯德。大書分注，正統表年。其綱則法《春秋》，而兼採羣史之長；其目則倣《左氏》，而并稽諸儒之粹。蓋合千數百年之行事，著為五十九卷之成書。凡國家之興衰，可開卷而盡得；凡制度之損益，可觸目而周知。詳備非李燾之《長編》，簡要刪司馬之《通鑑》，誠典刑之總會、冊牘之淵林也。恭惟〇〇〇〇，體居離正，
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The parallel prose has proper form; its author must excel in four-and-six prose.”

We humbly submit: The Way is recorded in the Classics, wondrously encompassing transformative workings for all ages; events are preserved in histories, making clear to successive sovereigns the principles that furnish examples and warnings. Although decisions in government rest solely with Your Majesty’s sagacity, understanding must draw upon ancient records. Thus, by studying ancient teachings, a worthy ruler restored the peace of the Yin age; by delighting in inquiry and applying the mean, a sage emperor inaugurated the flourishing government of the Yu dynasty.

As for Zhu Xi’s Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Gangmu), produced in recent times, it draws upon compilations by eminent scholars of successive dynasties. It begins with the wuyin year of King Lie [?] and ends with the Xiande era of Emperor Shizong. Major entries are written prominently, with subsidiary annotations; years are designated according to the legitimate succession. Its outlines take the Spring and Autumn Annals as their model while drawing upon the strengths of the various histories; its details follow the Zuo Commentary while also examining the finest contributions of the Confucian scholars. It gathers the events of more than a thousand years into a completed work of fifty-nine juan. All the rises and declines of states can be fully grasped by opening its pages; all additions to and reductions in institutions can be comprehensively understood at a glance. In its detailed completeness it differs from Li Tao’s Long Compilation [?]; in its concision it abridges Sima’s Comprehensive Mirror. It is truly a gathering of authoritative precedents and a vast treasury of written records.

We reverently consider that 〇〇〇〇 [honorific placeholder], occupying the proper sovereign position represented by the trigram Li…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德秉乾剛右道崇儒
恩數加於前哲繼志述事政每監于先王猶
勤周文未見之心益懋宣王厲精之志乃
謂此書之旨趣永為世道之範模發揮
命講於經筵善惡思求乎往轍臣等久塵勸講
慙無啓沃於
淵衷偶荷
傳宣喜獲敷陳于
黼扆爰進
===
九重之御仰祈
乙夜之觀彼緝熈光明詩著仔肩之義而剛
健篤實易稱多識之功伏願
考諸君臣事為之間察其成敗安危之迹行
其所善勿視為簡冊之陳言戒其所非不
諉諸
國家之故事於焉遠追夏商以上之治豈徒
不數漢唐以來之君臣等無任瞻
天仰
punctuated: 德秉乾剛，右道崇儒，恩數加於前哲；繼志述事，政每監于先王。猶勤周文未見之心，益懋宣王厲精之志。乃謂此書之旨趣，永為世道之範模。發揮命講於經筵，善惡思求乎往轍。臣等久塵勸講，慙無啓沃於淵衷。偶荷傳宣，喜獲敷陳于黼扆。爰進九重之御，仰祈乙夜之觀。彼緝熈光明，詩著仔肩之義；而剛健篤實，易稱多識之功。伏願考諸君臣事為之間，察其成敗安危之迹，行其所善，勿視為簡冊之陳言；戒其所非，不諉諸國家之故事。於焉遠追夏商以上之治，豈徒不數漢唐以來之君！臣等無任瞻天仰
translation_en:
… Your virtue embodies the firmness of Heaven. You uphold the Way and honor Confucian learning, extending gracious honors to the sages of former times. You carry forward their aspirations and undertakings, always modeling your government on the ancient kings. You remain as diligent as King Wen of Zhou, who sought the Way as though he had not yet glimpsed it, and further strengthen King Xuan’s resolve to exert himself wholeheartedly. You thus deem the purport of this book an enduring model for the governance of the world. You have ordered its meaning to be expounded at the Classics Colloquium, seeking to discern good and evil in the tracks of the past.

We, your servants, have long unworthily served as lecturers and are ashamed that we have provided no enlightenment to Your Majesty’s profound understanding. Having received your command, we rejoice at the opportunity to expound this work before your throne. We therefore submit it for your imperial use, reverently requesting that you peruse it during the second watch of the night. In speaking of continuing in brightness and illumination, the Book of Odes sets forth the meaning of bearing responsibility upon one’s shoulders; in speaking of firmness, vigor, sincerity, and solidity, the Book of Changes praises the achievement of broad learning.

We humbly hope that you will examine the deeds of rulers and ministers and scrutinize the traces of their successes and failures, security and peril. Practice what was good in them, without regarding it as merely stale words in old books; take warning from what was wrong, without excusing it as established precedent of the state. Thus may you reach far back to match the good government of the Xia and Shang and earlier ages. How could this mean merely surpassing the rulers of the Han and Tang and later times? We, your servants, cannot contain our feelings as we gaze toward Heaven and look up toward …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖激切屏營之至謹以朱熹通鑑綱目若干卷
隨
表上
進以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
鄭琬
考試官教諭姜批
君道十事正欲士子知我
聖祖德行之懿
列聖繼述之善此子敷答詳明及陳
今日法
祖之所當先者亦甚懇切忠愛末數語尤有警策足占所
養薦之於
上他日亦可以備
顧問矣
punctuated:
聖，激切屏營之至，謹以朱熹通鑑綱目若干卷，隨表上進以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
鄭琬
考試官教諭姜批：
君道十事，正欲士子知我聖祖德行之懿、列聖繼述之善。此子敷答詳明，及陳今日法祖之所當先者，亦甚懇切忠愛。末數語尤有警策，足占所養。薦之於上，他日亦可以備顧問矣。
translation_en:
…Your Sagely Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit the several volumes of Zhu Xi’s Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian gangmu), accompanying this memorial, for Your Majesty’s attention.
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Zheng Wan
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor:
The ten matters concerning the Way of the Ruler are intended precisely to enable the candidates to understand the excellence of our sagely founder’s virtue and conduct, and how well the successive sage emperors carried on his work. This candidate’s response is detailed and clear. His exposition of what should take priority today in emulating the founder is also deeply earnest, loyal, and devoted. His final few remarks are particularly incisive and admonitory, sufficiently revealing his moral cultivation. We recommend him to the throne; in time, he too may be available to offer counsel when consulted.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭張批我
皇祖盡
君道之大詳具於五倫書場中漫舉其目而於事實漠如也
此策鋪張揚厲殆盡而復敬陳法
祖守成之先務誠可為
今日率由之一助宜録以
獻
前聖之創業者固盡善而盡美
後聖之守成者尤至精而至密盖創業固難守
===
成亦不易也惟我
聖祖貽謀有以裕乎後而
神孫繩武有以光乎前共成正大光明之業於
億萬斯年之永正孟子所謂先聖後聖其
揆一也猗歟盛哉愚也遊化日光天之下
坐鳶飛魚躍之中固不能紬金匱之文發
蘭臺之祕然
祖功宗德輝耀瑶編
聖略神謀崢嶸寳閣亦甞伏讀
punctuated:
考試官敎諭張批：我皇祖盡君道之大，詳具於五倫書。場中漫舉其目，而於事實漠如也。此策鋪張揚厲殆盡，而復敬陳法祖守成之先務，誠可為今日率由之一助，宜録以獻。
前聖之創業者，固盡善而盡美；後聖之守成者，尤至精而至密。盖創業固難，守成亦不易也。惟我聖祖貽謀有以裕乎後，而神孫繩武有以光乎前，共成正大光明之業於億萬斯年之永，正孟子所謂「先聖後聖，其揆一也」。猗歟盛哉！愚也遊化日光天之下，坐鳶飛魚躍之中，固不能紬金匱之文，發蘭臺之祕，然祖功宗德輝耀瑶編，聖略神謀崢嶸寳閣，亦甞伏讀…
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Our imperial ancestor fully realized the greatness of the ruler’s Way, as set out in detail in the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu). Candidates in the examination hall merely enumerate its headings, while remaining vague about the actual deeds. This policy essay expounds and extols them almost exhaustively, and further respectfully presents the foremost duties in emulating the ancestor and preserving his achievement. It can indeed help guide conduct today and deserves to be recorded and presented to the throne.
The earlier sage’s founding of the dynasty was wholly good and wholly beautiful; the later sage’s preservation of that achievement is especially refined and meticulous. For founding an undertaking is certainly difficult, but preserving it is no easy matter either. Our sagely ancestor bequeathed plans sufficient to provide abundantly for his successors, while his divine descendant follows in his footsteps and thereby brings glory to his predecessor. Together they establish an upright and illustrious undertaking to endure for countless ages. This is precisely what Mencius meant when he said, “The earlier sage and the later sage share the same standard.” Ah, how magnificent! Ignorant though I am, I live beneath the sun of transforming influence and the radiant heavens, amid a world where kites soar and fish leap. Certainly I cannot draw forth the writings in the golden coffers or reveal the secrets of the Orchid Terrace archives. Yet the accomplishments and virtues of the imperial ancestors shine in precious volumes, and their sagely strategies and divine plans stand exalted in treasured pavilions. I too have reverently read…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
御製五倫書有以仰窺乎君道篇之大略矣謹
稽首頓首敬陳我
皇祖之盛蓋如恭遇
仁祖諱日而泣下不止永懷終天之恨此
聖孝之大也雖大舜之終慕豈不異世而同符
省覽尚書洪範而
聖心有契手為註疏之舉此
聖學之大也雖武王之銘丹書豈不異代而同心
語敬天也則當久旱之餘而減膳素食其
===
周宣之側身脩行乎語仁民也則當兵革
之後而減租免賦其帝堯之憂民不遂乎
儒士唐仲實直對築城頗怨即
命罷之此求言之廣也夫豈漢宣帝詔求直言
而徒事虚文者可彷彿其一二參軍宋思
顏正言豢虎無益即
命殺之此聽納之勇也又豈魏文帝行獵失鹿
而勉强赦人者可比擬其萬一若夫用賢
也則授何真以江西參政用慰來歸之誠
punctuated: 御製《五倫書》，有以仰窺乎《君道》篇之大略矣。謹稽首頓首，敬陳我皇祖之盛。蓋如恭遇仁祖諱日，而泣下不止，永懷終天之恨，此聖孝之大也。雖大舜之終慕，豈不異世而同符？省覽《尚書》《洪範》，而聖心有契，手為註疏之舉，此聖學之大也。雖武王之銘《丹書》，豈不異代而同心？語敬天也，則當久旱之餘，而減膳素食，其周宣之側身脩行乎？語仁民也，則當兵革之後，而減租免賦，其帝堯之憂民不遂乎？儒士唐仲實直對築城頗怨，即命罷之，此求言之廣也。夫豈漢宣帝詔求直言，而徒事虚文者，可彷彿其一二？參軍宋思顏正言豢虎無益，即命殺之，此聽納之勇也。又豈魏文帝行獵失鹿，而勉强赦人者，可比擬其萬一？若夫用賢也，則授何真以江西參政，用慰來歸之誠。
translation_en:
…the imperially authored Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), through which I have been able reverently to glimpse the broad outline of its chapter on “The Way of the Ruler.” Bowing low and knocking my head upon the ground, I respectfully set forth the greatness of our imperial ancestor. For example, whenever he reverently observed the anniversary of Renzu’s death, his tears flowed without cease, and he forever cherished a grief that would last his lifetime: such was the greatness of his sagely filial piety. Even great Shun’s lifelong yearning for his parents—did it not accord with this, though they lived in different ages? He examined the “Great Plan” chapter of the Book of Documents, and his sagely mind found accord with it; he undertook to write annotations and explanations with his own hand. Such was the greatness of his sagely learning. Even King Wu’s making inscriptions from the Cinnabar Writ—did it not reveal the same mind, though they lived in different eras?

As for revering Heaven, after a prolonged drought he reduced his meals and ate only vegetarian food. Was this not like King Xuan of Zhou’s humbling himself and cultivating his conduct? As for benevolence toward the people, after warfare he reduced land taxes and remitted levies. Was this not like Emperor Yao’s concern that his people were not prospering? When the scholar Tang Zhongshi frankly replied that building the city wall had caused considerable resentment, he immediately ordered the work stopped. Such was the breadth of his solicitation of advice. Could Emperor Xuan of Han, who issued an edict seeking frank speech but merely engaged in empty formalities, resemble him in even one or two respects? When the Military Staff Officer Song Siyan forthrightly declared that keeping tigers served no useful purpose, he immediately ordered them killed. Such was his resolve in accepting advice. Could Emperor Wen of Wei, who lost a deer while hunting and only reluctantly pardoned the person responsible, compare with him in even the slightest degree?

As for employing worthy men, he appointed He Zhen as Vice Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, thereby acknowledging the sincerity with which he had come to submit…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
勤政也未旦臨朝晡時還宮即成湯之克
用宅俊文王之不遑暇食焉謹戒也則謂
徐達以致謹於初保安天下之重節儉也
雕飾竒巧一切不用即穆王之怵惕惟厲
夏禹之卑宮惡服焉是則
皇祖不世之鴻休無前之偉績真度越古帝王
萬萬矣愚也仰高太虛固不能窺以管望
洋滄海亦豈能測以蠡哉然執事又詢以
法
===
祖之所當先者愚竊以為古之聖人達而在上
者宜莫如堯如舜亦莫如高宗窮而在下
者又莫如孔子而堯且考古舜亦稽古高
宗又學古孔子猶好古則
今日之務所宜先而不可後者固無外於法
祖之一事而
皇祖之所行者又孰非世世為法為則於天下
後世者邪欽惟
皇上念
punctuated: 勤政也，未旦臨朝，晡時還宮，即成湯之克用宅俊、文王之不遑暇食焉。謹戒也，則謂徐達以致謹於初、保安天下之重；節儉也，雕飾竒巧，一切不用，即穆王之怵惕惟厲、夏禹之卑宮惡服焉。是則皇祖不世之鴻休、無前之偉績，真度越古帝王萬萬矣。愚也仰高太虛，固不能窺以管；望洋滄海，亦豈能測以蠡哉？然執事又詢以法祖之所當先者，愚竊以為古之聖人，達而在上者，宜莫如堯、如舜，亦莫如高宗；窮而在下者，又莫如孔子。而堯且考古，舜亦稽古，高宗又學古，孔子猶好古，則今日之務所宜先而不可後者，固無外於法祖之一事。而皇祖之所行者，又孰非世世為法為則於天下後世者邪？欽惟皇上念
translation_en:
…As for diligence in government, he attended court before dawn and returned to the palace in the late afternoon: here were Cheng Tang’s ability to employ worthy men in office and King Wen’s inability to spare time even for a meal. As for vigilance, he spoke to Xu Da of the importance of exercising caution at the outset and preserving peace throughout the realm. As for frugality, he rejected all ornate embellishments and ingenious luxuries: here were King Mu’s apprehensive awareness of danger and Yu of Xia’s modest palaces and plain clothing. Thus the imperial ancestor’s extraordinary glory and unprecedented achievements truly surpassed those of ancient emperors and kings ten thousandfold. Gazing up at the lofty heavens, I, in my ignorance, certainly cannot survey them through a tube; looking out upon the vast ocean, how could I measure it with a ladle?

Yet you, honored examiners, further ask what should take priority in emulating the ancestor. I humbly believe that among the ancient sages who attained prominence and occupied high positions, none surpassed Yao and Shun, or Gaozong; among those who remained in obscurity and low station, none surpassed Confucius. Yet Yao examined antiquity, Shun likewise investigated antiquity, Gaozong studied antiquity, and Confucius, too, cherished antiquity. Thus, among today’s tasks, what should take precedence and must not be deferred is surely none other than emulating the ancestor. And which of the imperial ancestor’s deeds would not serve, generation after generation, as a model and standard for all under Heaven and for posterity? I reverently reflect that His Majesty bears in mind…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗創業之艱難思
今日守成之不易體
太宗
仁宗之心
覽商書周詩之訓凡所以法
祖者真如堯舜揖遜之傳文武授受之法而二
三大臣之守法又有所謂皐夔伊傅周召
之輩天下臣民方將覩二帝三王太平之
治於無窮也夫復何言若夫唱為祖宗不
===
足法之說而敢附會迎合立為一年一變
法之說或率意而輕法或眾辨而侮法或
擊斷而外法則王安石呂惠卿之徒萬世
之罪人也愚竊耻之而不敢為且不忍為
焉草野之人狂瞽之言不知忌諱取其意
而略其詞可也未識執事者以為然乎否
第二問
王埕
同考試官教諭方 批 文章政事之顯晦顧時
punctuated:
祖宗創業之艱難，思今日守成之不易，體太宗、仁宗之心，覽商書、周詩之訓。凡所以法祖者，真如堯舜揖遜之傳、文武授受之法，而二三大臣之守法，又有所謂皐夔伊傅周召之輩。天下臣民方將覩二帝三王太平之治於無窮也，夫復何言？若夫唱為祖宗不足法之說，而敢附會迎合，立為一年一變法之說，或率意而輕法，或眾辨而侮法，或擊斷而外法，則王安石、呂惠卿之徒，萬世之罪人也。愚竊耻之而不敢為，且不忍為焉。草野之人，狂瞽之言，不知忌諱，取其意而略其詞可也。未識執事者以為然乎否？

第二問
王埕
同考試官教諭方 批：文章政事之顯晦，顧時
translation_en:
…the hardships endured by the imperial ancestors in founding the dynasty, considers how difficult it is to preserve their achievements today, enters into the spirit of Taizong and Renzong, and studies the teachings of the Documents of Shang and the Odes of Zhou. In all his ways of taking the ancestors as his models, he truly follows the pattern of Yao and Shun handing on rule through courteous abdication, and of Wen and Wu transmitting and receiving it. Among the chief ministers who uphold these laws, moreover, are men comparable to Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao. The officials and people throughout the realm are about to witness the peaceful governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings continuing without end. What more need be said?

As for those who proclaim that the ancestors are unworthy of emulation, who dare to twist interpretations to curry favor and advocate changing the laws every year—whether they follow their whims and treat the laws lightly, heap up arguments to scorn them, or act peremptorily outside them—they belong among such men as Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing, condemned as wrongdoers for all generations. In my humble view, I find such conduct shameful: I dare not engage in it, nor could I bear to do so. These are the rash and uninformed words of a man outside official life, ignorant of what must not be said. You may accept their meaning and overlook their phrasing. I do not know whether you, gentlemen in charge, consider them right or not.

Second Question
Wang Cheng
Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: Whether literary accomplishment and administrative ability find expression or remain obscure depends upon the times…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之盛衰與君之用否何如耳此篇敷荅詳明剖
析當理可以占知其素蘊也允宜高薦
同考試官學正陳批隨問隨荅而文采爛然
文章可謂無負矣異日施之政事必有大可
觀者得士如此吾儕可以自慶
考試官敎諭姜批文章政事相為體用
觀子今日之文章則異時之政事從可知矣
健羨健羨
考試官敎諭張批文章政事存乎其人
===
尚論其世自當有得此策敷對詳明且有斷
制子之胷中品藻素定矣
文章政事之純疵本乎學術之淺深文章
政事之顯晦由乎人君之用舍蓋詩書禮
樂皆潤澤生民之具而功名事業實吾道
顯設之緒固不可岐而二之者豈可如歐
陽子所謂文章止於潤身政事止於及物
者哉故曰本乎學術之淺深也然文章有
餘而不得竟其所施者則又係於其時人
punctuated:
之盛衰與君之用否何如耳。此篇敷荅詳明，剖析當理，可以占知其素蘊也，允宜高薦。
同考試官學正陳批：隨問隨荅，而文采爛然，文章可謂無負矣。異日施之政事，必有大可觀者。得士如此，吾儕可以自慶。
考試官敎諭姜批：文章政事相為體用。觀子今日之文章，則異時之政事從可知矣。健羨，健羨！
考試官敎諭張批：文章政事存乎其人，尚論其世，自當有得。此策敷對詳明，且有斷制，子之胷中品藻素定矣。
文章政事之純疵，本乎學術之淺深；文章政事之顯晦，由乎人君之用舍。蓋詩書禮樂皆潤澤生民之具，而功名事業實吾道顯設之緒，固不可岐而二之者。豈可如歐陽子所謂文章止於潤身，政事止於及物者哉？故曰本乎學術之淺深也。然文章有餘，而不得竟其所施者，則又係於其時人
translation_en:
…whether the age flourishes or declines, and whether the ruler employs the man. This essay expounds its answers fully and clearly, and its analysis accords with principle. From it one can discern his accumulated learning. He certainly deserves recommendation at a high rank.
Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: He answers each question in turn, with brilliant literary expression. In literary composition, he may indeed be said to have fulfilled expectations. When he applies this ability to government affairs in the future, there will surely be much worth admiring. Having obtained a scholar like this, we may congratulate ourselves.
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: Literary composition and government affairs stand to one another as substance and function. From your literary composition today, one can discern what your conduct of government affairs will be in the future. How admirable, how admirable!
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: Literary composition and government affairs depend on the individual. By considering the age in which he lived, one should naturally gain understanding. This policy essay answers fully and clearly, and also displays decisive judgment. Your assessments have long been settled in your mind.
The purity or flaws of literary composition and government affairs are rooted in the depth or shallowness of learning; their prominence or obscurity depends on whether the ruler employs or sets aside their practitioner. Poetry, documents, rites, and music are all instruments for enriching the lives of the people, while achievements and undertakings are in truth the outward manifestations of our Way. These certainly cannot be divided into two separate things. How, then, could one follow Master Ouyang in saying that literary composition serves only to adorn oneself, while government affairs serve only to benefit others? Thus I say that their quality is rooted in the depth or shallowness of learning. Yet when someone possesses ample literary ability but cannot fully put it into practice, this also depends on the people of his time [?]…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者之用舍何如耳是烏足為文章累耶愚
也當懷鉛提槧之餘其於斯二者之議亦
嘗輾轉於胷中乆矣請因明問而詳言之
夫文章天下之公器近可以傳之家國遠
可以傳之天下後世政事平生之設施上
可以致君下可以澤民斯二者固君子之
所尚也然三代而上内而賡歌外而兵農
亦皆剛簡直寬之德出而使長入而使治
無非俊造秀義之士君民相忘於道化之
===
中天下交孚於泰和之治固不知所謂文
章亦不知所謂政事也自夫三代以還有
區區於操觚弄翰之末者有汲汲於粉飾
太平之具者於是乎文章政事始分為二
途矣以漢言之董仲舒一代之名儒也正誼
之言漢之文章宜莫有過之者施之政事
綽乎有餘然天人之策一陳而江都之命
隨下矣政事不聞於當時厥有由哉以唐
言之韓退之一代之山斗也原道一篇唐
punctuated:
者之用舍何如耳，是烏足為文章累耶？愚也當懷鉛提槧之餘，其於斯二者之議，亦嘗輾轉於胷中乆矣。請因明問而詳言之。
夫文章，天下之公器，近可以傳之家國，遠可以傳之天下後世；政事，平生之設施，上可以致君，下可以澤民。斯二者，固君子之所尚也。然三代而上，内而賡歌，外而兵農，亦皆剛簡直寬之德；出而使長，入而使治，無非俊造秀義之士。君民相忘於道化之中，天下交孚於泰和之治，固不知所謂文章，亦不知所謂政事也。自夫三代以還，有區區於操觚弄翰之末者，有汲汲於粉飾太平之具者，於是乎文章政事始分為二途矣。
以漢言之，董仲舒，一代之名儒也。正誼之言，漢之文章宜莫有過之者；施之政事，綽乎有餘。然天人之策一陳，而江都之命隨下矣。政事不聞於當時，厥有由哉！以唐言之，韓退之，一代之山斗也。《原道》一篇，唐
translation_en:
…depends only on whether those in authority employ or set aside such men [?]. How could this possibly discredit literary writing? In the intervals of my humble labors with writing lead and wooden tablets, I too have long turned over in my mind the relationship between these two pursuits. Permit me to explain it in detail in response to your discerning question.
Literary writing is a resource shared by all under Heaven: within a narrower sphere, it can be transmitted throughout the family and state; more broadly, throughout the world and to later generations. Government consists in what one puts into practice over a lifetime: above, it can bring the ruler to fulfillment; below, it can confer blessings upon the people. Both are indeed pursuits esteemed by the gentleman. Yet during the Three Dynasties and earlier, whether exchanging songs at court or attending to military and agricultural affairs outside it, men embodied the virtues of firmness, simplicity, uprightness, and generosity. Those sent out to lead and those brought in to govern were all men of outstanding talent and eminent righteousness [?]. Rulers and people lived so naturally within the transforming influence of the Way that they forgot distinctions between themselves; all under Heaven trusted one another under a government of supreme harmony. They knew nothing of a separate pursuit called literary writing, nor of one called government. After the Three Dynasties, some confined themselves to the trifles of handling writing tablets and wielding brushes, while others busied themselves with devices for putting a gloss of peace upon the realm. Thus literary writing and government first diverged into two paths.
To speak of the Han, Dong Zhongshu was a renowned Confucian scholar of his age. His words on rectifying righteousness surely had no superior in Han writing; applied to government, they would have been more than sufficient. Yet no sooner had he submitted his policy essay on Heaven and humanity than his appointment to Jiangdu followed. There was indeed a reason why his achievements in government went unheard of in his own time! To speak of the Tang, Han Tuizhi was the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of his age. His essay An Inquiry into the Way, among the writings of the Tang…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之文章亦莫有過之者措之政事豈有不
足然佛骨之表朝陳而潮陽之貶夕行矣
功業不著於海內豈無以哉至若宋之周
程張朱道承孔孟學有淵源前後著作輝
煌炳耀文章固無容喙矣使其大得設施
則二帝三王之治化伊傅周召之事功猶
反掌也然或隨用隨罷或小試郡邑奈之
何哉此宋之諸君子文章政事不能兩全
者職此故也要之功名不足以累其心而
===
其名則至今不衰人君用人其可忽諸雖
然從事於誦說章句之末則流於儒之腐
從事於法律刀筆之陋則墮於吏之俗古
人典謨之腴發為雍熙之治絃歌之化本
乎文學之施儒術飾吏事不可誣者彼漢
之蕭曹丙魏唐之王魏房杜宋之趙范呂
李雖未有制作之本於學術然天資之美
能輔相其君以成一代之盛治是豈可以
俗吏少之哉若夫漢之劉歆揚雄隋之王
punctuated:
之文章亦莫有過之者，措之政事，豈有不足？然佛骨之表朝陳，而潮陽之貶夕行矣。功業不著於海內，豈無以哉？至若宋之周程張朱，道承孔孟，學有淵源，前後著作輝煌炳耀，文章固無容喙矣。使其大得設施，則二帝三王之治化、伊傅周召之事功，猶反掌也。然或隨用隨罷，或小試郡邑，奈之何哉？此宋之諸君子文章政事不能兩全者，職此故也。要之，功名不足以累其心，而其名則至今不衰。人君用人，其可忽諸？

雖然，從事於誦說章句之末，則流於儒之腐；從事於法律刀筆之陋，則墮於吏之俗。古人典謨之腴，發為雍熙之治；絃歌之化，本乎文學之施。儒術飾吏事，不可誣者。彼漢之蕭曹丙魏、唐之王魏房杜、宋之趙范呂李，雖未有制作之本於學術，然天資之美，能輔相其君，以成一代之盛治，是豈可以俗吏少之哉？若夫漢之劉歆揚雄、隋之王
translation_en:
…among the writings of the Tang, too, none surpassed it. How could he have been unequal to applying it to government? Yet his memorial on the Buddha’s bone was submitted in the morning, and by evening he was sent into exile at Chaoyang. Could there have been no reason why his achievements failed to become manifest throughout the realm? As for Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu of the Song, they inherited the Way of Kongzi and Mengzi, and their learning had deep roots. Their successive writings shone brilliantly; their literary accomplishments were certainly beyond reproach. Had they been given ample opportunity to put their learning into practice, achieving the transformative rule of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and the accomplishments of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, would have been as easy as turning over a hand. Yet some were dismissed almost as soon as they were employed, while others were given only limited trials in prefectures and counties. What could they do? This alone explains why these gentlemen of the Song could not attain fulfillment in both writing and government. In essence, achievement and fame could not burden their minds, and their reputations remain undiminished to this day. Can a ruler afford to be heedless in employing men?

Nevertheless, to devote oneself to the minutiae of reciting and expounding textual passages is to lapse into the pedantry of the Confucian scholar; to devote oneself to the narrow business of laws and legal paperwork is to sink into the vulgarity of the functionary. The richness of the ancients’ Canons and Counsels issued in harmonious and glorious government; the transforming influence of strings and song was rooted in the application of cultural learning. That Confucian learning lends refinement to administrative affairs cannot be denied. Xiao, Cao, Bing, and Wei of the Han; Wang, Wei, Fang, and Du of the Tang; and Zhao, Fan, Lü, and Li of the Song may not have established institutions grounded in scholarly learning, yet their excellent natural gifts enabled them to assist their rulers in bringing about an age of flourishing government. How could they be belittled as vulgar functionaries? As for Liu Xin and Yang Xiong of the Han, and Wang of the Sui…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
通薛收唐之盧王楊駱雖嘗有著述之顯
名當時然學問之偏出於諂諛放浪而為
無實之空談是烏得免夫腐儒之誚哉愚
也學非經緯才非經濟然以仁義為儒固
不敢為夫腐者以教化為吏尤不敢為夫
俗者盖自有吾聖賢之家譜在也不曰文
學子游子夏乎政事冉有季路乎等而上
之則吾夫子之刪述六經垂憲萬世攝行
相事政化大行煥乎文章巍乎成功自生
===
民以來未有盛於孔子也是則所謂才之
全也乃所願則學孔子也執事幸勿以為
嘐嘐
第三問
方策
同考試官訓導鄭批字學一策書譜書評皆
有成說子能一二陳之必嘗游於藝者敬羨敬羨
考試官教諭姜批子豈嘗從事字學而
得家數者與何其知要如此也
punctuated:
通、薛收，唐之盧、王、楊、駱，雖嘗有著述之顯名當時，然學問之偏，出於諂諛放浪，而為無實之空談，是烏得免夫腐儒之誚哉？愚也，學非經緯，才非經濟，然以仁義為儒，固不敢為夫腐者；以教化為吏，尤不敢為夫俗者。盖自有吾聖賢之家譜在也。不曰「文學，子游、子夏」乎？「政事，冉有、季路」乎？等而上之，則吾夫子之刪述六經，垂憲萬世，攝行相事，政化大行，煥乎文章，巍乎成功，自生民以來，未有盛於孔子也。是則所謂才之全也。乃所願則學孔子也，執事幸勿以為嘐嘐。

第三問

方策

同考試官訓導鄭批：字學一策，書譜、書評皆有成說，子能一二陳之，必嘗游於藝者。敬羨，敬羨！

考試官教諭姜批：子豈嘗從事字學而得家數者與？何其知要如此也！
translation_en:
…Tong and Xue Shou, and Lu, Wang, Yang, and Luo of the Tang, although once renowned in their time for their writings, were partial in their learning, given to flattery and unrestrained conduct, and produced empty discourse without substance. How could they escape the reproach of being pedantic scholars? My learning is inadequate to ordering the world, and my ability inadequate to governing it. Yet, as a scholar who takes benevolence and righteousness as his foundation, I certainly dare not become a pedant; as an official who takes moral instruction and transformation as his task, I dare still less become a vulgar functionary. For we have the lineage of our sages and worthies to follow. Does it not say, “In literary learning, Ziyou and Zixia,” and “In government, Ran You and Jilu”? Ascending still higher, our Master edited and transmitted the Six Classics, bequeathing standards to ten thousand generations. Acting as chief minister, he brought government and moral transformation into widespread effect. Resplendent was his cultural achievement, lofty his accomplishment: since humankind first existed, none has surpassed Confucius. This is what is meant by completeness of talent. My aspiration, then, is to learn from Confucius. May you, sir, kindly refrain from considering this boastful.

Third Question

Fang Ce

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zheng: In this policy essay on the study of written characters, you have been able to set forth several established views from calligraphic treatises and critical appraisals. You must have spent time cultivating the arts. My respectful admiration, my respectful admiration!

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang: Have you perhaps devoted yourself to the study of written characters and mastered its methods? How thoroughly you grasp its essentials!

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張批書法隨世異制而揮
染因人異趣要之取其心畫之正不徒藝焉而
已此策能悉之用錄以示夫故意取妍者
聖賢之開物成務莫大乎字之作聖賢之
作字代繩一根乎心之理蓋文非字則弗
傳字非理則無本故作文而有其字則動
於此而應於彼自有以成天下之務作字
而根於理則理無窮而字無窮自足以資
萬世之用小則可以潤乎身大則可以濟
===
乎世是字學之所關也豈淺淺哉請因明
問而陳之自夫太極既判之初兩儀始奠
之候言其俗則顓蒙而質朴之未散言其
政則結繩而號令之未施于時則字未之
有也迨夫河出圖洛出書伏羲因之以畫
卦而字之點畫於是乎胚胎矣然八卦雖
畫而文猶未著蒼頡繼之則據理以造書
而聲音以諧形體以正字於是乎大明矣
由是經以之傳道以之載史以之而不失
punctuated:
考試官教諭張批：書法隨世異制，而揮染因人異趣。要之，取其心畫之正，不徒藝焉而已。此策能悉之，用錄以示夫故意取妍者。
聖賢之開物成務，莫大乎字之作。聖賢之作字代繩，一根乎心之理。蓋文非字則弗傳，字非理則無本。故作文而有其字，則動於此而應於彼，自有以成天下之務；作字而根於理，則理無窮而字無窮，自足以資萬世之用。小則可以潤乎身，大則可以濟乎世。是字學之所關也，豈淺淺哉？請因明問而陳之。自夫太極既判之初，兩儀始奠之候，言其俗，則顓蒙而質朴之未散；言其政，則結繩而號令之未施。于時則字未之有也。迨夫河出圖，洛出書，伏羲因之以畫卦，而字之點畫於是乎胚胎矣。然八卦雖畫，而文猶未著。蒼頡繼之，則據理以造書，而聲音以諧，形體以正，字於是乎大明矣。由是經以之傳，道以之載，史以之而不失
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: The forms of calligraphy change with the age, while the handling of brush and ink varies with each person’s inclinations. What matters, ultimately, is the rectitude of these visible expressions of the mind, rather than artistic skill alone. This policy essay comprehensively explains this point; it is therefore included to instruct those who deliberately strive for prettiness.
Among the sages’ achievements in opening up understanding and bringing affairs to completion, none surpasses the creation of written characters. When the sages created characters to replace knotted cords, they rooted them entirely in the principles of the mind. For compositions cannot be transmitted without characters, and characters have no foundation without principle. Thus, when compositions are made and characters are available for them, an impulse here elicits a response there, providing the means to accomplish the affairs of the world. When characters are created on the basis of principle, principle is inexhaustible and characters are inexhaustible, amply providing for the needs of ten thousand generations. On a small scale, they can enrich the individual; on a large scale, they can benefit the world. Such are the implications of the study of characters. Could they possibly be trivial? Allow me to explain in response to your illuminating question.
At the beginning, when the Supreme Ultimate had divided and the Two Modes had first become established, customs were simple and untutored, with pristine simplicity still intact; government employed knotted cords, and commands and ordinances had not yet been promulgated. At that time, written characters did not yet exist. Then the Yellow River brought forth the Chart and the Luo River brought forth the Writing. Fuxi drew upon these to delineate the trigrams, and the dots and strokes of characters were thereby conceived. Yet although the eight trigrams had been drawn, writing had not yet become manifest. Cangjie followed, creating writing on the basis of principle, harmonizing sounds and giving proper form to shapes. Written characters thus became fully manifest. Hence the classics were transmitted through them, the Way was recorded through them, and histories, through them, did not lose …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其書事以之而不遺其記百官之政賴此
以舉萬民之情賴此以通上而堯舜禹湯
文武之爲君詞命賴此以渙汗下而皐陶
伊傅周召之爲臣王命賴此以出納是則
字之用於天下也不其大歟及周嗣世宣
王中興而史籀有大篆之作顧篆書之體
雖創於一時而科斗之文猶存乎自古奈
之何世入於秦吾道之厄燔燒之禍旣熾
科斗之文不傳李斯變大篆而爲小篆斯
===
之罪不容誅也然而小篆之所存猶有蒼
史之遺意豈可以其人而遂泯其善歟程
邈變小篆而爲隸書邈之隸亦非優也然
而秦人厭篆之繁難喜隸之省徑豈非滅
詩書而專任吏之過歟漢襲秦弊欲縮之
以簡便未免失之疎而西京之敎寂無所
聞者有自來也晉矯漢失欲華之以姿媚
不免失之縱而清談之風習以成俗者有
由然也是皆世與道違字與時變無足議
punctuated: 其書，事以之而不遺其記。百官之政賴此以舉，萬民之情賴此以通。上而堯舜禹湯文武之爲君，詞命賴此以渙汗；下而皐陶伊傅周召之爲臣，王命賴此以出納。是則字之用於天下也，不其大歟？及周嗣世，宣王中興，而史籀有大篆之作。顧篆書之體雖創於一時，而科斗之文猶存乎自古。奈之何世入於秦，吾道之厄，燔燒之禍旣熾，科斗之文不傳。李斯變大篆而爲小篆，斯之罪不容誅也。然而小篆之所存，猶有蒼史之遺意，豈可以其人而遂泯其善歟？程邈變小篆而爲隸書，邈之隸亦非優也。然而秦人厭篆之繁難，喜隸之省徑，豈非滅詩書而專任吏之過歟？漢襲秦弊，欲縮之以簡便，未免失之疎，而西京之敎寂無所聞者，有自來也。晉矯漢失，欲華之以姿媚，不免失之縱，而清談之風習以成俗者，有由然也。是皆世與道違，字與時變，無足議
translation_en:
…their written accounts, and events thereby retain their records. The administration of the hundred officials relies on writing to be carried out, and the sentiments of the myriad people rely on it to be communicated. Above, rulers such as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu relied on it to issue proclamations as freely as sweat flows forth; below, ministers such as Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao relied on it to receive and transmit royal commands. Is not the usefulness of writing throughout the world immense?

When the Zhou succeeded to rule, and King Xuan brought about a restoration, Scribe Zhou devised the great seal script. Yet although the form of seal script was created at a particular time, tadpole writing had survived from antiquity. Alas, when the world entered the Qin era, our Way suffered calamity: the disaster of book burning raged, and tadpole writing ceased to be transmitted. Li Si transformed great seal script into small seal script; even execution could not adequately punish his crime. Nevertheless, what survives of small seal script still retains something of the conception of Scribe Cang Jie. How could we efface its merits simply because of the man responsible for it?

Cheng Miao transformed small seal script into clerical script. Miao’s clerical script was likewise no superior achievement. Yet the people of Qin disliked the complexity and difficulty of seal script and delighted in the economy and directness of clerical script. Was this not the fault of destroying the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents while relying exclusively on administrative functionaries?

The Han inherited the defects of Qin. Seeking to abbreviate writing for simplicity and convenience, they inevitably erred toward carelessness. Thus there was an underlying reason why the teachings of the Western Han fell silent and were no longer heard. The Jin sought to correct the failings of the Han. Seeking to embellish writing with graceful charm, they inevitably erred toward unrestrained freedom. Thus there was a reason why the vogue for pure conversation became an established custom. In all these cases, the age departed from the Way, and writing changed with the times; they merit no discussion…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也若夫王次中爲楷書此楷之始魏鍾胡
爲行書此行之始張芝承杜崔諸人之工
而愈妙於草書此草書之始蔡邕覩皇都
匠人之巧而刻意於飛白此飛白之始然
要其歸則之數體者皆適於述作之用究
其本則楷與行者尤切於日用之常學之
者其可不知所先務哉夫字也者原於心
之理發於心之用得之則令聞廣譽施於
身廓之則格君輔國鳴於世曷不觀諸古
===
人乎張伯英得執筆之五妙而草聖之名
見稱於當世王逸少得永字之八法而蘭
亭之書加重於貞觀宓子賤能掣肘善書
正其言而使之言而魯君遂爲之感悟非
格君之善者乎柳公權謂用筆在心心正
則筆正而憲宗即爲之改容非諷諫之善
者乎之數子者以字學而成天下之事也
不其大歟雖然亦有要矣善乎程子曰某
作字時甚敬非要字好即此是學夫敬也
punctuated:
也。若夫王次中爲楷書，此楷之始；魏鍾胡爲行書，此行之始；張芝承杜崔諸人之工，而愈妙於草書，此草書之始；蔡邕覩皇都匠人之巧，而刻意於飛白，此飛白之始。然要其歸，則之數體者皆適於述作之用；究其本，則楷與行者尤切於日用之常。學之者，其可不知所先務哉？夫字也者，原於心之理，發於心之用。得之，則令聞廣譽施於身；廓之，則格君輔國鳴於世。曷不觀諸古人乎？

張伯英得執筆之五妙，而草聖之名見稱於當世；王逸少得永字之八法，而蘭亭之書加重於貞觀。宓子賤能掣肘善書，正其言而使之言，而魯君遂爲之感悟，非格君之善者乎？柳公權謂用筆在心，心正則筆正，而憲宗即爲之改容，非諷諫之善者乎？之數子者，以字學而成天下之事也，不其大歟？雖然，亦有要矣。善乎程子曰：「某作字時甚敬，非要字好，即此是學。」夫敬也
translation_en:
… so it was. As for Wang Cizhong’s creation of regular script, this was the beginning of regular script; Zhong and Hu of Wei created running script, and this was the beginning of running script. Zhang Zhi inherited the skill of Du, Cui, and others, attaining still greater mastery of cursive script: this was the beginning of cursive script. Cai Yong observed the ingenuity of artisans in the imperial capital and devoted himself to flying-white script: this was the beginning of flying-white script. Yet, considering their ultimate purpose, these several styles are all suited to writing and composition; examining their fundamentals, regular and running scripts are especially pertinent to everyday use. Can those who study them fail to recognize what they must attend to first? Writing originates in the principles of the heart-mind and issues from its functioning. Master it, and a fine reputation and widespread renown accrue to oneself; extend it, and one wins distinction in the world by rectifying the ruler and assisting the state. Why not look to the ancients?

Zhang Boying mastered the five subtleties of wielding the brush and was acclaimed in his day as the Sage of Cursive Script. Wang Yishao mastered the eight methods embodied in the character yong 永, and his Orchid Pavilion calligraphy gained still greater esteem during the Zhenguan reign. Mi Zijian was able to tug at the elbows of those skilled in writing, correct their words, and have them speak [?], whereupon the ruler of Lu was moved to understanding. Was this not an excellent instance of rectifying the ruler? Liu Gongquan said that wielding the brush depended on the heart-mind: when the heart-mind was upright, the brush would be upright. Emperor Xianzong immediately changed his expression. Was this not an excellent instance of indirect remonstrance? These men accomplished affairs of the world through the study of writing. Was this not a great achievement? Nevertheless, there is also an essential point. How well Master Cheng put it: “When I write characters, I am deeply attentive and reverent. It is not that I want the characters to look good; this itself is learning.” As for reverent attentiveness …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者所以求放心明義理而爲學之所當先
也使學字者誠能閑邪以存其敬持敬以
養其心慾無不去而體以之全理無不窮
而知以之致將見援筆以施於字不求其
工而自工因字而見於爲不求其應而自
應即吾前所謂周天下之用而成天下之
事者不過此心之轉移耳愚也於字願學
而未能譬之射焉將執此以爲的不識執
事然之否也
===
第四問
李高
同考試官訓導鄭 批漢唐財用嬴縮之由
今日理財處置之宜條答亹亹卓有定見此豈但務於窮
經者乎
考試官教諭姜 批 理財正
今日要務非識時務者不能有此畫籌
考試官教諭張 批 財賦一策正欲觀士
子酌古準今有用之學塲中敷演問目了
punctuated:
者，所以求放心、明義理，而爲學之所當先也。使學字者誠能閑邪以存其敬，持敬以養其心，慾無不去而體以之全，理無不窮而知以之致，將見援筆以施於字，不求其工而自工；因字而見於爲，不求其應而自應。即吾前所謂周天下之用而成天下之事者，不過此心之轉移耳。愚也於字，願學而未能。譬之射焉，將執此以爲的，不識執事然之否也？

第四問
李高

同考試官訓導鄭批：「漢唐財用嬴縮之由，今日理財處置之宜，條答亹亹，卓有定見。此豈但務於窮經者乎？」

考試官教諭姜批：「理財，正今日要務。非識時務者，不能有此畫籌。」

考試官教諭張批：「財賦一策，正欲觀士子酌古準今有用之學。塲中敷演問目，了
translation_en:
…is the means of recovering the straying mind and clarifying moral principles, and thus should come first in learning. If those studying calligraphy can truly ward off evil to preserve their reverence, and maintain reverence to nurture their minds, every desire will be eliminated and the mind’s original substance thereby made whole; every principle will be investigated and knowledge thereby brought to its fullest extent. Then, when they take up the brush to write, their writing will become accomplished without their seeking accomplishment. As this manifests itself through calligraphy in their conduct, their actions will naturally accord with circumstances without their seeking such accord. What I spoke of earlier—meeting all the world’s needs and accomplishing its affairs—is nothing more than the workings of this mind. As for myself, untalented as I am, I wish to study calligraphy but have not yet mastered it. To compare it to archery, I shall take this as my target. I do not know whether you, sir, consider this right.

Fourth Question
Li Gao 李高

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng 鄭, Assistant Instructor: “He addresses point by point, with sustained diligence, the reasons for surpluses and shortfalls in the finances of the Han and Tang, and the appropriate measures for managing finances today. His judgments are remarkably firm. Can he be someone who concerns himself only with thoroughly studying the Classics?”

Comment by Examiner Jiang 姜, Instructor: “Managing finances is precisely an urgent task today. Someone who did not understand the needs of the times could not have devised such plans.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang 張, Instructor: “This policy question on revenue and taxation was intended precisely to reveal candidates’ practical learning—their ability to weigh ancient precedents against present circumstances. In the examination hall, their elaborations of the question’s topics utterly…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
無完言此策區處時宜切當非特取其記憶
也録之以備司
國計者之一畫
爲國莫要於理財理財莫先於節用盖財
用者生人之本有國之常經不可一日而
無者也故易載裒多益寡書稱懋遷有無
然非有以節之則所謂取之盡錙銖用之
如泥沙雖盡括天下之所出恐亦有不足
於國之用者此爲國者固以理財爲要而
===
理財又以節用爲先誠萬世不易之定論
也理財之說古今談之盡矣愚不能復有
說也請借明問所舉漢唐之事而紬繹以
對夫漢高之興當始皇頭會箕斂之後唐
室之起承煬帝窮奢極侈之餘故文帝太
宗之紹統宜乎國用不足矣然文帝則躬
脩節儉勸課農桑宫室苑囿車騎服御無
所増益有不便輒弛以利民是其務爲節
用在漢之諸君未能或之先也太宗則去
punctuated:
無完言。此策區處時宜切當，非特取其記憶也。録之以備司國計者之一畫。

爲國莫要於理財，理財莫先於節用。盖財用者，生人之本，有國之常經，不可一日而無者也。故《易》載裒多益寡，《書》稱懋遷有無。然非有以節之，則所謂取之盡錙銖，用之如泥沙，雖盡括天下之所出，恐亦有不足於國之用者。此爲國者固以理財爲要，而理財又以節用爲先，誠萬世不易之定論也。理財之說，古今談之盡矣，愚不能復有說也。請借明問所舉漢唐之事而紬繹以對。夫漢高之興，當始皇頭會箕斂之後；唐室之起，承煬帝窮奢極侈之餘。故文帝、太宗之紹統，宜乎國用不足矣。然文帝則躬脩節儉，勸課農桑，宫室、苑囿、車騎、服御，無所増益，有不便輒弛以利民。是其務爲節用，在漢之諸君未能或之先也。太宗則去
translation_en:
…not a single complete statement. This policy essay offers apt measures suited to present circumstances; it is selected for more than the candidate’s powers of recall. It is recorded to furnish those who manage the state’s finances with one possible plan.

In governing a state, nothing is more essential than managing its finances; in managing finances, nothing takes precedence over restraining expenditure. Financial resources are the foundation of the people’s livelihood and a constant concern of government: not a day can pass without them. Thus the Book of Changes speaks of diminishing abundance and augmenting scarcity, and the Book of Documents commends diligently exchanging what one has for what one lacks. Yet without restraint, this becomes what is called “exacting every last fraction and spending it like mud and sand.” Even if all that the realm produces were gathered up, it might still prove insufficient for the state’s needs. That governing requires sound financial management, and financial management requires above all restraint in expenditure, is indeed a settled principle that will remain unchanged for all ages.

Discussions of financial management, past and present, have exhausted the subject; I, in my ignorance, can add nothing further. Allow me to draw upon the events of the Han and Tang cited in your illuminating question, unravel their implications, and offer a response. The rise of Gaozu of Han followed the First Emperor’s levies, assessed by the head and gathered by the basketful; the rise of the Tang ruling house followed Emperor Yang’s unbounded extravagance. Thus, when Emperor Wen and Emperor Taizong respectively succeeded to the throne, it was only to be expected that state resources would be insufficient.

Yet Emperor Wen personally practised frugality and encouraged farming and sericulture. He made no additions to his palaces, parks, carriages, horses, clothing, or other articles for imperial use. Whenever a measure burdened the people, he relaxed it for their benefit. In his commitment to restraining expenditure, none of the Han rulers could surpass him. Taizong, for his part, eliminated…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
奢省費輕徭薄賦選用廉吏使民衣食有
餘自不為盜是其恭儉之政在唐之諸君
亦未有與之並也夫用節則費省費省則
國富雖寬恤之詔屢下征榷之令不行亦
何害其國用之有餘乎至於武帝德宗承
數世之積累固宜國用有餘也然武帝則
外事四夷内興工役故常賦不足而榷酒
酤筭舟車造緡錢之法興矣德宗則不能
推誠待物尊賢使能故兩河用兵月費百
===
萬府庫之積不支數月而稅間架除陌錢
括商錢之法起矣即是而觀則其盈虛消
息之間夫豈專在於下哉我
太祖有天下取民之制一倣于古田賦之外惟
有商稅凡漢唐苛刻之政一切罷去
神謀遠慮所以惠澤斯民培養元氣者至矣既
而永樂間歲之所入不足所出故一時拳
宜俯從臣下之請乃有戶口食鹽有坑冶
採鑄有鈔關設置有竹木榷取初猶暫行
punctuated:
奢省費，輕徭薄賦，選用廉吏，使民衣食有餘，自不為盜。是其恭儉之政，在唐之諸君，亦未有與之並也。夫用節則費省，費省則國富，雖寬恤之詔屢下，征榷之令不行，亦何害其國用之有餘乎？至於武帝、德宗，承數世之積累，固宜國用有餘也。然武帝則外事四夷，内興工役，故常賦不足，而榷酒酤、筭舟車、造緡錢之法興矣。德宗則不能推誠待物，尊賢使能，故兩河用兵，月費百萬，府庫之積不支數月，而稅間架、除陌錢、括商錢之法起矣。即是而觀，則其盈虛消息之間，夫豈專在於下哉？
我太祖有天下，取民之制一倣于古，田賦之外，惟有商稅。凡漢唐苛刻之政，一切罷去。神謀遠慮，所以惠澤斯民、培養元氣者至矣。既而永樂間，歲之所入不足所出，故一時拳宜，俯從臣下之請，乃有戶口食鹽，有坑冶採鑄，有鈔關設置，有竹木榷取，初猶暫行。
translation_en:
…extravagance and reduced expenditure, lightened labor services and taxes, and appointed incorrupt officials, so that the people had clothing and food to spare and naturally refrained from banditry. His administration, marked by reverence and frugality, likewise had no equal among the Tang rulers. When spending is restrained, expenses decrease; when expenses decrease, the state grows wealthy. Even if edicts granting relief were repeatedly issued and orders imposing levies and monopolies were not enforced, how could this prevent the state from having ample funds? As for Emperor Wu of the Han and Emperor Dezong of the Tang, they inherited the accumulated resources of several generations and should certainly have had ample funds. Yet Emperor Wu campaigned against the peoples of the four quarters abroad and undertook construction projects at home. Ordinary tax revenues therefore proved insufficient, and measures establishing a liquor monopoly, taxing boats and carriages, and minting strings of cash [?] arose. Dezong could not deal with others sincerely, honor the worthy, or employ the capable. Consequently, military operations in the Two He regions cost a million each month; the accumulated treasury reserves could not sustain even a few months. Thus arose the tax assessed on the bays and frames of houses, the cash transaction levy, and the exaction of merchants’ money. Viewed in this light, can the fullness or depletion, decline or growth of state resources really depend solely on those below?
When our Emperor Taizu gained possession of All under Heaven, his system of levying contributions from the people followed antiquity throughout. Apart from the land tax, there were only commercial taxes. All the oppressive policies of the Han and Tang were abolished. His sagacious planning and far-reaching foresight were unsurpassed in bestowing benefits upon the people and nurturing their fundamental vitality. Subsequently, during the Yongle reign, annual receipts fell short of expenditure. As a temporary expedient [?], the emperor graciously acceded to his ministers’ requests. There followed household salt assessments, mining and the casting of metal, the establishment of paper-money customs stations, and monopoly levies on bamboo and timber. Initially, these were still implemented only temporarily…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今著為令蓋立法之初雖未為不善而今
之奉行者恐未肯悉體
朝廷本意也則
今日之理財者可不思所以寬恤之哉蓋地
力之生物有大數人力之成物有大限取
之有度用之有節則常足取之無度用之
無節則常不足此所以必欲節用以止財
之流不可橫斂以傷財之源也宋之名賢
若蘇轍有曰所謂豐財者非求財而益之
===
也去事之所以害財者而已矣事之害財
者三曰冗吏曰冗兵曰冗費三冗既去天
下之財得以日生而無害是亦豈非節用
之意哉蓋斜封墨敕額外羨增所謂冗吏
也列屯坐食老弱不練所謂冗兵也橫恩
濫賜之溢出脩飾營造之泛興禱祀游玩
之紛舉所謂冗費也三者之中冗費為甚
誠能節用則不耗財於無益之事不費財
於無用之地不施財於無功之人而國用
punctuated: 今著為令。蓋立法之初，雖未為不善，而今之奉行者，恐未肯悉體朝廷本意也。則今日之理財者，可不思所以寬恤之哉？蓋地力之生物有大數，人力之成物有大限，取之有度，用之有節，則常足；取之無度，用之無節，則常不足。此所以必欲節用以止財之流，不可橫斂以傷財之源也。宋之名賢若蘇轍有曰：「所謂豐財者，非求財而益之也，去事之所以害財者而已矣。事之害財者三：曰冗吏，曰冗兵，曰冗費。三冗既去，天下之財得以日生而無害。」是亦豈非節用之意哉？蓋斜封墨敕、額外羨增，所謂冗吏也；列屯坐食、老弱不練，所謂冗兵也；橫恩濫賜之溢出、脩飾營造之泛興、禱祀游玩之紛舉，所謂冗費也。三者之中，冗費為甚。誠能節用，則不耗財於無益之事，不費財於無用之地，不施財於無功之人，而國用
translation_en:
…now they have been established as standing regulations. When these laws were first instituted, they were not necessarily ill conceived; yet those who administer them today may be unwilling fully to embody the court’s original intentions. How, then, can those managing finances today fail to consider ways to ease the people’s burdens? The earth’s capacity to produce goods has an overall measure, and human capacity to make goods has an overall limit. If revenue is collected within bounds and expenditure is restrained, there will always be enough; if collection knows no bounds and expenditure no restraint, there will never be enough. This is why expenditure must be restrained to stem the outflow of wealth, and why arbitrary exactions must not be allowed to damage its source. A celebrated worthy of the Song, Su Zhe, said: “What is called making wealth abundant does not mean seeking wealth and adding to it. It means only eliminating those things that harm wealth. There are three things that harm wealth: superfluous officials, superfluous troops, and superfluous expenditure. Once these three excesses are eliminated, the wealth of the realm can grow daily without injury.” Is this not also the meaning of restraining expenditure?

Appointments through irregular ‘slant-sealed’ documents and ‘ink-written decrees,’ and additions beyond the authorized quotas: these constitute superfluous officials. Troops stationed in garrisons who merely consume provisions, and old and weak soldiers left untrained: these constitute superfluous troops. The unchecked outpouring of unwarranted favors and indiscriminate rewards, the excessive undertaking of embellishment and construction, and the proliferation of prayers, sacrifices, excursions, and amusements: these constitute superfluous expenditure. Of these three, superfluous expenditure is the gravest. If expenditure can truly be restrained, wealth will not be squandered on unprofitable undertakings, spent where it serves no purpose, or bestowed upon people who have rendered no meritorious service; and the resources for the state’s needs…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之充自足以却虜禦戎矣尚何有於充國孔
明之患哉若舍此而別求富國足用之術則
不過桑弘羊蠹國壞民之爲固非有神運
天雨之法也愚也繩樞草舍之人井蛙甕
雞之見固不知所謂理財亦不知所謂國
計所知者紙上陳言易與大學而已不曰
節以制度不傷財不害民乎又不曰生財
有大道乎是故始終爲執事陳之惟執事
矜其愚恕其狂斐進而教之幸也
===
第五問
譚才養
同考試官教諭方批不意書生中有習知
兵事如吾子者尚囊括底蘊以俟他日鎖鑰
北門
同考試官學正陳批條荅無遺末後歸重得
人亦確論也經生如此其文事武備者耶
考試官教諭姜批善荅足見學識
考試官教諭張批事實不遺且有斷制
punctuated:
之充，自足以却虜禦戎矣，尚何有於充國、孔明之患哉？若舍此而別求富國足用之術，則不過桑弘羊蠹國壞民之爲，固非有神運天雨之法也。愚也，繩樞草舍之人，井蛙甕雞之見，固不知所謂理財，亦不知所謂國計。所知者，紙上陳言，《易》與《大學》而已。不曰「節以制度，不傷財，不害民」乎？又不曰「生財有大道」乎？是故始終爲執事陳之。惟執事矜其愚，恕其狂斐，進而教之，幸也。

第五問
譚才養

同考試官教諭方批：「不意書生中有習知兵事如吾子者，尚囊括底蘊，以俟他日鎖鑰北門。」
同考試官學正陳批：「條荅無遺，末後歸重得人，亦確論也。經生如此，其文事武備者耶？」
考試官教諭姜批：「善荅，足見學識。」
考試官教諭張批：「事實不遺，且有斷制。」
translation_en:
…the resulting abundance of state resources would itself suffice to repel the invaders and resist hostile peoples. What cause would remain for the anxieties of Chongguo and Kongming? If one abandons this and seeks some other means of enriching the state and ensuring sufficient resources, it will amount to nothing more than Sang Hongyang’s practices of consuming the state’s wealth and harming its people. There is certainly no method by which spirits transport wealth or Heaven rains it down.

I am an ignorant man dwelling in a thatched hut with rope-hinged doors, my understanding as confined as that of a frog in a well or a chicken in a jar. I know nothing of what is called managing wealth, nor of what is called state finance. All I know are old sayings on paper: the Book of Changes and the Great Learning, nothing more. Does the former not say, “Regulate expenditure through institutions and measures, without injuring wealth or harming the people”? And does the latter not say, “There is a great way to produce wealth”? Thus I have set these principles before you throughout. If you would take pity on my ignorance, forgive my rash and ill-considered words, and admit me to your instruction, I would count myself fortunate.

Fifth Question
Tan Caiyang

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “I had not expected to find among scholars someone as thoroughly acquainted with military affairs as you. May you fully master their underlying intricacies, in preparation for the day when you serve as the lock and key of the northern gateway.”

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The response addresses each item without omission. Its final emphasis on securing the right men is also a sound judgment. Is a classical scholar of this kind not one who combines civil accomplishments with military preparedness?”

Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “A good answer, amply demonstrating learning and discernment.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It omits none of the relevant facts and also displays decisive judgment.”

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知安危之相為倚伏則
國家於兵法當振舉於平時知文武之相為
倚用則學者於兵法當備陳於
今日盖久安而危不防則危必作隆文而武
弗繼則武必衰皆非保邦長治之良圖文
武並行不悖之全策也此其所以未事之
先當求夫將為有能之將兵為有制之兵
而臨事之日庶幾將得士心兵識將意近
足以保安天下遠足以流芳後世若漢之
===
諸葛宋之名將乃可以語此而我
國朝選將材定武舉則又安不忘危文不廢
武超百王而獨邁者政不必以兵為諱也
執事發策首逮於此其亦慮關廟廊而憂
先天下者乎愚請復其萬一兵果可言耶
古人有曰先王耀德不觀兵吾不得而知
也兵果不可言耶古人又曰兵者生民之
大本吾亦不得而知也要之治世雖未嘗
好戰也亦未嘗忘戰也既未嘗好兵也亦
punctuated: 知安危之相為倚伏，則國家於兵法當振舉於平時；知文武之相為倚用，則學者於兵法當備陳於今日。盖久安而危不防，則危必作；隆文而武弗繼，則武必衰。皆非保邦長治之良圖、文武並行不悖之全策也。此其所以未事之先，當求夫將為有能之將，兵為有制之兵，而臨事之日，庶幾將得士心，兵識將意，近足以保安天下，遠足以流芳後世。若漢之諸葛、宋之名將，乃可以語此。而我國朝選將材、定武舉，則又安不忘危、文不廢武，超百王而獨邁者，政不必以兵為諱也。執事發策，首逮於此，其亦慮關廟廊而憂先天下者乎？愚請復其萬一。兵果可言耶？古人有曰：「先王耀德不觀兵。」吾不得而知也。兵果不可言耶？古人又曰：「兵者，生民之大本。」吾亦不得而知也。要之，治世雖未嘗好戰也，亦未嘗忘戰也；既未嘗好兵也，亦
translation_en: Knowing that security and danger depend upon and lie latent within one another, the state should attend vigorously to military methods in times of peace; knowing that civil and military affairs depend upon one another in their application, scholars should set forth military methods fully today. For if, after prolonged peace, no precautions are taken against danger, danger will surely arise; if civil affairs flourish but military preparedness does not keep pace, military strength will surely decline. Neither is a sound plan for preserving the realm in lasting order, nor a comprehensive policy through which civil and military affairs proceed together without conflict. Thus, before trouble arises, we must seek capable commanders and properly organized troops, so that when action is required, commanders may have their soldiers’ allegiance and soldiers may understand their commanders’ intentions. In the immediate term, this will suffice to secure peace throughout the realm; in the longer term, it will leave an honored name to posterity. Of men such as Zhuge Liang of the Han and the famous generals of the Song, these things may indeed be said. Our own dynasty, by selecting men of military talent and establishing the military examinations, remembers danger amid security and does not neglect military affairs while cultivating civil affairs. In this it surpasses the hundred kings, standing unrivaled: there is certainly no need to treat military affairs as a forbidden subject. You, honored examiners, have placed this matter first in your policy questions. Surely your thoughts concern the affairs of the imperial court, and you take on the cares of the realm before all others? I beg leave, in my ignorance, to offer an answer covering some small part of the matter. May military affairs indeed be discussed? An ancient said, “The former kings displayed their virtue, not their armies.” I cannot tell. May military affairs then not be discussed? Another ancient said, “Military affairs are a great foundation of the people’s livelihood.” Here too I cannot tell. In essence, although an age of good government has never delighted in war, neither has it ever forgotten war; while it has never delighted in arms, neither …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未嘗去兵也然而兵屬於將將統乎兵而
君又擇乎將君不擇將是以國予敵也將
不練兵是以主予敵也甚矣兵將之間容
可忽耶兵將之論容可已耶虞舜惟其明
是也故當四方風動之時而在內則明射
侯以為教養之術在外則奮武衛以為備
禦之防汲汲然惟恐兵之未練固不聞以
兵為諱也武王惟其明是也故當四海永
清之時而於春夏則有振旅茇舍之名於
===
秋冬則有治兵大閱之法汲汲然惟恐兵
之未練亦不聞以兵為諱也我
孝宗敬皇帝惟心舜武之心也故開求將之科
而創試材之式我
皇上惟心
先帝之心也故求將材於天下而定武舉於
京師統兵衛國計出萬全乂安長治其盛矣
哉蓋嘗聞之武侯矣所謂將材有八如道
德齊禮仁將也而又義禮智信無一而不
punctuated: 未嘗去兵也。然而兵屬於將，將統乎兵，而君又擇乎將。君不擇將，是以國予敵也；將不練兵，是以主予敵也。甚矣！兵將之間，容可忽耶？兵將之論，容可已耶？虞舜惟其明是也，故當四方風動之時，而在內則明射侯，以為教養之術；在外則奮武衛，以為備禦之防。汲汲然惟恐兵之未練，固不聞以兵為諱也。武王惟其明是也，故當四海永清之時，而於春夏則有振旅、茇舍之名，於秋冬則有治兵、大閱之法。汲汲然惟恐兵之未練，亦不聞以兵為諱也。我孝宗敬皇帝惟心舜武之心也，故開求將之科，而創試材之式。我皇上惟心先帝之心也，故求將材於天下，而定武舉於京師。統兵衛國，計出萬全；乂安長治，其盛矣哉！蓋嘗聞之武侯矣，所謂將材有八，如道德齊禮，仁將也，而又義禮智信，無一而不
translation_en:
…nor have they ever dispensed with arms. Yet troops are entrusted to generals, generals command troops, and the ruler, in turn, selects the generals. If the ruler fails to select his generals properly, he hands his state over to the enemy; if a general fails to train his troops, he hands his sovereign over to the enemy. How grave this is! Can the relationship between troops and generals possibly be neglected? Can discussion of troops and generals possibly cease?
Shun of Yu understood this clearly. Thus, even when his transforming influence stirred the four quarters like the wind, at home he elucidated the practice of target archery as a means of instruction and cultivation; abroad he made a vigorous display of armed guards as a defensive precaution. His urgent concern was only that the troops might remain untrained; certainly we have never heard that he treated military affairs as taboo. King Wu understood this clearly. Thus, even when all within the four seas enjoyed lasting peace, in spring and summer there were exercises called “ordering the troops” and “encamping in the open,” and in autumn and winter there were procedures for “marshalling the troops” and the “grand review.” His urgent concern was only that the troops might remain untrained; again, we have never heard that he treated military affairs as taboo.
Our Emperor Xiaozong Jing took the intentions of Shun and King Wu as his own. He therefore instituted an examination for recruiting generals and established a procedure for testing military talent. Our reigning emperor takes the intentions of the late emperor as his own. He therefore seeks men with the talents of generals throughout the realm and has established the military examinations at the capital. In commanding troops and defending the state, his plans provide for every contingency. What flourishing achievement—lasting order and enduring peace!
I have heard from the Marquis of Wu that there are eight kinds of talent in generals. For example, one who guides through virtue and brings order through ritual is a benevolent general. Moreover, of righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness, there is not one that he does not…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
全好賢從諫大將也而短兵長射無往而
不利者是已若夫貪求妬賢好佞荒淫之
類兹非八弊歟所謂將德有五如廉節孝
悌可以勵俗而揚名信義力行可以交友
而立功者是已若夫謀不能料是非亂不
能正刑法之類兹非八惡歟所謂將善有
五知敵之形勢與夫進退虛實之道知天
時人事與夫山川夷險之勢者是已若夫
議欲共而謀欲密衆欲靜而心欲一兹
===
非四欲歟夫具是材全是德備是善充是
欲而其曰惡曰弊無一毫存焉其為將也
非天下之全將而何哉自夫兵言之所謂
兵強有四君政脩也臣陳力也民服教也
兵從令也是已而其兵義者王兵應者勝
兵忿者亡兵貪者死兵驕者敗兹非五戒
歟所謂武德有七制亂也耀德也時動也
守成脩備也勤政興利也是已而其曰輕
曰慢曰盜曰欺與背曰亂與誤兹非七禁
punctuated:
全。好賢從諫，大將也，而短兵長射，無往而不利者是已。若夫貪求、妬賢、好佞、荒淫之類，兹非八弊歟？所謂將德有五，如廉節孝悌，可以勵俗而揚名；信義力行，可以交友而立功者是已。若夫謀不能料是非，亂不能正刑法之類，兹非八惡歟？所謂將善有五，知敵之形勢，與夫進退虛實之道；知天時人事，與夫山川夷險之勢者是已。若夫議欲共而謀欲密，衆欲靜而心欲一，兹非四欲歟？夫具是材，全是德，備是善，充是欲，而其曰惡曰弊，無一毫存焉，其為將也，非天下之全將而何哉？
自夫兵言之，所謂兵強有四：君政脩也，臣陳力也，民服教也，兵從令也是已。而其兵義者王，兵應者勝，兵忿者亡，兵貪者死，兵驕者敗，兹非五戒歟？所謂武德有七：制亂也，耀德也，時動也，守成脩備也，勤政興利也是已。而其曰輕、曰慢、曰盜、曰欺，與背、曰亂、與誤，兹非七禁
translation_en:
…complete in all of them. One who esteems the worthy and accepts remonstrance is a great general; he is effective wherever he goes, in close combat and long-range archery alike. As for such things as covetousness, jealousy of the worthy, fondness for flatterers, and debauchery—are these not among the eight defects? There are said to be five virtues of a general: integrity, moral constancy, filial piety, and fraternal respect can improve customs and win renown; trustworthiness, righteousness, and diligent practice can secure friends and establish achievements. As for such things as being unable to distinguish right from wrong when planning, or to enforce penal laws properly amid disorder—are these not among the eight evils?
