There are said to be five excellences of a general: knowing the enemy’s disposition and circumstances, together with the principles of advance and retreat, weakness and strength; and knowing seasonal conditions and human affairs, together with the configurations of mountains and rivers and the ease or difficulty of the terrain. As for wishing deliberations to be shared but plans to remain secret, the troops to be calm and their minds united—are these not the four desiderata? If a man possesses these talents, fully embodies these virtues, has all these excellences, and fulfills these desiderata, while retaining not the slightest trace of the evils and defects mentioned, what could he be but a consummate general under Heaven?
Speaking of military affairs, there are said to be four sources of military strength: the ruler puts his government in order; ministers exert their abilities; the people submit to instruction; and soldiers obey commands. Moreover, those who wage righteous war attain kingship; those who fight in response to aggression prevail; those who fight in anger perish; those who fight out of greed die; and those who fight arrogantly are defeated. Are these not the five admonitions? There are said to be seven martial virtues: suppressing disorder, displaying virtue, acting at the proper time, preserving achievements, making preparations, attending diligently to government, and promoting benefits. As for recklessness, arrogance, theft, deception, betrayal, disorder, and error [?]—are these not the seven prohibitions …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
歟所謂兵勢有三五星合度天勢也險易
殊形地勢也主聖將賢人勢也是已而其
事機作而不能應勢機動而不能圖情機
發而不能行者非三機歟夫以有是强兼
是德乗是勢而於所謂戒與機者無有一
事忽焉其為兵也非天下之全兵而何哉
若我廣右固幅員之荒服也交廣之界限
也犬羊之出没也金革之交鳴也山川之
險阻也我
===
祖宗亦以此為軫轄而嚴總帥於要衝執事亦
以此為鎖鑰而詢先代之名將夫所謂奮
揚威武而撃曹成之寇者非黃齊歟忠義
果敢而戢儂賊之兵者非梁仲保歟歐陽
脩薦其智畧可任將軍者張守約也狄青
薦其驍勇而破儂賊者黄逵也文武兼全
則有陳本道焉一代名將則有楊文廣焉
嗚呼才不易生將不易名戎不易制功不
易立而數君子卒能建不世之竒績垂不
punctuated:
歟？所謂兵勢有三：五星合度，天勢也；險易殊形，地勢也；主聖將賢，人勢也，是已。而其事機作而不能應，勢機動而不能圖，情機發而不能行者，非三機歟？夫以有是强，兼是德，乗是勢，而於所謂戒與機者，無有一事忽焉，其為兵也，非天下之全兵而何哉？
若我廣右，固幅員之荒服也，交廣之界限也，犬羊之出没也，金革之交鳴也，山川之險阻也。我祖宗亦以此為軫轄，而嚴總帥於要衝。執事亦以此為鎖鑰，而詢先代之名將。夫所謂奮揚威武而撃曹成之寇者，非黃齊歟？忠義果敢而戢儂賊之兵者，非梁仲保歟？歐陽脩薦其智畧可任將軍者，張守約也；狄青薦其驍勇而破儂賊者，黄逵也。文武兼全，則有陳本道焉；一代名將，則有楊文廣焉。嗚呼！才不易生，將不易名，戎不易制，功不易立，而數君子卒能建不世之竒績，垂不
translation_en:
…are these not the seven prohibitions? There are said to be three strategic advantages in warfare: the five planets moving in their proper courses constitute the advantage of Heaven; the differing configurations of difficult and easy terrain constitute the advantage of Earth; and a sagely ruler and worthy generals constitute the human advantage. These are they. Yet when an opportunity arises in events and one cannot respond, when an opportunity emerges from shifting circumstances and one cannot devise a plan, or when an opportunity reveals itself in the state of affairs and one cannot act—are these not the three critical opportunities? With such strengths, joined to such virtues and making use of such advantages, if not a single one of these cautions and opportunities is neglected, how could such an army be anything other than an army complete in every respect under Heaven?
Our Guangyou is indeed a remote outer region of the realm, the boundary between Jiao and Guang, a place where “dogs and sheep” appear and disappear, where weapons and war drums sound together, and where mountains and rivers present formidable obstacles. Our imperial ancestors likewise regarded this region as a linchpin [?] and established firm supreme military command at its strategic points. You, honored examiners, likewise regard it as a strategic gateway and inquire about the celebrated generals of earlier times. Was it not Huang Qi who displayed martial might and struck the bandit forces of Cao Cheng? Was it not Liang Zhongbao who, loyal, righteous, resolute, and bold, subdued the forces of the Nong rebels? The man whom Ouyang Xiu recommended as possessing the intelligence and strategic ability to serve as a general was Zhang Shouyue. The man whom Di Qing recommended for his valor and who defeated the Nong rebels was Huang Kui. For someone fully accomplished in both civil and military affairs, there was Chen Bendao; for a celebrated general of his age, there was Yang Wenguang. Alas! Talent does not readily arise; a general does not readily win renown; warfare is not readily brought under control; achievements are not readily established. Yet these gentlemen ultimately accomplished extraordinary feats rarely seen in any age and handed down an enduring…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
世之偉名雖其將才將德將善之足稱者
固未純乎諸葛之所云也而皆千夫之特
萬人之雄矣其兵强武德兵勢之足法者
亦未必純乎諸葛之所云也而皆節制之
師勇鋭之卒矣執事有懷於前而又有望
於後乃曰側陋之中豈無非熊伏龍而深
知擇將用兵之畧者是亦問陶朱於三家
之市求忠信於十室之邑雖然兵民本一
塗文武非二道而前人固有以攻刺擊殺
===
之事非儒其衣冠者所可能也愚竊謂鳴
條之師誰爲之牧野之師誰爲之東山之
師又誰爲之則夫山鳴谷應之間固未必
無鷹揚虎嘯之士也然則將之爲將何以
擇之不拘於門望也不拘於地理也而得
一傑然於庸將之中者則知其爲才之小
得一傑然於才將之中者則知其爲才之
大而又窮之言辭以觀其變與之簡牒以
觀其誠明白顯問以觀其德使之以財以
punctuated: 世之偉名。雖其將才、將德、將善之足稱者，固未純乎諸葛之所云也，而皆千夫之特、萬人之雄矣。其兵强、武德、兵勢之足法者，亦未必純乎諸葛之所云也，而皆節制之師、勇鋭之卒矣。執事有懷於前，而又有望於後，乃曰：「側陋之中，豈無非熊、伏龍，而深知擇將用兵之畧者？」是亦問陶朱於三家之市，求忠信於十室之邑。雖然，兵民本一塗，文武非二道，而前人固有以攻刺擊殺之事，非儒其衣冠者所可能也。愚竊謂：鳴條之師，誰爲之？牧野之師，誰爲之？東山之師，又誰爲之？則夫山鳴谷應之間，固未必無鷹揚虎嘯之士也。然則將之爲將，何以擇之？不拘於門望也，不拘於地理也，而得一傑然於庸將之中者，則知其爲才之小；得一傑然於才將之中者，則知其爲才之大。而又窮之言辭，以觀其變；與之簡牒，以觀其誠；明白顯問，以觀其德；使之以財，以
translation_en:
…extraordinary renown for ages to come. Although their praiseworthy abilities, virtues, and accomplishments as commanders did not fully accord with what Zhuge Liang described, they were outstanding among thousands and heroes among multitudes. Likewise, although their exemplary military strength, martial virtue, and strategic dispositions did not necessarily accord fully with what Zhuge Liang described, their armies were disciplined and their soldiers courageous and keen.

You, honored examiners, cherish the achievements of the past and also place hopes in those to come. Thus you ask: “Among men of humble and obscure station, might there not be a ‘Non-Bear’ or a ‘Sleeping Dragon’—men like Jiang Ziya or Zhuge Liang—who deeply understand the strategies of selecting commanders and employing troops?” This is like seeking a Tao Zhu in a market of only three households, or seeking loyalty and trustworthiness in a settlement of only ten households.

Nevertheless, soldiers and civilians fundamentally follow one path; civil and military pursuits are not two separate ways. Yet some men of earlier times certainly regarded attacking, stabbing, striking, and killing as things beyond the ability of those who wear the robes and caps of Confucian scholars. I venture to ask: Who conducted the campaign at Mingtiao? Who conducted the campaign at Muye? And who conducted the campaign at Dongshan? Surely, amid the sounding mountains and answering valleys, there may well be men who soar like eagles and roar like tigers.

How, then, should one select a commander fit to command? One must not be bound by family prestige or geographical origin. If a man stands out among ordinary commanders, one knows his talent to be of the lesser order; if he stands out among talented commanders, one knows his talent to be of the greater order. Furthermore, press him to the limits in discussion to observe his adaptability; give him written documents to observe his sincerity; question him plainly and openly to observe his virtue; entrust him with wealth in order to…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
觀其廉試之以色以觀其貞凡於諸葛之
所尚者尚之所懲者懲之如此而曰將不
得人未之聞也借曰專制閫外皆膏粱之
流運籌帷幄者非韜畧之輩真兒戲耳何
有於擇將兵之為兵又何以用之必先明
之物采辨之等列以昭其尊卑貴賤順之
少長習之威儀以申其孝弟忠信而又於
未戰則養其財將戰則養其力既戰□□
其氣既勝則養其心凡於諸葛之所用者
===
用之所革者革之如此而曰兵不得人未
之聞也借曰散於州縣者籍為營壘之符
游於田畝者律以卒伍之令亦虛文耳抑
何有於用兵愚於此又有說焉論兵非難
論將為難得良將非難得良相為難未有
將得人而兵非其兵者也亦未有相得人
而將非其將者也故韓信之拜將由於蕭
何趙充國之進計本於魏相將顧不係於
相耶有方叔則不患師干之不試有吉甫
punctuated: 觀其廉，試之以色以觀其貞。凡於諸葛之所尚者尚之，所懲者懲之。如此而曰將不得人，未之聞也。借曰專制閫外皆膏粱之流，運籌帷幄者非韜畧之輩，真兒戲耳，何有於擇將？兵之為兵，又何以用之？必先明之物采，辨之等列，以昭其尊卑貴賤；順之少長，習之威儀，以申其孝弟忠信。而又於未戰則養其財，將戰則養其力，既戰□□其氣，既勝則養其心。凡於諸葛之所用者用之，所革者革之。如此而曰兵不得人，未之聞也。借曰散於州縣者籍為營壘之符，游於田畝者律以卒伍之令，亦虛文耳，抑何有於用兵？愚於此又有說焉：論兵非難，論將為難；得良將非難，得良相為難。未有將得人而兵非其兵者也，亦未有相得人而將非其將者也。故韓信之拜將由於蕭何，趙充國之進計本於魏相，將顧不係於相耶？有方叔則不患師干之不試，有吉甫
translation_en:
…to observe his integrity; test him with sexual temptation to observe his constancy. Honor whatever Zhuge Liang honored, and condemn whatever he condemned. With such measures, I have never heard of a failure to find suitable men as generals. Suppose, however, that those exercising independent command beyond the palace gates are all sons of privilege, while those devising plans within the command tent lack strategic ability: this is truly child’s play. What does it have to do with selecting generals?

As for soldiers, how should they be employed? First make their insignia clear and distinguish their ranks, so as to display differences of precedence and status. Order them by seniority and train them in proper bearing, thereby reinforcing their filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness. Before battle, nurture their material resources; as battle approaches, nurture their strength; once battle has begun, [two illegible characters] their fighting spirit [?]; after victory, nurture their hearts. Employ whatever Zhuge Liang employed, and abolish whatever he abolished. With such measures, I have never heard of a failure to obtain suitable soldiers. Suppose, however, that men scattered throughout the prefectures and counties are merely entered on registers as tokens of military encampments [?], and men working in the fields are subjected to regulations for military units: this too is empty formality. What does it have to do with employing troops?

I venture to offer a further observation here: assessing soldiers is not difficult; assessing generals is difficult. Obtaining good generals is not difficult; obtaining good chief councilors is difficult. Never have suitable generals been appointed while their soldiers proved unfit for service; nor have suitable chief councilors been appointed while their generals proved unfit for command. Thus Han Xin’s appointment as general was due to Xiao He, and Zhao Chongguo’s presentation of his strategy owed its origin to Wei Xiang. Do generals not, then, depend upon chief councilors? With Fang Shu, there is no need to fear that the army’s shields will not be put to use; with Ji Fu…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
則不患武事之不嚴兵顧不係於將耶是
故閱兵在將任將在相而論相又在我
皇上總乾斷廣離明以爲將將之權衡也
punctuated: 則不患武事之不嚴。兵顧不係於將耶？是故閱兵在將，任將在相，而論相又在我皇上總乾斷、廣離明，以爲將將之權衡也。
translation_en: …then there is no need to fear that military affairs will lack discipline. Do the troops not, then, depend upon their generals? Thus, reviewing the troops rests with the generals, and appointing generals rests with the chief minister. Assessing the chief minister, in turn, rests with our Emperor, who must exercise the decisive authority of Qian (Heaven) and extend the illuminating discernment of Li (Fire), making these the standard by which he commands his commanders.

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
正德癸酉瀛應聘預廣右校
試由岳陽浮洞庭觀衡岳迤
邐入安道寔桂嶺第一程也
立馬四望萬山在目而草木
叢密遼廓眇忽竊喜踪跡未
半天下倏得竒觀夙願亦足
===
少償不兩舍許抵清湘則風
景更熾而長松古栢夾道綿
三百里餘其霜皮溜雨黛色
參天有偃盖蛟龍形者有躚
徙鶴翅廻者又有錯落龍鱗
出者且風韻颼颺若奏笙簧
掩竽籟而勝益竒至桂林則
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

正德癸酉，瀛應聘預廣右校試，由岳陽浮洞庭，觀衡岳，迤邐入安，道寔桂嶺第一程也。立馬四望，萬山在目，而草木叢密，遼廓眇忽。竊喜踪跡未半天下，倏得竒觀，夙願亦足少償。

不兩舍許，抵清湘，則風景更熾，而長松古栢夾道綿三百里餘。其霜皮溜雨，黛色參天，有偃盖蛟龍形者，有躚徙鶴翅廻者，又有錯落龍鱗出者。且風韻颼颺，若奏笙簧，掩竽籟，而勝益竒。至桂林，則
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the guiyou year of the Zhengde reign [1513], I, Ying, accepted an invitation to participate in examining candidates in Guangyou [Guangxi]. From Yueyang I sailed across Lake Dongting, viewed Mount Heng, and made my winding way into An [?]. This route was indeed the first stage toward the Guiling mountains. Reining in my horse, I gazed in all directions: myriad mountains lay before my eyes, thickly covered in vegetation, stretching into a vast and indistinct distance. I was privately delighted that, although my travels had not yet covered half the realm, I had suddenly encountered such extraordinary sights. My long-held wish could thus find some fulfillment.

Within roughly two travel stages, I reached Qingxiang, where the scenery grew still more luxuriant. Tall pines and ancient cypresses lined the road for over three hundred li. Rain streamed down their frost-weathered bark, and their dark green crowns towered into the sky. Some spread like canopies or took the shapes of dragons; some seemed to sway like wheeling cranes’ wings [?]; others displayed overlapping forms like dragons’ scales. Moreover, the wind’s music rustled and soared through them, as though sheng mouth organs were playing, drowning out the sounds of yu mouth organs and pipes, making the scenery still more wondrous. Upon reaching Guilin, …

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
山峭拔如畫水清而駛松栢
益茂蓋山川之秀產乎異材
者如此於戲地靈人杰固也
鍾於物者且然人生其間豈
無光明俊偉之習卓犖魁竒
之才文章德行之士可以名
世者乎及得士之文讀之不
豐贍而平淡則清勁而飄逸
雖所造有淺深醇疵不同然
養之正詞之順氣之充槩有
足觀者柳子厚嘗恠陽德之
炳耀獨發於紛葩瓌麗而罕
鍾乎人是方恐兼有之也雖
然松栢之可愛者豈直瀛前
punctuated: 山峭拔如畫，水清而駛，松栢益茂。蓋山川之秀，產乎異材者如此。於戲！地靈人杰，固也。鍾於物者且然，人生其間，豈無光明俊偉之習、卓犖魁竒之才、文章德行之士，可以名世者乎？及得士之文讀之，不豐贍而平淡，則清勁而飄逸。雖所造有淺深醇疵不同，然養之正、詞之順、氣之充，槩有足觀者。柳子厚嘗恠陽德之炳耀，獨發於紛葩瓌麗，而罕鍾乎人，是方恐兼有之也。雖然，松栢之可愛者，豈直瀛前
translation_en:
…the mountains rise steeply, as in a painting; the waters are clear and swift; and the pines and cypresses grow still more luxuriantly. Such is the way the finest essences of mountains and rivers produce extraordinary timber. Ah! That a land endowed with spiritual potency produces outstanding people is surely true. If these essences manifest themselves so abundantly even in material things, could there fail to be, among those born here, people of bright and noble disposition, exceptional and remarkable talent, and literary accomplishment and moral conduct, who might win renown in their age?

When I obtained the candidates’ writings and read them, they were either ample in substance yet plain in expression, or limpid and vigorous yet flowing with ease. Although their attainments differed in depth and in purity or imperfection, their sound cultivation, fluent diction, and fullness of vital force generally offered much to admire. Liu Zihou once wondered why the brilliance of yang’s potency manifested itself only in profuse blossoms and magnificent beauty, but rarely gathered in human beings. This region, I venture to think, possesses both.

Even so, could what makes pines and cypresses worthy of affection be merely what Ying previously [described][?]…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所狀者哉有心也記禮者稱
之後凋也孔子取之必有以
也今夫貞心勁質禦攘氷霜
剛也四時一貫榮悴不易常
也畝毒以蔽行道無苦仁也
蔦與女蘿上有兎絲義也雖
春陽氣王不與羣木鬭榮謙
===
也凡此數德可比君子及乎
將用大可以柱明堂棟大廈
次之為榱為桷非若樗櫟之
竟老山林耳矣然則諸士子
歷階而升其亦松栢之有資
於世用者乎而其自處所宜
比德松栢殷勤封殖為他日
punctuated: 所狀者哉？有心也，記禮者稱之；後凋也，孔子取之，必有以也。今夫貞心勁質，禦攘氷霜，剛也；四時一貫，榮悴不易，常也；畝毒以蔽行道無苦，仁也；蔦與女蘿，上有兎絲，義也；雖春陽氣王，不與羣木鬭榮，謙也。凡此數德，可比君子。及乎將用，大可以柱明堂、棟大廈，次之為榱為桷，非若樗櫟之竟老山林耳矣。然則諸士子歷階而升，其亦松栢之有資於世用者乎？而其自處，所宜比德松栢，殷勤封殖，為他日
translation_en:
…what has been described? For possessing a heart, they are praised by the compiler of the Record of Rites; for withering last, they are commended by Confucius. There must be reasons for this. Their steadfast hearts and sturdy substance withstand ice and frost: this is fortitude. Remaining consistent through the four seasons, unchanged by flourishing or decline: this is constancy. Spreading shelter [?], they protect travelers along the road from hardship: this is benevolence. Mistletoe and climbing lichens, with dodder growing upon them: this is righteousness. Though the vital force of spring is abundant, they do not compete with other trees in luxuriance: this is humility. In all these virtues, they may be compared to gentlemen.

When put to use, the largest can serve as pillars for the Hall of Light or ridgepoles for great halls; those of the next size can become rafters and roof timbers. They are unlike the ailanthus and the oak, which merely grow old in the mountain forests. Thus, as these scholars ascend the steps of advancement, are they not also like pines and cypresses that contribute to the needs of the world? In conducting themselves, they ought to emulate the virtues of pines and cypresses, diligently tending and nurturing themselves, to become in days to come…

title: 正德八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廊廟器則於地之靈可謂無
負矣不然是亦凡草木而已
奚取焉事竣謹書此列于左
湖廣衡州府耒陽縣儒學教
諭姜瀛謹序
punctuated:
廊廟器，則於地之靈可謂無負矣。不然，是亦凡草木而已，奚取焉？事竣，謹書此，列于左。
湖廣衡州府耒陽縣儒學教諭姜瀛謹序。
translation_en:
…men fit for service at the imperial court, then they may be said not to have failed the numinous spirit of this land. Otherwise, they are merely ordinary plants and trees: what would commend them? With the proceedings concluded, I have respectfully written these words and placed them to the left.
Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Ying, Instructor of the Confucian School of Leiyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang.
